records.title: 0.0% is still Stella Artois
records.description:
The workday comes to an end. You decide to crack open an ice-cold Stella Artois as a reward for all your hard work. You deserve it… go for it. But just as that incredible golden liquid touches your lips, you hear your boss about to walk in. Your survival instinct kicks in, and you hide the beer behind you, even though there’s nothing to hide, because it’s a Stella Artois 0.0%.
That’s how Stella Artois launches its new campaign, “0.0% is still Stella Artois,” for Stella Artois 0.0%, created by GUT Buenos Aires. Through a series of graphic and audiovisual pieces, the brand taps into those awkward moments that can arise around a non-alcoholic beer—as if it did contain alcohol. Micro-scenes told with Stella Artois’ signature humor, all landing on a clear message: “if it feels like beer, it’s because it is.”
“In a work or academic setting, even without alcohol, if it’s a Stella Artois, the instinct kicks in. And when that happens, an automatic reflex appears: to hide it. Because Stella Artois 0.0% isn’t lacking alcohol. it’s overflowing with attitude,” added  Christian Rosli, CCO of GUT Buenos Aires.
“With Stella Artois 0.0%, we wanted to stop talking about what it doesn’t have and focus on everything it does. If your first instinct is to hide it, then the experience is already there,” said Agustina Vadori, Brand Manager for Stella Artois.

records.title: 150th Anniversary
records.description: Budweiser marks a milestone summer, celebrating its 150th anniversary alongside United States’ 250th birthday with a nationwide campaign rooted in shared moments. Bringing its legacy to life across the country, the brand shows up where people gather, reflecting its long-standing role in American celebrations. Honouring traditions that unite communities, the campaign reinforces Budweiser’s enduring connection to the nation as it joins in the lead-up to this historic milestone.

records.title: 30 Years of Success
records.country: Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and United Arab Emirates
records.description:
“30 Years of Success” is a documentary-led integrated advertising campaign created by Jenica Marketing Agency to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Alex Apparels, one of Egypt’s established apparel manufacturing companies with a growing international presence and long-standing relationships with global fashion brands and partners.

Rather than treating the anniversary as a celebration of time alone, the campaign focused on the journey behind three decades of success — the people, partnerships, milestones, foundations, awards, and achievements that have shaped Alex Apparels into the company it is today.

At the heart of the campaign was an anniversary documentary that brought this 30-year journey to life, reflecting on defining moments in the company’s history and recognizing the people and partners who contributed to its growth.

The campaign began with a pre-launch phase that introduced the story and legacy of Alex Apparels through its achievements, milestones, industry experience, and long-standing partnerships, gradually building momentum toward the 30th-anniversary celebration.

More than commemorating the past, “30 Years of Success” reinforces Alex Apparels’ position as an Egyptian apparel manufacturer with a global outlook, while positioning its three-decade legacy as the foundation for the company’s next chapter.

records.title: $5 McValue Meal
records.description: McDonald’s Canada and Cossette have launched a national, music-driven campaign that turns the $5 McValue Meal and all-day menu into an emotional brand experience. Built on McDonald’s one-year price promise, the work uses fast-paced storytelling, iconic characters, and the nostalgic energy of Britney Spears’ Gimme More to make value feel exciting, cultural, and anything but transactional.

records.title: A better idea
records.description: Financial advertising has a habit of making simple things sound complicated. Turbo's latest campaign for ARQ flips that convention on its head. Starring Bruna Marquezine and Diego Boneta, the films begin with the actors rejecting the script before taking over the production themselves. As the visuals become increasingly cinematic, the message becomes increasingly clear, proving that talking about money doesn't have to be confusing.

records.description:
It just takes one fake pill to kill. And because the fentanyl in counterfeit pills is unevenly distributed, there's no sure way to know whether that pill in your hand is going to be your last.
To raise awareness about this lethal "chocolate chip cookie effect," the effort brings a pill to life to save lives - and open up conversation between adults and kids around a devastating reality.

records.description: A new brewery with restaurant opened in Bratislava, Slovakia. Because the establishment is located on the promenade of a popular shopping mall with many fashion brands, the brewery's initial campaign borrowed the language of fashion, which it linked to gastronomy.

records.title: A delicacy for true food lovers
records.campaign_title: A delicacy for true food lovers
records.description:
Tohfe, constantly looks for ways to bring you a fresh and exciting seafood experience. In its latest campaign, we're taking a step beyond the familiar canned seafood and introducing Tohfe, not just as a brand known for tuna, but as a name that represents a wide variety of premium canned seafood in Iran. We wanted to show that Tohfe is more than just a can of tuna; it's a complete range of flavorful seafood dishes, from seafood stews to other delightful meals that you can enjoy every day.
The concept behind our campaign, 'A delicacy for true food lovers,' highlights the idea that Tohfe isn't just about convenience,it’s about quality and taste. Every video spotlights a different variety, brought to life through a playful narrative featuring a mischievous seagull determined to steal the tuna. This seagull became the signature of the campaign. Its presence going beyond the screen with the seagull shadow also being cleverly integrated into Out-of-Home (OOH) placements to pique curiosity and provide a single visual story across channels. 
With this campaign, our goal is simple: to introduce Tohfe as a brand that goes beyond your expectations and brings a variety of delicious seafood options into your life. Tohfe isn’t just a product, it’s a companion on your journey through the world of seafood, taste, and great meals.

records.title: A Grain of Love
records.description:
The advertising campaign was based on the tagline: "A Grain of Love." The word "grain" here refers to seeds like coffee beans, with the idea that this grain brings love.

The concept was developed through different situations where two people face a conflict that escalates, but then Mehbaj grains appear, transforming the mood into love and happiness.

records.title: A Handful of Happiness
records.description:
St Luke’s has created a maverick gang of three rapping woodland creatures to lift the nation’s mood in KP Nuts’ first TV campaign for more than three years. The nutty trio are here to remind us of the feel-good factor that a handful of delicious KP Nuts can bring, unleashing a sense of joy every time a bag of KP Nuts’ new premium Signature range is opened. 

The new film opens on a shot of a couple, Billy and Tash, slumped on the sofa, idly watching a nature documentary or scrolling on the phone. But when Billy grabs a handful of KP Signature nuts, the evening takes on a whole different tone as the Woodland Clan jump into action and liven up the moment.

Suddenly, the lights dim, and we meet Squirrel-D (A.K.A P-Nut) , Striiipes the badger, and a hedgehog named Smiler the Hibernator, who pop up unexpectedly in front of Billy and Tash on the table. The trio instantly up the tempo of the evening with an energetic rap that brings to life the joy of KP Nuts, while highlighting all the benefits of eating and enjoying Signature’s delicious premium cashew snacks. 

The couple are irresistibly drawn into the rhythm as the Woodland Clan start their rap on the coffee table in front of them and are captivated as it builds to a crescendo. Squirrel-D, Striiipes and Smiler the Hibernator’s performance provides a moment of delight to the couple as they enjoy the trio’s rap, which begins with a line about the couple’s hard day and ends with a celebration of the way KP’s new Signature range has “levelled up” their snack game.  

St Luke’s spot ends with the couple visibly lifted and enjoying the evening so much more as they reflect, slightly puzzled, on the unexpected moment of delight they have just experienced. We finish on a pack shot of the newly-launched KP Nuts signature range, accompanied by the endline “New KP Signature – A Handful of Happiness.” 

Beth George, Senior Brand Manager at KP Snacks, said: “At KP, we believe in adding a little fun to the everyday with great-tasting snacks. We’re thrilled to see KP Nuts back on TV with an entertaining ad that reflects the way our new Signature range can instantly elevate a run-of-the-mill evening into a night that brings ‘A Handful of Happiness’ to the occasion.” 

Richard Denney, Joint Chief Creative Officer at St Luke’s, said: “We’ve all experienced those dull nights in front of the TV but now, thanks to KP Nuts’ new Signature brand, we can liven up the everyday with a snack that brings out the joy in all of us, whether we’re a badger, a squirrel, a hedgehog or a human.” 

KP Snacks’ Signature roasted jumbo cashew nuts come in two flavours, Sea Salt & Rosemary and Smoked Chilli & Red Pepper. TV ads, which launch from 17 October, will run across broadcast and VOD on Sky, Channel 4 and ITV across TV and VOD in 30 and 20-second versions, with media planning and buying by Starcom. 

St Luke’s won KP Snacks brands Tyrrells, Popchips, KP Nuts in March 2019 after a pitch against incumbent agencies Wieden & Kennedy London, And Rising and BMB respectively.

records.title: A Life in the Day of Marty
records.campaign_title: A Life in the Day of Marty
records.description:
Tricon Residential - one of North America’s largest owners and operators of rental homes and a Blackstone Real Estate portfolio company has introduced a significant brand refresh that repositions the company around its long-standing commitment to resident care.

The new identity was developed by FUNDAMENTALco, the value-creation consultancy spun out of Blackstone, and brought to life in partnership with creative agency American Haiku. While many rental brands focus on price points or amenities, FUNDAMENTALco identified a differentiator: Tricon’s hospitality-first culture, rooted in years of service training inspired by organizations like the Four Seasons.

That insight became the foundation for a full brand refresh across the U.S. and Canada - including updated visual identity, website, signage, uniforms, and every resident-facing touchpoint. From a warm orange color palette to family-focused photography - every element has been rebuilt to convey genuine welcome and care, replacing corporate polish with a richer, more residential feel.

To introduce the new identity, American Haiku created a campaign built around the everyday work of Tricon’s maintenance managers. “A Life in the Day of Marty” highlights the small, human moments that shape the resident experience - precision before a move-in, hanging a solar system in a child’s room, or simply offering empathy on a hard day. 

Four 30-second films anchor the campaign:

“Visible Numbers” shows Marty’s attention to detail ahead of move-in.

“Cut Corners” contrasts human imperfection with Marty’s refusal to take shortcuts.

“World Builder” turns a repair call into a moment of imagination for a child.

“Heavy Lifting” acknowledges that some moments call for humanity, not tools.

The campaign draws from stories shared directly by employees and adopts a slower, more deliberate pace to reflect the real rhythm of Tricon teams at work.

Here’s how leaders describe the work:
"Our people deliver out-caring service to residents every single day—it's what makes Tricon who we are. This brand refresh brings that culture and commitment to the forefront. We wanted our brand identity to better reflect the genuine care, the attention to detail, and the service our teams provide. It's not about a different look—it's about ensuring our brand reflects the people and mission at our core.” Gary Berman, President and CEO, Tricon
“Every Tricon employee we spoke to embodied this incredible commitment to caring for the residents. This sense of decency and ‘doing things right’ permeated every conversation we had with them,” said Thom Glover, Founder and CCO at American Haiku.
“We consider ourselves specialists in building worlds for brands. Having the opportunity to collaborate with FUNDAMENTALco, who are at the apex of their field in a slightly different discipline, helped deliver the best possible campaign for Tricon. We look forward to partnering with them again for future projects where strategic clarity and creative storytelling can come together to push the category forward,” added Glover. 

By grounding the refresh in Tricon’s operational reality - not just a new look - FUNDAMENTALco and American Haiku have helped the company articulate a clearer, more resonant identity at a time when expectations around renting continue to evolve.

records.title: A Life in the Day of Marty
records.campaign_title: A Life in the Day of Marty
records.description:
Tricon Residential - one of North America’s largest owners and operators of rental homes and a Blackstone Real Estate portfolio company has introduced a significant brand refresh that repositions the company around its long-standing commitment to resident care.

The new identity was developed by FUNDAMENTALco, the value-creation consultancy spun out of Blackstone, and brought to life in partnership with creative agency American Haiku. While many rental brands focus on price points or amenities, FUNDAMENTALco identified a differentiator: Tricon’s hospitality-first culture, rooted in years of service training inspired by organizations like the Four Seasons.

That insight became the foundation for a full brand refresh across the U.S. and Canada - including updated visual identity, website, signage, uniforms, and every resident-facing touchpoint. From a warm orange color palette to family-focused photography - every element has been rebuilt to convey genuine welcome and care, replacing corporate polish with a richer, more residential feel.

To introduce the new identity, American Haiku created a campaign built around the everyday work of Tricon’s maintenance managers. “A Life in the Day of Marty” highlights the small, human moments that shape the resident experience - precision before a move-in, hanging a solar system in a child’s room, or simply offering empathy on a hard day. 

Four 30-second films anchor the campaign:

“Visible Numbers” shows Marty’s attention to detail ahead of move-in.

“Cut Corners” contrasts human imperfection with Marty’s refusal to take shortcuts.

“World Builder” turns a repair call into a moment of imagination for a child.

“Heavy Lifting” acknowledges that some moments call for humanity, not tools.

The campaign draws from stories shared directly by employees and adopts a slower, more deliberate pace to reflect the real rhythm of Tricon teams at work.

Here’s how leaders describe the work:
"Our people deliver out-caring service to residents every single day—it's what makes Tricon who we are. This brand refresh brings that culture and commitment to the forefront. We wanted our brand identity to better reflect the genuine care, the attention to detail, and the service our teams provide. It's not about a different look—it's about ensuring our brand reflects the people and mission at our core.” Gary Berman, President and CEO, Tricon
“Every Tricon employee we spoke to embodied this incredible commitment to caring for the residents. This sense of decency and ‘doing things right’ permeated every conversation we had with them,” said Thom Glover, Founder and CCO at American Haiku.
“We consider ourselves specialists in building worlds for brands. Having the opportunity to collaborate with FUNDAMENTALco, who are at the apex of their field in a slightly different discipline, helped deliver the best possible campaign for Tricon. We look forward to partnering with them again for future projects where strategic clarity and creative storytelling can come together to push the category forward,” added Glover. 

By grounding the refresh in Tricon’s operational reality - not just a new look - FUNDAMENTALco and American Haiku have helped the company articulate a clearer, more resonant identity at a time when expectations around renting continue to evolve.

records.title: A Real Nigerian Prince
records.description:
Vaseline has created a new authentication tool and enlisted the help of a Nigerian Prince to launch a fight back against fake versions of Vaseline Body Oils in Nigeria through a campaign created by Leo Singapore of Publicis Groupe.
With the global trade in fake goods estimated at USD 467 billion[1], Nigeria's skincare market has not been spared. Consumers are increasingly at risk of using products made with unregulated, untested and potentially harmful ingredients that can lead to adverse reactions and health risks.
While Unilever already works with local authorities, the effects of enforcement action against fakes rarely reach consumers fast enough. This initiative makes it possible for consumers to shop with peace of mind and protect themselves from fakes.
Chat and Check
First launched in Nigeria, the innovation behind the campaign is the Vaseline Authenticator - a free, WhatsApp-based tool that allows consumers to confirm the authenticity of their Vaseline Body Oils in seconds.
Consumers scan a QR code or click on the WhatsApp link appearing on campaign materials to open a WhatsApp conversation. Users will then chat with the “Prince’s assistant” who would request for photos of the front and back of the Vaseline Body Oil product and receive instant confirmation of whether the product is real or fake. The authenticator is currently built for Vaseline Body Oils, the most vulnerable product to being counterfeited at the moment.
“Counterfeit products are a growing concern for Nigerian consumers, particularly when it comes to products people trust for their skin. This initiative is about making authenticity simple to check, using a tool they already have in their pocket” says Shazan Zahir, Head of Beauty & Wellbeing, Unilever International.
“This initiative is our way of fighting back, not just as a brand, but alongside the consumers and retailers who are affected most. We want every Vaseline product picked up in Lagos, Abuja or anywhere in Nigeria to be the real thing." says Anirban Mullick - Head of Sales Africa, Unilever International.
Getting Real with Royalty
For years, the idea of a “Nigerian Prince” has been synonymous with online scams, making Prince Chris Okagbue of the Onitsha Kingdom the perfect figure to reclaim the narrative and restore trust.

In the social media video, Prince Okagbue refers to the fake Prince scam but affirms that he is the real thing. He suggests that fakes make people question the authenticity of everything. He picks up a bottle of Vaseline which looks authentic but throws it in the bin as it is a counterfeit.
At this point, he announces that he has partnered with Vaseline to launch a new solution which allows consumers to check if their Vaseline Body Oil is real or fake. He delivers the campaign slogan: “Don’t let fakes get under your skin.”
Leo Singapore developed the Vaseline Authenticator tool and social media campaign in partnership with Unilever International.
"This brief started as a counterfeit problem but turned out to be one of the most engaging campaigns we've ever made. A real Nigerian Prince fighting fakes - we felt that would be quite a surprising solution to a real business problem," says Asheen Naidu, Group Executive Creative Director at Leo Singapore.
The campaign will run with OOH buys featuring the QR codes in Lekki for awareness and Surulere which has a strong youth presence and also retail stores across Nigeria, from structured hubs like Market Square and SPAR, to neighbourhood superstores like Justrite, and trusted pharmacy chains such as H-Medix.

records.title: A RESIST'R CASE
records.description:
Eastpak’s “A “Resist’r Case campaign is a clever nod to action thrillers like Ronin and Pulp Fiction. It tells the story of two guys tasked with delivering a suitcase from point A to B. Naturally, things go sideways. Spies, chaos, and urban chases ensue, with rooftops, alleys, and gritty cityscapes in Brussels setting the tone.

The real star? The suitcase. It’s tossed, scraped, dropped, and dragged through it all—never missing a beat. No dents, no fuss, just pure resilience. More than just a bag, it feels like a reliable sidekick, built for the kind of chaos life throws your way. Built to resist.

The campaign is simple yet striking, showing off Eastpak’s design in a way that feels effortless but memorable. It’s not flashy—it’s functional, and that’s exactly the point.

records.title: A Summer of Soccer
records.description:
Mondelēz International has launched a soccer-focused summer campaign created by LePub New York and produced by Publicis Production USA. Directed by Max Gutierrez, the campaign brings together football stars Christian Pulisic, Alex Morgan and Sophia Wilson alongside Pitbull to celebrate a summer of soccer through the brand’s best-known snack products.

The initiative includes limited-edition releases from brands such as RITZ and CHIPS AHOY!, positioning snacking as a central part of the fan experience during major sporting moments. Anchored by the “Score Snack Goals” sweepstakes, the campaign gives consumers the chance to win prizes including trips and meet-and-greet experiences with players and celebrities, blending fandom, entertainment and product engagement.

Building on Mondelēz’s broader sports marketing strategy, the campaign reinforces the role of snacks in communal viewing occasions, from international soccer to major American sporting events. By pairing globally recognised talent with nostalgic snack brands, the company aims to create a culturally resonant platform that connects food, football and celebration throughout the tournament season.

records.title: Action Bronson Want You to Slow Down This Fourth of July
records.campaign_title: Action Bronson Want You to Slow Down This Fourth of July
records.description:
Minute Maid Spiked® & Action Bronson Want You to Slow Down This Fourth of July

This Fourth of July, Action Bronson is redefining what it means to raise a glass. As an integrated part of the Minute Maid Spiked® Duality Campaign, in the Sip Slow spot Bronson brings his signature passion for food, flavor and culture to a simple idea: the best things in life aren't rushed—including your drink.

Rather than relying on traditional "drink responsibly" messaging, the spot reframes moderation through Bronson's lens. If you take your time with a great meal, a backyard cookout, or good company, why wouldn't you do the same with what you sipping?

Launching ahead of July 4th, one of the biggest holidays for backyard indulgence of the year, the campaign aims to make responsible drinking feel less like a rule and more like a lifestyle, one rooted in savoring the moment instead of speeding through it.

records.title: AFCON 2025 – "Supporting Your Team From Afar"
records.description:
Being an immigrant means carrying two worlds at once. The daily reality of building a life abroad, and the emotional pull of home. During AFCON 2025, that pull gets louder.

This campaign taps into a universal moment: watching your team play from thousands of miles away. The tension of following a match while pretending to work. The joy that bursts out in inappropriate places. The strangers who suddenly become family when your team scores.
"Supporting your team from afar is hard. Sending money with Sendwave is easy."

Two spots capture these moments with humor and heart. Part of Sendwave's broader "Immigrant Life" platform, adapted for the biggest football tournament on the continent.

records.title: AI-Generated Custom Brand Music for A Cafe
records.campaign_title: AI-Generated Custom Brand Music for A Cafe
records.description:
AI-generated brand anthem and custom-written rap created exclusively for Cafe Blob.

The objective was not just to create a reel but to translate the café’s personality into an original audio-visual identity that audiences could instantly feel and associate with the brand. Instead of relying on stock music or trending sounds, the entire track was conceptualised from scratch around the energy, atmosphere, and tone of the space.

The rap lyrics were written specifically for the brand, following which an AI-generated custom track was developed to match the intended mood and rhythm. The final reel was then edited frame-by-frame to sync with the music, resulting in a branded anthem unique to Cafe Blob.

At a time when digital content often feels repetitive and template-driven, the idea was to create something native to the brand, culturally relevant, memorable, and impossible to replicate through conventional formats.

records.title: AI-Verts
records.description:
FCB is rolling out a global campaign for Intuit QuickBooks to support the financial management software’s new ‘Intuit Platform’, an advanced, all-in-one, AI-powered business management system designed to help businesses and accountants work smarter, faster, and more strategically.

The campaign celebrates the powerful blend of AI and HU (Human Intelligence). Its message, “Whatever is holding you back, you can Outdo It with Intuit”, highlights how the Intuit Platform gives business owners time back for what really matters – getting richer insights for better money outcomes – while allowing accountants to foster better client collaboration. 

FCB New York developed the global platform idea, creative strategy, and global TVC and VOD, while FCB London took the lead on social, radio, and influencer activity across UK and EMEA. The multi-channel campaign brings to life the simple, seamless way business owners collaborate with QuickBooks’ AI agents to support the way they work, every day.

The social-first films from FCB London bring the use of AI to life with playful, tech-leaning spots that dramatise the partnership between human stories and AI wizardry. Dubbed ‘AI-verts’, the spots show the growth and transformation of real people and real businesses working with QuickBooks. They feature an eclectic range of enterprises including a retro-inspired ski wear brand, a video production company and bespoke tent installation company, all sharing how QuickBooks’ new product has powered their prosperity.

FCB London worked with 456 Studios and Purple Martin to utilise the latest AI tools to shift time from technical execution to creative development. Combining both in-person and AI production techniques, the team shot real humans in real life and used AI to place them right into the environment where QuickBooks is having the most impact on their business – whether that’s a ski slope, a race track, a tech convention, or even a Pirate-themed computer game.

The global launch is supported by an influencer workstream, with FCB London partnering with social teams across FCB’s global network and creators such as Ali Abdaal, Timony Armoo, Kelly Hoppen, Nisha Shah, and Ben Askin to drive momentum across EMEA.

The campaign breaks late November 2025, with additional content rolling out through December. The TVC and VOD will run in Australia, Canada, the UK and US, while the social, radio, and influencer content will go live across the UK and EMEA priority markets including Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, South Africa, and the UAE.

The TVC and VOD will run in Australia, Canada, the UK and US, while the social, radio, and influencer content will go live across the UK and EMEA priority markets including Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, South Africa, and the UAE.

records.title: Airheads Have More Fun
records.description:
Airheads is putting a fresh twist on its head inflation ads from the early 2000s to appeal to both new and old fans.

A recurring visual gag in earlier Airheads commercials showed heads expanding after eating the candy and then bouncing around tennis courts or train carriages. A new series of irreverent spots, created by agency Highdive, is the latest example of a brand tapping into millennial nostalgia.

Four 15-second spots, directed by Harold Einstein, include the tagline, "Airheads have more fun."

The campaign launches today (Aug. 11) across YouTube, Meta platforms, TikTok, Snapchat, and online video, with more head-inflation fun to come throughout the year.

"Grandpa Likes ‘Em" sees two kids being reprimanded after inflating the head of their unsuspecting grandfather, while "Inflate Off" features an intense face-off between an Airhead chewer and inflatable flamingo.

"Oh Snap" has two fans getting into mischief by the pool, and "Pumped Up" stars a wannabe muscle man trying an Airhead-assisted shortcut.

The new ads are inspired by what older fans remember most about the brand, said Chad Broude, co-founder and co-chief creative officer at Highdive.

"The head inflation ads came up again and again, completely unprompted," Broude said. "That kind of recall is a big opportunity. It reminded us that just because a brand has been around for a while, it doesn't mean people are tired of it. In fact, it's often the opposite."

Injecting fun into the brand was a key goal of the campaign, according to Chris Borges, brand director of the non-chocolate portfolio at Perfetti Van Melle, the owner of Airheads.

"This campaign was inspired by the people who grew up loving Airheads and still enjoy them today," he said. "We're leaning into what fans remember most-the inflating heads-and building fun, imaginative stories around why it happens when you bite into Airheads. Because people who enjoy Airheads truly have more fun."

records.title: Akylas Meal
records.description:
There are a few cases where  a celebrity collaboration feels less like a brand deal and more like a genuine cultural moment. The Akylas Meal for McDonald's Greece was one of those.

Akylas, the pop star who carried Greece's flag to the Eurovision Song Contest and became a European sensation with his song FERTO (bring it), wasn't just lending his name to a menu. 

He was already a McDonald's fan and had the same style energy: authentic and unapologetically feel-good.
Thus, utilizing his new song "PARTO" (take it/get it) we tapped into a McDonald's truth: Deep down, we already know what we want, we just haven't admitted it yet.

The insight came from something deeply human: we almost always know what we want. We just talk ourselves out of it. That moment of fake hesitation — "should I get the nuggets?", "what should I order?" — is a ritual we all perform, even when the answer is already written all over our faces.
So we gave that inner voice a face. With the song.

In two films, the same comic premise plays out in different McDonald's settings. A friend pretends to weigh up whether to grab a nugget. A driver at the McDrive acts undecided about the Akylas Meal. Before anyone can answer, Akylas himself appears, bursting into his now-trending hook: "papapapapa-párto" (get it.) 
He's not there to persuade anyone. He's there to say out loud what everyone already feels.

The casting was the creative. Akylas's natural charisma, comic timing and way of appearance made the conceit work not just as advertising but as entertainment. The kind of content people share because it makes them smile, not because an algorithm pushed it at them.

records.title: Alentá como el mejor (Root like the best)
records.campaign_title: Alentá como el mejor (Root like the best)
records.description: In a World Cup year, Grido wanted to make a bold statement with its campaign—but with one small limitation: it didn’t have the official license of the Uruguayan national team. So instead, we went after La Celeste’s greatest icon, Luis Suárez. We realized it would be his first World Cup as a fan, not a player. After so many years, Uruguay’s all-time top scorer became just another supporter—cheering for his country, while enjoying Grido, of course.

records.title: All Dressed Up
records.description:
Shania Twain has teamed up with McDonald’s Canada to launch the “All Dressed Up” campaign, spotlighting two of the chain’s beloved fan-favourites transformed with a fashionable twist. Starting August 12 for a limited time, patrons can order the All Dressed McShaker™ Fries—iconic fries dusted in the quintessential Canadian “All Dressed” seasoning—and a warm, flaky Strawberry Pie filled with real strawberry pieces. Appropriate for the occasion, these styled-up menu items are available across participating locations, through the McDonald's app, or via McDelivery®.

The collaboration carries extra meaning for Shania—it’s a heartfelt full-circle moment. Before her meteoric rise to country music stardom, she worked behind the counter at McDonald’s in Toronto. “I fell in love with McDonald’s fries while working as a crew member in Toronto,” she reflects. “Being able to dress them up with my personal touch was surreal.” As part of the campaign, fans can also score a playful Cowboy Boot Keychain with the purchase of an Extra Value Meal, adding a collectible charm to their order. The ad captures Shania’s effervescent energy and Canadian pride as she helps “dress up” the classic McDonald’s experience.

records.title: All Over the Body & Lower Body
records.campaign_title: All Over the Body & Lower Body
records.description:
Cannes Gold Film Craft winners Axe’s “Robbery” and “Funeral” were standout ads last year, perfectly blending humor with the brand’s signature edge. 

Now, creative agency LOLA MullenLowe reunites with directing duo Lionel Goldstein to deliver a new and bold campaign for Axe, titled: "Dog", “Bear”and “Baby”.

This time, they explore the theme of sweetness, but with an unexpected twist. The new spots cleverly subvert traditional notions of charm and kindness, offering a version of “sweet” that’s anything but conventional. The result? A series of hilariously ads that stay true to Axe’s playful, irreverent tone while keeping audiences laughing.

Lionel is the Belgian directing duo of Joe Vanhoutteghem and Koen Mortier.

records.title: Amazon Shoppers Great Freedom Sale
records.description:
Amazon India's campaign for the Great Freedom Sale 2026 directly highlights consumer shopping behaviours by focusing on relatable shopper personas. Created in collaboration with the agency- Schbang, produced by- Mothership Productions, and Directed by- Karan Shetty the campaign shifts away from just listing price cuts and instead focuses on how Indian consumers uniquely navigate major sales. 

The Core Campaign - Personas of Shoppers

The Shikari (hunter) Shopper: The ad film begins by using the iconic A-to-Z arrow from Amazon's logo to transition into the world of the Shikari (hunter) shopper, who is always on the look out for the best deals, like a hunter. 
The Tol-Mol (comparing) Shopper: Hyper-calculative buyers who refuses to hit checkout until they have stacked every possible coupon, bank discount, and cashback offer and have compared every possible deal. 
The Deal-Pe-Deal Shopper: The impulsive bargain hunters who continuously finds "one more great deal" to add to their cart. 
The FOMO Shopper: The shopper who continuously makes sure that he isn’t missing out. He is the Fear Of Missing Our (FOMO) shopper.  
The BOGO Shopper: The shopper who constantly tries to get a one plus one deal offer. They are the Buy One Get One (BOGO) Free shoppers.  

The campaign was narrated by a very honest voice over artist that spoke about these shoppers in a witty, charming style whilst being relatable making the montage moments in the campaign stand out.

records.title: & More
records.description:
Hennion & Walsh Asset Management highlights its’ services in new “& More” campaign created by AML

Independent US financial services firm Hennion & Walsh Asset Management is taking the message about its growing comprehensive wealth management (CWM) offer to television as part of a new integrated campaign. The work has been created by London-based agency AML, Hennion & Walsh’s creative agency for 10 years.

Founded in New Jersey with a strong heritage in municipal bonds Hennion & Walsh has seen growth in its wealth management subsidiary. 
Hennion & Walsh’s brief to AML was to develop a brand idea to communicate the “why” of its CWM appealing both to an audience without a wealth management provider at all and to those whose funds are currently managed elsewhere.

To do this AML developed a series of TVCs building on Hennion & Walsh’s “The Second Opinion People” creative platform which was introduced in 2024. Under the strapline “& More” the three 30-second TVCs emphasize different aspects of Hennion & Walsh’s core beliefs in the service delivery to its clients. 

“Committed To You” focuses on the firm’s founding values of honesty loyalty and integrity underlining its dedication to clients’ financial goals. “A Team of Specialists” highlights the bespoke team of financial planners portfolio managers and other specialists assembled to suit each client’s unique circumstances. In “A Human Connection” viewers learn about Hennion & Walsh’s belief that clients should always reach the right person directly rather than an automated system.

Bill Walsh Co-founder and Partner at Hennion & Walsh said: “We are excited about this new campaign which clearly articulates for existing and potential clients alike what makes what we call the Hennion & Walsh Experience so different and distinctive from other financial services firms. Ever since Hennion & Walsh was founded in 1990 our unique structure has ensured personalized hands-on advice and service that goes above and beyond to help clients achieve their financial aspirations – a commitment which we believe the “& More” theme perfectly encapsulates.” 

Hugo Bone Executive Creative Director at AML added: “What we love about working with the team at Hennion & Walsh is that they approach growing their brand with the same rigour they apply to supporting clients with their wealth management needs. With this campaign we’re making a compelling case for trusting Hennion & Walsh and helping drive the next stage of their journey.”

The campaign runs on national TV, with further activity running on radio digital display PPC and direct mail activity across multiple US states.

records.campaign_title: Taste Changes Everything: Romeo and Juliet
records.description: This isn’t a Shakespearean tragedy—it's the commercial for the launch of the new Maxibon Red Cheesecake: so irresistible it rewrites the most famous love story in world literature, giving it a deliciously unexpected ending.

records.title: Andy Reid - 2025 Big Game Ad
records.description: Coach Andy Reid appreciates the comfort and convenience of Skechers Hands Free Slip-ins® so he can easily work his side hustle when not focused on football.  There’s so much you can do with your hands when you don’t have to pull on or tie your shoes.  Just Slip In®.

records.title: Anything for the Official Beer of the NFL
records.campaign_title: Anything for the Official Beer of the NFL
records.description:
Football is back, and Bud Light is diving headfirst into the action with a new campaign that showcases the hilarious ways fans do anything for the clean, crisp taste of Bud Light. Starring long-time brand partner and Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning, the Official Beer Sponsor of the NFL is debuting a new commercial, ‘Parachute’, that takes fan devotion to new heights, literally. Bud Light is also helping 21+ fans take their fandom to another level with the return of its limited-edition NFL team cans featuring team logos and colors across 27 sponsored teams across the league. This year’s team cans grant access to special online content, epic at-home tailgates, gear, and prizes all season long.

“As the Official Beer Sponsor of the NFL for nearly three decades, Bud Light has a deep history of going to great lengths to give NFL fans epic experiences. In return, we’ve had a front row seat to the great lengths fans go to support their team and do anything to enjoy a cold Bud Light on gameday,” said Todd Allen, SVP of Marketing for Bud Light at Anheuser-Busch. “This season’s campaign is all about celebrating the passion fans bring day in and day out during the NFL season. With a new spot featuring our longtime partner Peyton Manning, the return of our fan-favorite NFL team cans, and weekly at-home tailgate experiences for fans across the country, we’re raising a cold Bud Light to celebrate fans everywhere who make football season unforgettable.”

Bud Light’s new NFL campaign kicks off with “Parachute,” highlighting just how far fans will go – or free-fall – for a Bud Light. The spot depicts Peyton Manning epically skydiving into a football stadium as part of the NFL airman brigade. Aiming for the field, he calls a last-minute audible to change course towards what he thinks is an ice-cold Bud Light, but instead meets his fate when he learns it’s actually a very realistic stadium billboard. In a light-hearted salute to the great lengths fans (and football legends) will go for the clean, crisp taste Bud Light, Parachute is set to run in both :15 and :30 formats starting today and throughout the NFL season.

“This Bud Light campaign captures the go-all-out spirit that NFL fans bring to their team each season,” said Pro Football Hall of Famer and Bud Light partner Peyton Manning. “Whether you're going ‘jumping-out-of-a-plane’ big or more low-key and just enjoying a beer at home, Bud Light helps to celebrate the love we all have for the game.”

This marks Manning’s sixth campaign with Bud Light, most recently starring in Bud Light’s digital comedy sketch ‘Armchair Quarterback’ that debuted as part of the brand’s larger partnership with Netflix and Omaha Productions on Netflix’s “Quarterback” season 2.

BUD LIGHT DEBUTS 2025 LIMITED-EDITION NFL TEAM CANS

Bud Light is going the distance for fans once again as the brand brings back its fan-favorite NFL team cans for the 2025 season with a sleek new look that is sure to get 21+ fans everywhere pumped to rep their team this season whether they are watching at home, at the bar or in the stadium. This year’s team can lineup includes all 27 of Bud Light’s sponsored NFL teams, prominently showcasing team logos, full bleed official team colors, and jersey-inspired retro stripes wrapping the top and bottom of each can. Each can also includes a QR code giving fans access to content and exclusive experiences like VIP tailgates, game tickets, and one-of-a-kind merch drops.

GOING THE EXTRA YARD FOR FANS ALL SEASON LONG
For the first time, Bud Light is bringing the ultimate tailgate from the stadium lots to fans at home with its “Bring Home the Official Tailgate” program. Every week of the NFL regular season, 21+ fans can enter for the chance to win an at-home tailgate experience. The experience comes complete with epic game-day essentials including a Traeger grill and backyard TV delivered straight to their door. Fans will also have the chance to win NFL game tickets, team merchandise, and NFL Shop gift cards throughout the season.

records.title: AS REFRESHING AS
records.description: Any beer can claim to be refreshing, but only Amstel—with its Amsterdam-born recipe—can say it’s as refreshing as being yourself.

records.title: ASMR Of Progress
records.description: ASMR of Progress is a sound-first Ramadan TVC for Emirates Development Bank, built around the idea that real progress isn’t loud it’s precise. Through cinematic macro shots and tactile, satisfying foley, the film turns small moments of making, building, and movement into a calm rhythm that feels intimate and intentional. Every second is designed to be heard as much as it’s seen delivering a modern Ramadan tone rooted in craft, focus, and forward momentum.

records.title: At the Heart of Home Life
records.campaign_title: At the Heart of Home Life
records.description:
A washing machine with the wit of Russell Tovey. An oven with Phillipa Dunne’s comic timing. A fridge voiced by Terence Maynard. After 100 years on the high street, Hughes, the family-owned electrical retailer beloved across East Anglia, has unveiled its first ever brand campaign, created by BIRD London with media partner Palace Project.

Titled *At the Heart of Home Life*, the campaign brings household appliances to life as quirky, chatty characters who bicker, banter, and quietly keep family life running – a playful twist on Hughes’ belief that electricals are the unsung heroes of every home.

Hughes has long been seen as a dependable high street retailer, much loved by its loyal customers, quietly part of everyday life. But in a crowded market, staying visible is harder than ever. This campaign brings the brand to life by giving voice and personality to the machines that keep homes running, reminding a new generation why Hughes still matters – and making people smile while doing it.

"This campaign represents a significant moment for Hughes," said Emily Stoten, Marketing Director, Hughes. "After a century of serving East Anglian families, we recognised the need to evolve our brand connection while staying true to our family values. These animated characters perfectly capture how our appliances become part of people's daily lives – reliable, hardworking, and essential to keeping families happy."

Seven animated characters take centre stage in the campaign’s 30" and 20" TV spots; a lively cast designed by award-winning illustrator and director Al Murphy of Everyone Agency. The characters gossip like co-workers once the humans leave, showing the everyday dedication of the machines that keep homes humming.

The voice cast includes Russell Tovey (*Being Human, Years and Years*) as the ever-diligent washing machine, Phillipa Dunne (*Derry Girls*) as the warm-hearted oven, and Terence Maynard (*Coronation Street*) as the no-nonsense fridge.

“Electrical retailers usually compete on specs and price,” said Steve Parker, Strategy Partner, BIRD London. “But Hughes has survived 100 years because people genuinely love and trust it. We wanted to tell a bigger story. One that’s warm, funny, and human. These characters let us show that appliances aren’t just machines. They’re the heartbeat of family life.”

*At the Heart of Home Life* marks Hughes’ first fully integrated, cross-channel brand campaign, with Palace Project driving the media strategy. The 360 campaign first launches on TV before rolling out across outdoor, radio, digital, and in-store. The campaign focuses on long-term brand-building, key to a family business looking to secure their place in the minds – and hearts – of families planning their next big purchase.

"After a century of serving East Anglian families, we recognised the need to evolve our brand connection while staying true to our family values. These animated characters perfectly capture how our appliances become part of people's daily lives – reliable, hardworking, and essential to keeping families happy."

Seven animated characters take centre stage in the campaign’s 30" and 20" TV spots; a lively cast designed by award-winning illustrator and director Al Murphy of Everyone Agency. The characters gossip like co-workers once the humans leave, showing the everyday dedication of the machines that keep homes humming.

The voice cast includes Russell Tovey (*Being Human, Years and Years*) as the ever-diligent washing machine, Phillipa Dunne (*Derry Girls*) as the warm-hearted oven, and Terence Maynard (*Coronation Street*) as the no-nonsense fridge.

“Electrical retailers usually compete on specs and price,” said Steve Parker, Strategy Partner, BIRD London. “But Hughes has survived 100 years because people genuinely love and trust it. We wanted to tell a bigger story. One that’s warm, funny, and human. These characters let us show that appliances aren’t just machines. They’re the heartbeat of family life.”

*At the Heart of Home Life* marks Hughes’ first fully integrated, cross-channel brand campaign, with Palace Project driving the media strategy. The 360 campaign first launches on TV before rolling out across outdoor, radio, digital, and in-store. The campaign focuses on long-term brand-building, key to a family business looking to secure their place in the minds – and hearts – of families planning their next big purchase.

records.title: Ba Codes Of Love
records.description:
Nestlé MILO Vietnam's Father's Day campaign "BA CODES OF LOVE" transforms an overlooked barcode silhouette into a tribute to the quiet ways Vietnamese dads express love.

Though dads play such an undeniably important role in kids' growth journey, they hardly ever show up as the heroes of FMCG campaigns. While Mother’s Day is widely celebrated, Father's Day doesn’t receive as much attention. And MILO wanted to change it.

The Insight 
In Vietnam, as across much of Asia, dads do not often say "I love you." Their love is communicated through everyday actions: spending the time to do the things kids love, buying 10x the things kids said they liked once, playing sports with them despite the weather, or being at their side even when nobody is watching.

The Discovery
All Nestlé MILO packs sold in Vietnam have a barcode. But not many people noticed there’s an illustration of two people playing basketball together. That discovery became the starting point for "BA CODES OF LOVE." with a play on the word barcode, where "ba" means dad in Vietnamese.

The Craft
Instead of relying on technology to do the work, the brand collaborated with real artists to hand-draw nearly 300 illustrations. Each drawing captured a sports moment between a dad and kid. Frame by frame, those moments grew into a story.

The illustrations were then photographed one by one and assembled into a handcrafted stop-motion film — a process that required patience, and hundreds of hours of work. But that was exactly the point. Because just like a dad's love, the most meaningful things are often built through small actions repeated over time.

The Execution
The stop-motion film expanded the tiny story hidden inside the barcode into something many families would recognize. It tells the story of a dad who may never say "I love you" out loud, but shows it in different ways. Rooted in MILO's belief that Sport Is A Great Teacher, the film shines a light on the dads helping those lessons happen every day. 
The story then moved beyond the pack and onto Vietnam's busiest streets through an LED series, bringing dads into the spotlight.
To invite more people into the campaign, MILO also launched a digital experience where users could create and share their own Ba Codes Of Love - turning personal memories into a collective thank-you to the dads who have been there all along.

Mr. Binu Jacob, Chairman & CEO of Nestlé Vietnam, added:
“As a dad, I've learned that many of the things you do for your children often go unnoticed. But that doesn’t stop dads showing up. Maybe that's why so many people saw their own dad in the campaign. Because it didn't ask people to discover something new but to notice something that had always been there.”

Ms. Le Bui Thi Mai Uyen, Business Executive Officer of Nestlé MILO Vietnam, shared:
“Many dads express love through actions rather than words. They wake up early, make time, and stand by their children through every practice and every setback. Through BA CODE OF LOVE, we wanted to celebrate those everyday moments that may seem small, but leave a lasting impact on a kid’s growth.”

Ms. Tra My Nguyen, Managing Director of Ogilvy Vietnam, added:
“In more than 15 years partnering with MILO, I've told many stories about children's growth, where mothers have traditionally been at the heart of the narrative. This campaign challenged us to ask a different question: what if the hero of that journey had been there all along? 
Rather than creating a new story, BA CODE OF LOVE invited people to see the everyday story of fatherhood through a different lens—one that celebrates the quiet acts of love that shape a child's growth every day.”

From barcode to “Ba Code Of Love”, MILO and Ogilvy Vietnam turned a detail no one had ever noticed into a story millions of people could see themselves in.

records.title: Baby
records.description:
Mike’s Amazing, a Chefler Foods condiment brand, is back with the next chapter of its award-winning brand campaign, “When It’s On, It’s On,” once again starring renowned comedic actor Jason Alexander. The fifth installment of the campaign will debut during the Opening Ceremony of the 2026 Winter Olympic Games, marking the brand’s biggest media moment yet.
Building on the momentum of previous spots, including last year’s summer campaign and regional Super Bowl appearance, the new ad, titled “Baby,” features Alexander playing six distinct characters whose lives hilariously intersect over a shared love of Mike’s Amazing all playing out while one character is in the labor and delivery room. The spot highlights both Mike’s Amazing Real Mayonnaise and Mike’s Amazing Deli Mustard, reinforcing the brand’s expanding portfolio with its standard comedic humor and charm. 
Alexander first joined the “When It’s On, It’s On” campaign in 2024, helping the brand earn industry recognition, an Effie and Gold and Silver LIA awards, for its distinctive humor and bold creative voice.
“Every time I think we’ve taken these characters as far as they can go, this team finds a way to push it even further,” said Alexander. “I like that Mike’s Amazing doesn’t play it safe…”
Founded in 2016, celebrating their 10th anniversary this year, the Mike's Amazing brand is the fastest-growing condiments brand in America; and well known amongst sports fanatics for being the official mayonnaise, mustard and vegetable oil of the New York Yankees, New York Mets, New York Rangers, New Jersey Devils, Philadelphia Phillies, Philadelphia Flyers, Boston Red Sox, Boston Bruins, Miami Heat, Tampa Bay Lightning, Florida Panthers, Atlanta Braves, Atlanta Falcons, Baltimore Orioles, New Orleans Saints, New Orleans Pelicans, Carolina Hurricanes and the Washington Capitals.
“For years, I watched major brands take the Olympic stage and thought, that’s a different level. This year, we’re no longer watching—we’re part of it,” said Michael Leffler, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Mike’s Amazing/Chefler Foods LLC.
The brand’s competitive spirit and pride in product quality continue to serve as the foundation for the campaign’s confident, high-energy tone. The campaign was created in collaboration with creative agency of record Havas New York and media by Ramp 97. Talent procurement was handled by Official Partner.
“To go from a start up out of New Jersey to sponsoring the Winter Olympics so quickly is nothing short of amazing,” said Michael Kurland, Chief Financial Officer of Mike’s Amazing/Chefler Foods LLC.
“Launching a fifth spot during the Winter Olympics gave us permission to go bigger-and weirder-than ever,” said Josh Schildkraut, Executive Creative Director, Havas New York. “Six characters, two products, one very pregnant Jason Alexander. Because when it’s on, it’s really on.”
The campaign will run across broadcast, connected TV, digital, social, and additional high-impact placements.

records.title: Badman's trap
records.description:
Seeing a 220% surge in phishing reports—over 69,000 cases in Q1 alone—DANA and our team responded with the hashtag #AwasJebakanBadMan (Watch Out for the Badman's Trap). The phrase "AWAS JEBAKAN BADMAN" is a playful slang in Indonesia with a twist. It originates from "Jebakan Batman," which means "Batman’s trap," a term used to describe falling into a trick or deception without realizing it. In this case, "Batman" has been changed to "Badman" to give it a humorous, streetwise twist, suggesting the trap or scam was set up by a "bad guy." It’s a warning to be cautious of hidden scams or traps from people with bad intentions.

This campaign takes a fresh spin on digital safety, breaking down three essential anti-scam tips in an engaging way that sticks.
These tips are presented in a creative and relatable way, featuring talents that you wouldn’t traditionally expect in this context. The unconventional casting choice is intended to deliver a ‘stopping power’ effect, catching attention and making the message even easier to digest for our target audience.

records.title: Bags of Northern Soul
records.description:
Seabrook Crisps is launching "Bags of Northern Soul," a new brand platform created by Quiet Storm, marking the agency's first work since winning the account in a competitive pitch in September 2025.
A significant new creative direction for the brand, "Bags of Northern Soul" stakes out challenger territory for Seabrook, built to accelerate its nationwide growth, both within and beyond its Northern heartland.
To take Seabrook beyond product-led advertising and into a broader brand space, the platform draws on the brand's Bradford heritage, bringing to life a distinctive Northern attitude that feels universally appealing: warm, grounded, resilient and quick to offer encouragement. At the heart of the idea is the belief that Northern Soul is about more than where you're from. It's about how you show up - a strong, memorable platform built to stretch across regions, channels and future campaigns.
The launch campaign runs across TV, paid social, radio, out-of-home and in-store activations, brought to life through a distinct visual and tonal world that is warm, witty and unmistakably Northern.
At the heart of the hero film is Seabrook's sentient potato character, who arrives at just the right moment to turn an everyday crisis of confidence into a celebration of self-belief, brilliantly embodying the Northern Soul platform with deadpan humour and infectious optimism.
Across out-of-home and social, the campaign extends the platform through product-focused executions that carry the same playful tone. Lines like "Life is like a sandwich, better with crisps" and "There's always a silver lining" capture the brand's glass-half-full spirit, inviting audiences to smile before they even reach for the bag.
The campaign was directed by Gustav Egerstedt and created and produced in-house by Quiet Storm.
Media, planned by Cheeky Communications, takes a dual North/South approach. In the North, the campaign focuses on maintaining a strong share of voice across TV, VOD, digital and social. In the South, activity is designed to build mental availability through ITVX, digital audio, podcasts and proximity out-of-home.
The campaign is being further supported with organic social media managed by Box Cat Creative, and PR by Open Communications.

records.title: Bart the Old Fart
records.description:
Presenting a new campaign for Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH) from Doner. The healthcare network is leaning into humor to tackle a serious subject: colorectal cancer screening. The campaign, “Bart the Old Fart,” developed in partnership with its creative agency of record, Doner, introduces Bart as a witty, wise elder who urges younger audiences to get screened so they, too, can “live to be an old fart” like him. It has a clear goal: normalize colonoscopies as a lifesaving measure while driving patients to HMH physicians for screenings.

Five spots sit at the center of the campaign. “Nap” shows Bart on his recliner addressing the fact that a colonoscopy is easy and nothing to worry about. "Think of it as a lifesaving nap," he says as he leans back to close his eyes. “Penny” dispels concerns about affordability, while “Safe” underscores the benefits of screening for early detection and long life. “Good Ol’ Days” corrects misconceptions around the colonoscopy prep process. Finally, “Fishing” shows Bart using his wisdom to discuss the importance of getting a colonoscopy so you can live a long life.

Unlike many health pushes that rely on statistics and somber tones, this one banks on relatability. By using a candid, elder spokesperson, HMH aims to break down stigmas and reframe colonoscopies as part of responsible self-care.

“This campaign takes a fresh, approachable tone to a topic many people would rather avoid,” said Opeyemi Oluwole, SVP Chief Marketing Officer, Hackensack Meridian Health. “By using levity through Bart’s character, we’re able to ease concerns and ultimately encourage more people to get screened. Early detection saves lives, and if we can break through and get that message across with a smile, we’re doing our job.”

“One of the most challenging tasks in healthcare marketing is to create work that informs and inspires action,” said David DeMuth, CEO of Doner. “This campaign, and the creation of the Bart character, strikes a delicate balance of being educational, instructional and undeniably charming.”

The campaign goes live today across social, streaming video, programmatic display and CTV.

records.title: BDC in tune with entrepreneurs
records.description:
The Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) and Cossette are striking the right note this year with a new national brand campaign that strengthens BDC’s position as an accelerator for the ambitions of Canadian entrepreneurs. Following an economic downturn, this campaign illustrates how BDC drives the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SME).  

The key visual of the campaign features metronomes symbolizing Canadian businesses, guided by talented violinist Tanya Charles Iveniuk, who represents BDC. She uses rhythm to breathe life and energy into the metronomes, illustrating how BDC supports businesses. She then starts to increase the tempo, building the momentum that businesses need to grow. This shows how BDC works with businesses to orchestrate and support their growth, allowing them to reach their full potential.

records.title: Be a Bonehead
records.description:
For years Kettle & Fire has grown a massive, and passionate, fanbase in the bone broth category, earning shoutouts from Joe Rogan and building from a startup into a $100 Million brand that’s sold in grocery stores across the country. 
Now, fresh off expanding its production capabilities to meet demand, the brand is rolling out its first-ever brand campaign—a bold, comedic, and proudly weird swing that was created by Chicago-based agency Someoddpilot.
Titled “Be a Bonehead,” the campaign takes a prehistoric point of view that champions simplicity in a world of overcomplicated health trends; drawing from the brand’s tagline, “Simple ingredients. Simple prep. Simple nutrition.”
It’s a massive departure for the category, which typically focuses on clean kitchens and cooking moms. Instead, Someoddpilot delivers dirty cave-people, sipping on the best broth in the land. 
Running across web, social, and CTV, the campaign centers on a :30 hero spot that follows a cavewomen and caveman going about their daily routine, eating “grass-feed, free-range, all-organic everything.”
Targeted towards the modern wellness seeker overwhelmed by powders, pills, and pricey gadgets, these no-frills cave-people remind people of the original superfood: bone broth.
In a tech-forward world, the campaign attempts to make things feel real, carving out a world Kettle & Fire can continue to build equity in.
The work strategically tethers the brand to the product and category, while positioning Kettle & Fire as the go-to for health seekers who know that sometimes, simpler really is smarter.

records.title: Be Unforgettable
records.description:
Colle McVoy is behind Revlon’s latest global push, bringing back the iconic “Revlon Be Unforgettable” platform with a modern twist aimed at restoring the brand’s cultural and category relevance.

Leading the relaunch is multi-platinum country star Megan Moroney, signaling a deliberate shift toward a new wave of talent shaping modern femininity. She’s the first in a global roster of “unforgettable” women the brand will introduce over time.

An award-winning artist redefining modern femininity, Moroney brings a fresh, contemporary sensibility to the storied platform – pairing effortless glamour with authenticity and creative expression. As she embarks on her first massive arena tour – THE CLOUD 9 TOUR – she represents a new generation of women shaping culture on their own terms, reinforcing that true impact is rooted not only in beauty, but also in depth, confidence and self‑definition.

“This campaign represents a truth I believe in: beauty is only one part of what makes someone unforgettable,” added Moroney. “There's power in reminding women they can take up space and lead with confidence, authenticity and strength. Being part of that message means a lot to me.”

A modern expression of a legacy platform that has long celebrated confidence, glamour and individuality, this fresh chapter of “Revlon Be Unforgettable” will speak to today's consumer through voices who embody both beauty and substance.

The fully integrated global campaign spans TV, social, digital, influencer, retail and OOH, with Moroney fronting creative for key franchises including PhotoReady and Glimmer. The campaign launches with two :15 spots featuring Moroney: “Be Unforgettable” and “Lip Plump.”

This also marks the first work for Colle McVoy since the agency was tapped as Revlon’s newest creative partner late 2025. 

“We set out to honor Revlon's history and brand DNA while evolving the campaign through contemporary creative choices, including modern camera techniques,” said Lia Khayami Quiñones, Group Creative Director at Colle McVoy. “The quick, fluid camerawork moves around the women to reflect their multidimensionality. The original imagined what it meant to be unforgettable – now, we're defining what it truly means today."

records.title: Beans Again
records.description:
GOYA®'s latest campaign, Beans Again, is anything but business as usual. Created to highlight the brand’s wide variety of beans and its ongoing mission to stay fresh with younger audiences, the new spot brings a surreal, high-energy twist to a very familiar question: Beans again?

Enter Charlie. He’s in the bean aisle (relatable), thinking about dinner. Beans again? he wonders. And then, boom, the entire universe answers. A talking sweatshirt, a fun sloth, a swordfish, and even a tomato can all start cheering him on. Beans again! Beans again! Yesssss, beans again! It’s weird. It’s loud. It’s oddly inspiring.

And it ends the way all great grocery stories should: with a basket full of beans. Black, pinto, chickpeas, red kidney, and like... a dozen more. GOYA® has options. Serious variety for every taste, vibe, or mood. So yeah, beans again. But never the same beans twice.

The spot was created by Dieste, directed by PLÁSTICO, and produced by Easy Mondays. It’s part of GOYA®’s ongoing effort to reclaim its iconic status in America’s pantries.

records.title: Beauty in Motion | Seto's Post-Production
records.description: A stylish three-part beauty campaign created for Turquaz Dubai, blending luxury cosmetics, feminine elegance, and modern visual storytelling through sleek motion design and cinematic post-production. The campaign focused on highlighting makeup products, beauty aesthetics, and premium brand identity using glossy visuals, soft lighting, elegant transitions, and fashion-inspired pacing tailored for digital platforms and social media audiences.

We decided to showcase the various 'Vahanas' accompanying the children of Goddess Durga along the same lines as normal humans who love pandal hopping. Since who doesn't like to be in the thick of festival spirits?

records.title: Better When It's Bonkers
records.country: New Zealand, United Kingdom, and United States
records.description: Is your cat darting across the room in a flash? Is your dog violently spinning in circles? Has the pet you optimistically named Zen suddenly and irretrievably gone feral?  It may be the Bonkers Effect—an affliction of zoomies brought on by environmental exposure to Bonkers treats. When Rhodes Pet Science popped into This January’s inbox looking to scoop a heap of interest on one of its signature brands, we helped them lean into the chaotic good.  No humans were harmed in the making of this campaign.

records.campaign_title: Bharat ke Har Jeet Mein Win Pens
records.description:
This is a 9-reel Instagram campaign for WIN Guide Pen that celebrates every win in India, big and small. The campaign is built around one simple truth — every win in your life had a pen beside it. That pen is WIN.

The WIN Guide Pen is not the hero of the campaign. It is the silent witness. It is present at every win. From the first time a child writes their name to a father signing house papers to a grandfather passing his pen to his grandchild.

Every reel ends on one powerful Hindi word that captures the feeling of that WIN.

records.title: Biggest Fan Contest
records.description:
From Cinnamon Toast Crunch loyalists to Lucky Charms obsessives, General Mills cereals have inspired devoted fans for generations. And now, those fans have something BIG to rally around. General Mills is passing the ball to sports legend and cereal superfan Shaquille O'Neal, to bring his big personality and love of competition to the first ever Biggest Fan Contest — inviting fans to prove their cereal devotion for the opportunity to win epic prizes, exclusive merch and unforgettable experiences inspired by General Mills Cinnamon Toast Crunch, Lucky Charms, Reese's Puffs and Honey Nut Cheerios cereals.

"I have been eating cereal my whole life, and I'm still just as excited about it now as I was when I was young," said Shaquille O'Neal. "Lucky Charms has always been a favorite — those marshmallows never get old to me. This contest is a chance to celebrate that same excitement in fans everywhere who love cereal as much as I do."

From cereal-themed tattoos to cereal bars at weddings, fans have found bold ways to show off their cereal love for years. With the Biggest Fan Contest, General Mills is giving their superfans the opportunity to prove their passion by uploading a photo or video and sharing why they deserve the title of Biggest Fan.

The competition will feature one massive grand prize plus four cereal-inspired fan experiences and a year's supply of their favorite cereal:

• Grand Prize: A BIG trip to Shaq's Fun House, including two VIP tickets and $1,000 spending cash, plus a BIG cash prize of $20K and a meet and greet with Shaq.
• Lucky Charms Pot of Gold: A cauldron complete with two 1 oz gold bars along with VIP tickets and a trip for two to Shaq's Fun House.
• Cinnamon Toast Crunch Cinnafan Cave: A fully decked-out, Cinnadusted fan cave for the ultimate game day setup and tickets to Shaq's Fun House.
• Reese's Puffs VIP Pass: A "Very Important Puff" experience to Shaq's Fun House plus $1,500 spending cash and a ride in style to one of the most talked-about parties of football's biggest game, along with a custom Reese's Puffs turntable and sound system.
• Honey Nut Cheerios "Bowl" Hot Tub: A BIG Honey Nut Cheerios bowl-inspired hot tub paired with Cheerios-themed lawn chairs, plus tickets to Shaq's Fun House.

Fans who act fast can score even more — early entrants will unlock access to limited-edition brand-inspired merch, available while supplies last.

Hitting shelves this August, shoppers can also find a lineup of Fandemonium Faves including limited-edition boxes of Cinnamon Toast Crunch, Lucky Charms, Reese's Puffs and Honey Nut Cheerios featuring custom tattoos inspired by each cereal so fans can show off their spirit. Plus, when shoppers spend $25 on select General Mills products, they can receive $10 back* by uploading their receipt at ScoreWithGeneralMills.com.

"Our cereal fans bring incredible passion and personality to the brands they love, and we believe we have some of the best fans out there," said Megan Brooks, Business Unit Director for Family Favorite Cereals at General Mills. "With Shaq bringing his larger-than-life energy to the Biggest Fan Contest, we wanted to create a fun way for people to join in, show their love for their favorite cereals and compete for some seriously unforgettable prizes."

Through December 31, 2026, fans can visit BiggestFanContest.com to enter for a chance to win. The top 100 highest-scoring entries will be evaluated by cereal content creator Ami Moyal, known online as @cereallife and recognized for his love of cereal culture and fandom. From there, Shaq will select the grand prize winner, who will be announced on National Cereal Day, March 7, 2027.

Beginning Monday, September 1, 2026, fans can see Shaq alongside a surprise lineup of cereal superfans in a new ad spot rolling out across TV, streaming and social platforms nationwide.

records.title: Black Diamond
records.description:
In a category where "stuffed crust" has become a commodity defined by mystery-brand cheese, Topper’s Pizza decided to lean into the power of a household name. By partnering with Black Diamond Cheestrings, Topper’s transformed a standard menu item into a premium differentiator, leveraging the instant trust and iconic "pull" of a Canadian favorite.
The campaign takes "Black Diamond" literally, following a spokesperson as he navigates a treacherous run with a delicious slice in hand. It’s a high-octane, humorous nod to the fact that while competitors are content with the status quo, Topper’s is willing to go to the extreme to deliver quality.

records.title: Blueberries. GO BIG
records.description: With July known as National Blueberry Month, the U.S. Highbush Blueberry Council (USHBC) is debuting a new marketing platform designed to grow consumer demand and drive more households to enjoy blueberries every day.  Working with SCC (Schafer Condon Carter), the independent agency that was named USHBC’s agency partner last year, the Blueberry Council has developed a new rallying cry:  “Blueberries Go Big.” And it is debuting the platform this month via a multimedia campaign. The campaign includes video, social, search, influencer and more. There will also be a TikTok Top View takeover. The advertising demonstrates blueberries snackability in a variety of situations, from recreational sports to workout recovery.

records.title: Break Up With Your Debt
records.description:
Break Up With Your Debt is a campaign from Farber Debt Solutions that looks at debt the way many people actually experience it. Like a bad relationship.

For people living with serious debt, it is always there. It takes up space in your home, keeps you awake at night, and follows you into moments that should feel normal or enjoyable. Over time, that presence gets normalized, even when it is draining, toxic and unhealthy.

The campaign brings that feeling to life by personifying debt as an intrusive, inconsiderate partner who shows up uninvited in everyday moments. Debt sits beside you while you are trying to get things done, steals your sleep, and takes more than it gives. The behaviour is familiar, uncomfortable, and intentional.

By framing debt as a relationship people can leave, Break Up With Your Debt shifts the conversation away from shame and toward agency. Farber is positioned as the partner that helps people make that break and move forward.

records.title: Breathe Easy
records.description:
Cat’s PrideⓇ, the cat litter brand from Oil-Dri Corporation of America (NYSE: ODC), is debuting a fresh new campaign with full-service ad agency partner Two by Four that takes a powerful swing at one of pet ownership’s most awkward realities: litter box care. The Breathe Easy campaign visualizes odor as an oversized cat dominating everyday life, dramatizing the overwhelming presence of both odor and heavy, cumbersome litter, and the instant relief Cat’s Pride’s unique lightweight formula with superior odor control provides.

Shifting away from purely functional messaging, Breathe Easy elevates the brand into emotional storytelling, positioning Cat’s Pride as more than just litter, but as a source of confidence, convenience, and peace of mind. By addressing the “heavy weight” challenges of litter, both the embarrassing odor and the burden of hauling heavy litter, the campaign showcases Cat’s Pride as the lightweight, effective solution that lets cat owners breathe easy.

The creative includes two TV spots, “Groceries” and “Dinner Party,” where giant cats interrupt daily routines until Cat’s Pride’s lightweight litter, which delivers superior instant and long-lasting odor control, “knocks litter care down to size.” The work is supported by digital banners, high-impact digital units, and social activations.

“Cat owners want peace of mind that odor won’t disrupt their home and that litter care won’t feel like a heavy burden,” said Lisa Mak, Vice President of Marketing, Oil-Dri Corporation. “With Breathe Easy, we’re showing that Cat’s Pride delivers superior odor control in a lightweight, easy-to-carry formula so you can focus on enjoying life with your cat.”

“Odor is invisible, but the stress it creates can be overwhelming,” said Adam Von Ohlen, Chief Creative Officer, Two by Four. “By bringing both odor and weight to life as giant cats, we created a fresh, unforgettable way to dramatize Cat’s Pride’s performance and the relief it delivers.”

The campaign marks the first time Cat’s Pride has leaned into a dramatic, metaphor-driven creative approach. By balancing humor and authenticity, Breathe Easy stands out in a crowded, commoditized category where most competitors focus on functional claims.

Cat’s Pride has partnered with Two by Four for three years, and the new work continues the agency’s momentum in creating breakthrough campaigns for challenger brands.

records.title: Bring the Juice
records.description:
Minute Maid has extended its long-running ‘Bring the Juice’ platform to its Zero Sugar range for the first time with a new campaign celebrating the small victories of everyday adult life. Created by WPP Open X, led by Studio X and RSA Films, the work highlights how a little positivity, confidence and a glass of Minute Maid Zero Sugar can transform life’s everyday compromises into moments worth celebrating.

The campaign features three humorous spots inspired by familiar situations, from awkward social encounters to making the most of unexpected downtime. In each film, ‘The Juice’ acts as an encouraging inner voice, helping characters approach everyday challenges with greater confidence and optimism. The campaign launches in both English and Spanish, with comedian and actress Melissa Villaseñor providing the voice of ‘The Juice’ in the Spanish-language versions.

Built around the idea that choosing zero sugar should not mean sacrificing flavour, the campaign reinforces Minute Maid Zero Sugar’s full-flavour positioning while encouraging consumers to find joy in everyday moments. The creative extends onto social media through *Minute-atures*, a series of handcrafted miniature worlds and action-figure storytelling that transforms ordinary wins into larger-than-life adventures, bringing the campaign’s playful personality to digital audiences.
