records.title: Dead Flower Shop
records.description:
As the number of women killed in Ireland continues to rise, one thing is clear:
violence against women cannot end without men's help.

Allianz and Women's Aid wanted to help enable men to become allies in the fight against gender-based violence.

So, as the nation's men entered flower shops to buy flowers for their partners,
we took the opportunity to remind them of the women who were killed by theirs.

The Dead Flower Shop looked like a normal flower shop but, once people entered, they saw an exhibition of dead flowers. Each bouquet was expertly designed and arranged to represent and memorialise an individual woman who had died at the hands of her partner.
A large bouquet of roses was at the centre of the exhibition, a single dead flower representing each of the 274 women killed in Ireland.

We then asked men to become allies and gave them a resource to do just that:
The Ally Action List. A list of positive actions they can take at womensaid.ie/men

records.title: Death Deserves Better - Back For A Moment
records.campaign_title: Death Deserves Better - Back For A Moment
records.description:
The palliative care and bereavement charity Sue Ryder and independent creative agency Impero have launched a deeply moving campaign, Back For A Moment, to introduce a powerful new brand platform, ‘Death Deserves Better’. 
The campaign takes an unflinching look at how society handles death and grief, seeking to inspire a cultural shift in the way we talk about life’s most inevitable event.

Breaking the Silence Around Death and Grief
Sue Ryder is passionate about creating a social movement that breaks down the barriers to talking about death and dying. Death and grief, however, remain among the last taboos in modern society, and something that many people find difficult to talk about. Too often, people struggle to find the right words to say and, fearing saying the wrong ones, end up saying nothing at all. The result, at its best, is often an empty platitude, and at its worst, is neighbours crossing the street to avoid the discomfort of speaking to someone grieving. The latter is something heard several times during focus groups ahead of developing the campaign. 
Awkwardness around the topic intensifies the suffering of those facing death or grief. It can leave them feeling scared, unseen, and alone. The new campaign from Sue Ryder and Impero aims to change that by sparking meaningful conversations and encouraging society to give death—and those affected by it—the respect and support they deserve.
Additionally, the charity will reach thousands of grieving people, giving them access to a suite of free support, ranging from an online community for bereaved people, through to online bereavement counselling.
Back For A Moment

The work, which comprises two films, radio and digital content, puts real people at its heart and captures genuine moments of them revisiting digital memories of their loved ones.

In each film, we meet a different person at home, alone, using content on their phones as a means to bring their loved ones back for a moment. 

One film features a woman listening to a heartfelt voice note from her mother  saying that she loves her. She moves around her empty flat while listening to the voicemail over and over.

Another film shows a woman watching a video of her partner playing with their child, as she cries alone on her sofa, with framed photos of her partner visible in the background.

In both films, the names of the people who have died appear on screen, followed by writing stating that 88% of people feel alone in their grief. A voiceover says: “Together, we can make sure that no one faces death or grief alone, because, at Sue Ryder, we believe grief deserves better.”

Finding Comfort in What’s Left Behind
For many who have experienced the death of loved ones, the reminders — no matter how everyday — bring comfort. Whether it’s an old voicemail message, a video, or a short voice note, these everyday digital memories allow people to reconnect, even if just for a fleeting moment. In a society where people generally try to avoid sharing open feelings of grief with others, these digital memories  have become an important form of comfort for those facing grief. 
The campaign highlights how disconnected we can be from each other in these moments of need, underscoring the message that death and grief deserve better.

Shot by the award-winning director duo Tubby Brothers, the campaign is raw, real, and carefully crafted - something that doesn’t shy away from the complexities of grief. Every interaction, every tear, every smile is genuine, offering an unfiltered look at the impact of death and bereavement, and amplifying the message that society can do better in supporting those facing death and grief. The aim was to create something respectful, honest and authentic.

Death Deserves Better
On the launch of the campaign Victoria Kubie, Head of Brand and Marketing at Sue Ryder said: “This campaign marks the start of a long term brand strategy for Sue Ryder to break the taboo of death, and ultimately to help build a society that supports everyone through dying and grief. We’re incredibly grateful to our contributors for sharing such intimate stories and allowing us to see them at their most vulnerable. Through this campaign we are working to ensure no one faces death or grief alone. And by sharing real stories, we hope people watching relate to them, get talking about death and grief with their loved ones and feel inspired to support Sue Ryder.”

“For many, death is a taboo subject , but it’s a part of every one of our lives. The pain of grief is amplified by the silence surrounding it. With this campaign, we want to show that Death and Grief Deserves Better—better conversations, better support, and better understanding," said Emily Winterbourne, Managing Director at Impero. "We’re proud to work with Sue Ryder, a charity that does so much to provide vital care and bereavement support. We want this campaign to inspire change. To nudge society to show up for people in their hardest moments. When you show people in focus groups your idea, and they say “That’s me, I do that. I’ve still got my Dad’s voice, on my landline answering machine” you know you’re onto something powerful.”
The campaign will run across TV, VOD, radio and digital, for a three month period. There will also be a partnership with ITV, in January.

records.title: Deep Connection
records.description:
The influence a father has over his son is once in a lifetime.  

C Spire is kicking off its latest campaign with a heartfelt Super Bowl spot that highlights the power of its nationwide 5G wireless network in the moments that matter most. Developed in partnership with C Spire’s creative agency of record Lewis, the campaign continues to strengthen C Spire’s brand as both authentic and aspirational—one that understands and is inspired by its customers’ lives. The campaign aims to put the technology in the background and really focus on the simple story of a father who will do just about anything to help his son do what he loves. 

The hero spot, entitled “Deep Connection” is rooted in relatable, everyday moments, the spot follows a dad who, with the help of C Spire’s reliable cell network, is preparing to coach his son’s football team for the first time. Whether studying plays or brushing up on the finer details of the game, he’s using his phone to ensure he’s ready to step up—not just as a coach, but as a father.

With a primary goal of reinforcing C Spire’s reputation as a brand that truly connects with its customers, the campaign also highlights the strength, speed, and reliability of its wireless network. It builds upon the company’s “Inspired by You” brand ethos, which has been central to previous campaigns, including the Brand Anthem, iPhone, and Holiday spots.

The campaign goes live regionally February 9th in Mississippi, Tennessee and Alabama across TV, Cable, Social, OTT, Radio, Programmatic, etc.

records.title: Delicious Contradiction
records.description:
Real Good Foods, the brand behind some of the most disruptive better-for-you frozen meals, is unveiling a bold transformation with a new identity, fresh voice and culturally sharp campaign called Delicious Contradiction. In a market where consumers are often forced to choose between taste, nutrition and convenience, Real Good Foods proudly delivers all three — offering indulgent yet nourishing comfort food that’s high in protein, low in carbs, and made with real ingredients that never taste like a compromise.

What started as a challenger brand in the frozen aisle has become a movement, driven by a passionate community and a belief that healthy eating shouldn’t feel like punishment. Now, with a refined strategy and elevated design, Real Good Foods is aiming higher: to lead the conversation in health and wellness, not just react to it. The brand wants to remind consumers that the freezer aisle doesn’t have to be a nutritional wasteland — it can be one of the most exciting parts of a modern wellness journey.

“As a brand, Real Good Foods is flipping the script on wellness branding with Delicious Contradiction — a bold new campaign that embraces the tension between indulgence and nutrition,” said Rikki Ingram, chief marketing officer at Real Good Foods. “While traditional frozen food giants lead with price or convenience, we’re leaning into a different kind of value: empowerment, it’s about the unexpected joy of food that’s both craveable and good for you.”

Real Good Foods is redefining the playbook, not just with bold moves, but with lasting impact. In partnership with Magic Camp, led by Holly Willis, the relaunch goes beyond aesthetics. It’s a statement of intent: to build a brand with meaning, longevity and real cultural relevance. This isn’t just a campaign; it’s a commitment to storytelling that resonates, products that deliver and a platform built to endure.

At the heart of the relaunch is a simple truth: you can have it all. For years, consumers have felt forced to choose between clean eating and delicious eating. Real Good Foods is challenging that false choice — from high-protein chicken nuggets made without seed oils to grain-free meatballs that taste like actual meatballs.

Backed by a loyal fanbase, active online communities and constant collaboration with real consumers, the brand’s growth has always been fueled by connection. This next chapter is no exception. Whether it’s Enhancers, families seeking better options that still taste great — or Performers — high-achievers focused on clean fuel and functional nutrition — Real Good Foods is showing up with real solutions and a voice that feels direct, bold and unapologetically human.

With Delicious Contradiction, Real Good Foods enters this next chapter with clarity, confidence and category-defying energy. And if the early reaction from its community is any indication, this isn’t just a campaign; it’s a cultural shift.

Explore more at realgoodfoods.com, and follow the journey on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube @realgoodfoods.

records.title: Despierta tu Lado Pantera
records.description:
Let’s be honest, kids have only one priority: PLAY.
But even play takes energy. Energy to awaken your Panther Side and keep going. 
Energy to win every “race to the corner.”
Energy to become the GOAT in Fortnite.
Energy to score that goal with the paper ball you kick on your way home.
That’s why Choco Milk is there with you every morning, giving you the boost you need to do what you love most and to unleash your Panther Side.

records.title: Stranger Things Mystery Popcorn
records.description:
Yoki, a Brazilian brand owned by General Mills, has launched a new limited-edition popcorn inspired by the final season of Stranger Things. Available only in Brazil, the product introduces a bold “Upside-Down Coating,” a blue, mystery-flavored seasoning that transforms during preparation and delivers a chilling cooling effect.

Created by DAVID São Paulo, the campaign brings the Stranger Things universe to life through a film set inside Hawkins Lab, where scientists experiment with an otherworldly, blue-coated popcorn. The spot plays with visual parallels between the snack’s texture and the show’s iconic creatures, building suspense around the flavor’s mysterious origins.

“To bring this partnership to life, we leaned into the visual tension and mystery of Stranger Things, translating the show’s atmosphere into a fun, unexpected product experience,” says Marie Julie Gerbauld, CCO at DAVID São Paulo.

The launch includes digital films, OOH and creator collaborations across Brazil. The packaging and seasoning sachet feature easter eggs referencing Hawkins Lab, adding to the immersive fan experience.

“Innovation is key to our leadership in the microwave popcorn category in Brazil,” says Fabiola Menezes, CMO of General Mills Brazil. “This partnership with Stranger Things reinforces our commitment to surprising and delighting consumers with new experiences.”
Yoki remains one of Brazil’s most iconic popcorn brands, known for its quality, variety and continuous product innovation.

records.title: Dinner is the Show
records.description:
Carbone Fine Foods, in partnership with Geletka+, has unveiled a new fully integrated brand campaign designed to translate the iconic restaurant experience into a scalable, at-home lifestyle brand.
Anchored in the platform “Dinner is the Show,” the campaign extends across multiple touchpoints, including a cinematic hero film, modular social and website content spanning pre-, during-, and post-dinner moments, food styling, live experiences, and an immersive digital hub. Together, these elements invite consumers to recreate the Carbone experience in their own homes.
“Carbone has always been about more than food. It's about theater, energy, and experience,” said Chris Wending, EVP at Carbone. “This campaign captures that spirit and makes it accessible. It allows people to bring that same sense of occasion into their own homes in a way that feels authentic to the brand.”
At the center of the campaign is a dynamic website that blends storytelling, recipes, curated playlists, and commerce into a seamless journey, positioning Carbone not simply as a sauce, but as a way to “make every meal an event.”
“This campaign isn’t just about selling sauce, it’s about inspiring people to think more about what dinner can be,” said John Geletka, Founder and ECD at Geletka. “We built a campaign where content, commerce, and experience work together to move Carbone from a product people buy into a brand that moves people.”
Strategically, the campaign is built on orchestration:
The hero film establishes the emotional narrative and brand mythology.
Short-form content across social and web translates that narrative into always-on, usable moments.
The website functions as the conversion layer, where inspiration seamlessly becomes action through recipes, hosting ideas, and product integration.
Rather than a traditional campaign, the initiative represents a modern CPG brand experience—bridging content, commerce, and culture into a unified system designed for today’s consumer.

records.title: Dinner Time
records.description:
JustFoodForDogs has a bone to pick with dog dinners, and they’re getting loud about it in the #1 vet-recommended fresh dog food brand’s first national campaign with full-service agency Giant Spoon. 

Pets deserve better than stale dog food standards. The pioneers in science backed, vet-formulated fresh dog nutrition tapped a dog-loving (and people not-so-loving) human spokesperson to berate on dogs’ behalf the state of fresh food: “fresh” by name, just because it’s stored in the fridge. That’s not good enough for JustFoodForDogs and their menu of real, 100% human grade ingredients. In the campaign, the irate owner may not be home for callers, but he’s always here to stand up for dog diets.
 
The ad will air across Meta and Amazon for CTV & YouTube, with local linear TV spanning news, entertainment and sports content, as well as placements during Olympics broadcasts in Chicago and San Diego.

records.title: Dip Into A World of Flavor
records.campaign_title: Dip Into A World of Flavor
records.description:
Domino’s, the UK's favorite pizza takeaway, has today unveiled ‘Dip Into A World of Flavor’, a playful new campaign created by UK creative agency of record VCCP, promoting its new chicken concept, CHICK ’N’ DIP.

Domino’s is synonymous with takeaway pizza, and CHICK ‘N’ DIP now sits alongside it as part of the brands’ core offer. It features boneless bites, wings, tenders, and nine globally inspired dips. The recent rollout to nearly 1,400 stores aims to showcase the brand’s versatility and reinforce its reputation for delivering high-quality food at an unbeatable speed (a delivery time of 25 minutes on average). CHICK ‘N’ DIP meets the growing consumer demand for chicken and gives customers more reasons to choose Domino’s.

CHICK ’N’ DIP promises to bring big flavor to the night-in experience by offering customers chicken alongside a wealth of dips inspired by tastes from around the world. From the fire of Buffalo Hot Dip to the zest of Mexican Mayo and the richness of Katsu Curry Dip, Domino’s new concept transforms a simple meal into an immersive experience. To capture the bold energy of CHICK ’N’ DIP, Domino’s has introduced a unique cast of characters who represent each dip: a world flavour adventure, delivered.

records.title: Director Erynn Lamont Helms Vibrant New Winter Lifestyle Campaign Produced by Agüita
records.campaign_title: Director Erynn Lamont Helms Vibrant New Winter Lifestyle Campaign Produced by Agüita
records.description:
Production company Agüita has produced the Autumn/Winter 2024 New Winter Lifestyle Campaign for iconic Southern California-based global lifestyle brand UGG®, highlighting the brand’s seasonal offerings in bold, cinematic films and photographs. Directed by Erynn Lamont, and creatively led by AKQA, the spots are playful and magical, brought to life with a diverse cast of characters. Lamont served as both director and DP for the film campaign, bringing her technical expertise to an otherwise complicated shoot. She is known for her highly skilled directorial approach, informed by her background in cinematography. 

The dynamic, colorful hero films convey the UGG® brand’s fashion-forward aesthetic juxtaposed with its signature and unparalleled comfort and durability. The UGG® brand’s New Winter Lifestyle campaign and collection features its beloved heritage icons, reimagined through a fashion lens, and its next chapter of UGGextreme™ fuses high-performance tech with slopes-to-street style. The new winter-ready collection boasts elevated fashion and delivers the unparalleled comfort UGG® is known for. The brand campaign encourages consumers to make winter their runway with a path plowed for passing which quickly and playfully becomes a fashion runway surrounded by the snow-dusted trees. Designed to endure any weather, UGG® invites the viewer to don their winter collection and explore one’s sense of adventure.

Shot on location in Chile, the project was logistically challenging, with all scenes filmed in a remote mountain town over three days. The campaign deliverables encompass two hero films, ten product shorts, 50 stills, and a large volume of social content, all shot with the same talent. Each day had to accommodate the live-action team, the photography team, and the social team, working to maximize optimal lighting and location restrictions. records.title: A Ridiculously Serious Campaign to Make 4/20 a National Holiday
records.campaign_title: A Ridiculously Serious Campaign to Make 4/20 a National Holiday
records.description:
District Cannabis Launches a Ridiculously Serious Campaign to Make 4/20 a National Holiday

Brilliant & Absurd Creative, Serves As High-Profile Branding Platform 

District Cannabis, an irreverently innovative cannabis company operating in Washington, D.C., and Maryland, is launching a bold, tongue-in-cheek campaign complete with a petition on Change.org calling on the White House to finally recognize what millions of Americans already know: 4/20 deserves federal holiday status. 

While the campaign begins in the nation’s capital, founder Andras Kirschner sees the mission as much bigger than the DMV. “Weeding the people goes beyond our zip code. We want to make cannabis more accessible, more accepted, and more celebrated nationwide,” said Andras.

Partnering with Nick Cade’s Ugly Agency, the feisty, independent creative shop, the campaign is built out from the petition, turning this outrageously funny effort into a literal smokescreen for the brand’s rallying cry: “Weed The People,” transforming a local tagline into a cultural platform designed to travel coast to coast.

The campaign, “Make 420 A National Holiday,” launches April 16 with a :30 spot, print ads, posters, stunts, social media, in-store activations and radio. The core campaign element, the online petition, is a gorgeously realized piece of satire that begins: “Millions of Americans already celebrate 4/20 like a national holiday. We’re simply asking the government to catch up. This country was built on pipe dreams—and that pipe was chock-full of Mary Jane.” 

The hero :30, a mixed-media film in the style of Terry Gilliam’s work for “Monty Python,” plays like a government PSA viewed after eating one too many edibles and blends revisionist History 101 with the political chaos of South Park, reimagining iconic American moments through a cannabis lens. Static images from the video, like a huge pipe being hoisted up to George Washington’s lips on Mount Rushmore, will be featured across the media executions.

“4/20 is the Super Bowl of cannabis culture,” Kirschner said. “The one time of year when consumers, media, lawmakers and brands are all talking about cannabis at the same time. People all over the country celebrate the holiday, yet cannabis still isn’t federally legal. Legalization has moved faster in culture than it has in Washington, but now that the government is finally reconsidering cannabis classification, the timing felt right to ask them to reconsider their holiday calendar too.”

The hero print image, featured at the top of the online petition, is a submarine-sized, hand-rolled joint that sits on the steps of the Capitol building. District Cannabis has promised that, once enough signatures are collected, they will deliver a hard copy of the petition to Congress—rolled into a giant spliff and placed on the steps. The strategy was to mix humor, populist enthusiasm, public participation and a giant joint of bureaucratic proportions that elevates 4/20 into the kind of cultural spectacle the media cannot ignore and the internet was born to spread.

District Cannabis is a family-owned, vertically integrated cannabis company operating in Washington, D.C., and Maryland that is focused on providing high-quality flower and concentrate products at accessible prices. Famous for strains like Gelato Cake and Cherry Chem, they use advanced, AI-controlled, and eco-friendly cultivation technology. Founded in 2015, District Cannabis has a flagship dispensary in the Union Market neighborhood of D.C. and in Hagerstown, MD. The company emphasizes advanced AI-powered cultivation to enhance efficiency and maintain low, competitive pricing. The campaign establishes the brand as an advocate for legalizing marijuana at the federal level and making it accessible to all.

“We decided to meet absurdity with absurdity,” said Nick Cade of Ugly Agency. “If millions of Americans already celebrate 4/20 like a national holiday, why not make it official? We wrapped that effort in satire, civic theater, and stoner logic.” With a straight face, the online petition solicits the input of the White House, winking at the outdated, Prohibition-modeled federal position on cannabis use.

Because the media buy will be aimed at the Washington, D.C., Maryland, Pennsylvania and West Virginia markets, the creative had to navigate strict local advertising and compliance rules that prevented depicting consumption, promoting intoxication, or showing close-up product visuals. The agency worked around those rules by selling an idea instead of a product. Rather than talk strains, show close-ups, or pretend no one knows what weed does, they promoted a petition and a cause. The creative adopted a low-fi, handmade aesthetic. The work avoids problematic words like “marijuana” and “high” and speaks in code, using phrases like “that good good,” “munchies,” and other wink-and-nod shorthand. Every touchpoint treats the campaign with the gravity of a presidential election and the logic of a stoner brainstorm.

The :30-second spot will appear on WMAR Baltimore; a streaming version will appear in regional buys on A&E, ABC, BBC, Barstool Sports, CBS, Comedy Central, CNN, ESPN, FX, MSNBC and YouTube and Vimeo. Online print and OOH will appear on FanDuel Sports Zone, the Outdoor Channel, PBS, Pluto, Vice, Viceland, Yahoo Finance, and in Leafly and High Times magazines.

records.title: Discover Life Outside the Box
records.description:
In a world where speed and convenience often come at the cost of quality and connection, OfferUp is inviting people to rethink how they shop and tap into the possibilities right outside their door.

The “Discover Life Outside the Box” campaign leans into what makes OfferUp unique: the thrill of finding something unexpected, the satisfaction of giving an item a second life, and the personal touch of a real-world handoff. Whether it’s vintage, barely used, or a conversation with a neighbor, OfferUp makes local feel like the better option again.

records.title: Ditch the Inch
records.description:
Dentsu Creative Canada has developed a clever new campaign for Subway Canada that flips convention on its head: ditching inches in favour of the metric system. The campaign introduces a lineup of 15.24 cm Canadian Classics, available for $5.99 each for a limited time.

Subway has long been known for its 6-inch and footlong subs, but this playful reframe replaces imperial with metric, tapping into a very Canadian sense of humour and delivering Subway’s value story with a wink. 

Raj Gupta, Group Creative Director of Denstu Creative Canada, shared, “Canadians have such a well-calibrated sense of humour about ourselves and our neighbours to the south, so the tone of this campaign hit the sweet spot.” 

The integrated “Ditch the Inch” platform was designed to spark conversation, reinforce Subway’s place in Canadian culture, and highlight unbeatable value at a time when consumers are especially value-conscious.

“We found a timely way of reinforcing a distinctly Subway brand ordering experience, while communicating value messaging with a wink,” said Denny Downie, Head of Marketing for Subway Canada.

records.title: DIY by IKEA
records.country: Egypt, Qatar, and United Arab Emirates
records.description:
DIY by IKEA, developed by VML UK, showcases IKEA's affordable product range as ingenious solutions for covering everyday household mishaps and wear and tear. The campaign platform uses a series of striking before-and-after visuals, demonstrating how IKEA's Scandinavian design can transform common household eyesores into stylish features.

The campaign, set to roll out across the UAE, Qatar, Egypt, and Oman in April 2025, presents a fresh perspective on home improvement during a time of rising repair costs. 

The campaign employs a minimalist aesthetic across multiple channels, including film, out-of-home, and print advertisements. In a strategic move, IKEA is also targeting homeowners at key decision-making moments, with pre-roll ads appearing before DIY YouTube videos.

DIY by IKEA represents a paradigm shift in home improvement, offering consumers an alternative to expensive repairs through clever design solutions; ‘the affordable fix’. The campaign reinforces IKEA's commitment to making beautiful, functional designs accessible to everyone while addressing real consumer pain points in today's economic climate.

records.title: Don't Be Sure. Be Insured.
records.description:
When it comes to confidence, Latinos lead the way. Dieste’s latest spot for Progressive Insurance®, Lamps/Don’t Be Sure. Be Insured. taps into that familiar blend of over-the-top certainty that sometimes takes a wrong turn.

Directed by Martin Jalfen, the ad follows two Latina friends driving behind a truck loaded with teetering furniture. “It’s fine …right?” As lamps start to topple, their confidence is suddenly, well, misplaced.

In this campaign, Dieste brings a fresh, culturally rooted perspective to Progressive’s message of providing safety to consumers, with an approach that combines humor and relatability. Through Lamps/Don’t Be Sure. Be Insured. Dieste reinforces Progressive’s goal of security on the road for Hispanic audiences by meeting them on their own terms—showcasing everyday humor, communicating in Spanglish, and featuring a bit of puppetry to add an old-school touch.

Through this spot, Dieste wants to celebrate the Latino spirit while offering a reminder that even the most confident of us could use reliable protection. Dieste’s unique creative choices here reflect a true understanding of the audience, showing that the best way to feel “sure” on the road is to have the right coverage.

records.title: Don’t Take Slow for an Answer
records.campaign_title: Don’t Take Slow for an Answer
records.description:
Following the successful launch and positive business impact of the “Don’t Take Slow for an Answer” campaign and tagline, Optimum is introducing two new spots under the same umbrella. In its latest creative campaign by Saatchi & Saatchi, Optimum is leaning into what consumers want more than anything – speed. In the :30 spots, one focusing on Optimum’s Fiber Internet network and the second on Optimum Mobile, viewers will be immersed into a brand universe where they see familiar faces and stories intertwined from inside the home to the outside world, with each spot telling a unique story that highlights the products’ strengths.

“In the two latest spots, we have leaned into Optimum’s speed and reliability and designed our creative to drive awareness and demand,” said Jason Schragger, chief creative officer at Saatchi & Saatchi. “We’ll see the reliability and speed of Optimum Fiber inside the home then head outside where we see familiar faces and stories experience Optimum Mobile outside the home.”

“Don’t Take Slow for an Answer” was first introduced in the spring and quickly became a fan-favorite. It has been lauded as Best in Category on all measures, according to an industry leading benchmarking tool, driving Optimum Fiber awareness up from 54% to 62%, outperforming Verizon’s celebrity spot. The campaign was also Optimum’s most successful spot in Q2.

“Don’t Take Slow for an Answer” campaign and tagline has played a key role in Optimum’s fiber and mobile growth. Since its launch in Q2 Optimum has seen fiber growth accelerated with a 53% increase in total fiber customers in Q2 2025 compared to Q2 2024 while mobile saw a 42% increase in mobile lines in Q2 2025 compared to Q2 2024.

“The positive results for the ‘Don’t Take Slow For An Answer’ tagline and campaign have played a key role in increasing brand awareness of Optimum and the growth of our fiber and mobile business,” said Kristin Malaspina, chief marketing officer at Optimum. “We’re excited to introduce two new spots that bring Optimum’s speed and reliability to life, all set in seasonal and cultural settings our customers can relate to.” 

The “Don’t Take Slow for an Answer” campaign takes a 360-approach covering TV, OLV, OTT, direct mail, in-store signage, OOH, social, digital, email, radio, search, and DCO. The Optimum Fiber and Mobile spots are now running. Social and digital will run from September 15 to November 9 featuring “Fast Hair”, which showcases Optimum’s speed by blowing back people’s hair when they use Optimum Fiber and Mobile.

records.title: Don’t Take Slow For An Answer
records.campaign_title: Don’t Take Slow For An Answer
records.description:
Optimum Unveils New Campaign Highlighting the Speed and Reliability of its Award-Winning Network

Optimum is debuting its brand-new marketing campaign and tagline, “Don’t Take Slow For An Answer” that highlights the speed of the company’s always on, always working internet and mobile services and how they power our everyday moments. The campaign is built on the company’s award-winning network and services, including Optimum’s 100% Fiber Internet network, and Optimum Mobile. 

The campaign, created by Saatchi & Saatchi, includes two :30 spots, one focusing on Optimum’s Fiber Internet network and the second on Optimum Mobile. The spots tell a beautifully integrated story with Optimum Fiber Internet being set inside the home and mobile out in the world, all within the same universe. Each spot tells a unique story that showcases the product’s strengths while addressing the need for fast and reliable connectivity services. 

“Optimum Fiber Internet and Optimum Mobile provided us with a unique opportunity to create a brand universe where we see familiar faces and stories intertwined across the campaign going from home to the outside world,” said Jason Schragger, chief creative officer, Saatchi & Saatchi. “We have two different spots for Optimum products that seamlessly weave together everyday characters in everyday situations into one world.”

records.title: Donations that give back.
records.description:
Tap4Change, the Australian platform connecting charities, brands and people, is launching its first major digital and social campaign.

And instead of another guilt-heavy fundraising film or polished corporate sponsorship message, one of the first ads features… a koala in a blond wig.

Created for People For Nature and Franck Provost, the campaign reflects Tap4Change’s core idea: giving should feel rewarding too.

The platform lets people donate to charities they care about, with 100% of donations going directly to the charity, while participating brands thank donors with offers, rewards or experiences in return.

But beyond the mechanic, Tap4Change aims to make charitable communication more engaging, more flexible and more connected to real life, giving smaller charities and local businesses the same creative opportunities and visibility as larger organisations.

records.title: Dreaming of DEELING
records.description:
Deel, the rapidly growing all-in-one payroll, HR, and IT services platform has spent the last year ramping up its presence across brand partnerships and category-first crypto integrations. This month it’s debuting a new, 100% AI-generated creative campaign from Superbloom House (SBH).

Called “Dreaming of DEELING,” the campaign expands on the hybrid AI-powered visuals from last year’s “Feeling of Deeling” work, visualizing more expansive, dreamlike worlds where Deel customers are transported to a space where their emotional needs are met. “Dreaming of DEELING” integrated AI from idea to execution, with the only human-developed element being the creative copywriting. This push to a fully-AI generated workflow is an intentional evolution from the brand's first campaign, which used hybrid AI and real actors and real production set design with transportative AI world building.

The concept was taken to new heights thanks to Creative Collective member, Si Parmeggiani (the AI creator behind Neptunian Glitterball, a viral IG followed by creative tastemakers like Darren Aronofsky, James Gunn and Will.i.Am). Si worked with the agency creative team from start to finish, helping not only create a new visual brand identity and virtual world inspired by real world customers, told through a series of 30 second spots, rolling out globally from February into May. The worlds created by Si and produced by SuperBloom will include an entire package of creative assets that the brand can customize and leverage across its lower-funnel executions, giving the campaign continued life far beyond launch.

The campaign includes the launch spot, as well as two other :30 films (coming in March), a host of digital ads, and a series of massive OOH work that will be used to ambush dream locations like SXSW, host cities for the 2026 World Cup, and conferences and key events in Vegas.

For the campaign, SBH tapped Parmiggiani to leverage his deep knowledge of creative technology and expertise in AI. Si acted as not only a technologist and practitioner of AI worlds, but also the Co-Creative Director, leading art direction and design across all creative, including still imagery and video. 

Si was a key member of the creative team, working alongside SuperBloom Creative Director to create the original visual worlds and characters using AI technologies, creating prototypes, alternative realities and vision boards.
Si worked in Krea AI, which serves as a high-velocity command center, bridging the gap between initial ideation and final delivery by integrating leading video models like Runway, Pika, and Luma directly into its real-time workspace. 
This unified pipeline allows Si, supported by an official Krea partnership, to storyboard with Flux-driven precision and upscale assets to 4K resolution without the friction of switching platforms. The result is a streamlined, "all-in-one" workflow that transforms raw concepts into cinematic reality with unprecedented speed and artistic consistency.

Keeping the team tight, the Creative Collective utilizes multi-hyphenate makers, facilitated experimentation, real-time high-fidelity prototyping, and collaboration along the way. It also offered a new experience for the brand team, who served as creative collaborators, not just clients, consulting on brand worlds with visibility into the end product from the very first day of creation and well before the work launched- taking the “big surprise” out of the traditional client pitch backs.

How SBH’s Production Model Works
The project is a prime example of SBH’s unique creative and production model, which pairs brands with specialist creatives (selected specifically for the needs of the client/project) and a lean-team of advertising creatives to work in close collaboration from start to finish. This approach offers brand marketers access to talent they wouldn’t typically find, while also allowing them to work faster, create more flexible outputs from shoots/projects, and to push the boundaries of what working with an agency should look like. 

That process relies on SBH’s Creative Collective (a group of 200+ non-advertising creatives—TV producers, AI experts, choreographers, chefs, etc.) to bring tailored expertise, viewpoints and ideas to brand marketers. Appointing Creative Collective talent embedded with the SBH team flips the traditional creative process on its head, bringing in outside experts for the entire project, rather than handing off scripts/concepts during the production phase when experts have less input and influence on the final project.

records.title: Dreams
records.description:
Cuisinart®, a leading brand in kitchen appliances, is launching its new Dreams brand campaign – a bold, cinematic series designed to connect with a new target audience, younger modern families. Developed in partnership with creative agency Fallon, Dreams builds on last year’s A Work of Cuisinart platform and reflects the brand’s evolution from Joy of Cooking to Joy of Kitchen – highlighting the kitchen’s role as the central gathering place.

“Cuisinart is deepening its connection with modern, young consumers who represent nearly two-thirds of all kitchen product purchases and value high-quality kitchen products that elevate their cooking experience,” said Thales Soares, Vice President of Marketing at Cuisinart. “This new campaign positions Cuisinart as the go-to brand for this influential audience, while showcasing the essence of what the brand stands for: inspiring people to cook great food with the way it looks, the way it cooks, and the joy it creates.”

A Kitchen That Cooks Like a Dream

Debuting across cinema, television, connected TV, digital, social, and retail and backed by the brand’s largest paid media investment ever, Dreams aims to help consumers resolve the tension between the joy they want and the time they have. With 93% of Americans planning to cook at home more this year, consumers are seeking products that balance efficiency, quality, and style. Cuisinart products and the new creative address this with a simple insight: when your kitchen finds its rhythm, day-to-day cooking feels like a dream.

records.title: Dreams Take Flight
records.description: In Bangladesh, a student can win the admission and still lose the seat. Visa files get rejected over bank statements, solvency letters, and timing, so the dream ends at a desk rather than an exam hall. This film puts that stake on screen. Two students watch planes leave Dhaka from a rooftop and imagine the lives waiting on the other side, while the Student File quietly handles the paperwork that decides whether they board. Premiered at the Daily Star and Prime Bank O and A Level Awards, in front of the students living exactly this pressure. Produced end to end as a generative AI film.

records.title: Dunked
records.description:
McDonald's Australia has partnered with Wieden+Kennedy Sydney to launch its ‘Dunked Korean Sticky BBQ’ range, enlisting the Harlem Globetrotters to bring their signature trick-shot flair to the campaign. Built on the fan insight that there’s no such thing as too much sauce, the work positions dunking as the hero behaviour, turning it into a spectacle led by masters of the craft.

The film follows Globetrotters players through a playful “day in the life” as Macca’s employees, blending high-energy basketball stunts with kitchen antics. From clocking in to executing elaborate trick shots, the action culminates in a final dunk on a hoop mounted atop the Golden Arches. The stylised, handheld approach enhances the sense of spontaneity, while reinforcing the campaign’s central idea: that sauce isn’t just an extra, it’s the main event.

Extending beyond film, the campaign rolls out across social, out-of-home and in-store channels, with the Globetrotters teaching fans “The Art of Dunking.” Supporting a broader ‘Peak Chicken’ platform, the work amplifies the new menu range, including McCrispy and McSpicy variants pre-coated in Korean Sticky BBQ sauce, alongside shareable favourites like McNuggets and McWings, positioning the launch as both a product innovation and a cultural moment.

records.title: Easy to Love
records.description:
LUNA Bar, the gluten-free snack bar brand dedicated to helping consumers elevate the moment, today launched its new “Easy to Love” creative campaign, starring longtime brand fan Jessica Alba as its inaugural ambassador.

For years, Jessica Alba has kept one thing constant in her bag and on set: a LUNA bar. Now, the award-nominated actress, bestselling author, entrepreneur, and wellness advocate is officially taking her brand love to the next level with LUNA Bar.

“When the LUNA Brand approached me to become their new Brand Ambassador and help collaborate on their new campaign, it was an easy yes,” said Jessica Alba, actress, entrepreneur, and LUNA Bar Brand Ambassador. “I've loved this bar for years. LUNA Bar reflects what’s important to me: quality ingredients, great taste, and an intentional approach to everyday snacking.” 

“Easy to Love” Campaign Features Brand Ambassador, Jessica Alba 
The new “Easy to Love” campaign highlights how LUNA Bar is simply easy to love with the help of Jessica Alba – a real fan-turned-Brand Ambassador. The collaboration is grounded in authenticity as Alba is a genuine LUNA Bar enthusiast who helped bring the campaign to life from concept to execution, bringing her passion for the brand to champion its “Deliciously Good Agenda” on commitment to great taste and quality ingredients.

Launching across TikTok and Instagram, the “Easy to Love” campaign features a series of short and long form social videos (LEMONZEST, Spokesperson, Texture, and Work) that trace Alba’s journey from a devoted fan to Brand Ambassador. Throughout the creative, Alba highlights what she loves most about LUNA Bar: standout flavors, quality ingredients, and a convenient bar format that fits seamlessly into her everyday routine. 

The multi-platform “Easy to Love” campaign rollout includes organic and paid social across LUNA Bar TikTok and Meta accounts; organic social content on Jessica Alba’s Instagram and TikTok; and display and shopper ads at top national retailers.

The LUNA Brand Enters New Deliciously Good Era
Alba's partnership comes as LUNA Bar undergoes one of its most significant transformations since its debut over two decades ago. The new campaign marks the brand’s first major creative effort in seven years alongside its first new bar innovation, Berry Bars, in six years. Crafted with organic oats and 7-9 grams of plant-based protein, LUNA bars are available in flavors that deliver on consumer demand for taste including LEMONZEST, LEMONZEST + Blueberry, NUTZ OVER CHOCOLATE Flavored, and Chocolatey Dipped Coconut. 

"The debut of our first creative campaign in seven years is the start of a new chapter for the LUNA Brand," said Valerie Van Arkel, Director of Marketing for the LUNA and ZBAR Brands at Mondelēz International. "With LUNA Bar, we‘re focused on delivering bars with delicious flavors and quality ingredients that fit into your daily routine. From our classic LEMONZEST flavor to our new Berry Bars innovation, LUNA Bar is truly easy to love, and we're thrilled to partner with Jessica Alba as we enter a new chapter.”

Flavor Meets Fiber: New LUNA Berry Bars Product Details 
The LUNA Brand recently introduced Berry Bars, the brand’s first bar innovation in nearly six years. Available in Mixed Berry and Strawberry Banana flavors, LUNA Berry Bars offer real fruit, real deliciousness, 7-8 grams of plant-based protein, and are a good source of fiber with 4 grams per bar, answering consumer demand for delicious fiber options. The new Berry Bars join the brand’s iconic lineup, expanding choice while staying true to the LUNA Bar core mission of quality ingredients and great taste.

records.title: Eat Awesome!
records.description:
Blake’s Lotaburger set out to celebrate something bigger than a meal. The campaign recognizes that Blake’s isn’t just where New Mexico eats, it’s where life happens. From everyday routines to unexpected moments, Blake’s shows up as a familiar constant, woven into the rhythms of real life.
Eat Awesome! positions the brand as an ever-present part of those moments, elevating the ordinary by reminding people that when Blake’s is there, the moment is already a little more awesome.

So, we created a series of ads to celebrate the times our customer's enjoy Blake's.

records.title: Eat less meat. Eat less shit.
records.campaign_title: Eat less meat. Eat less shit.
records.description:
The Shit the Meat Industry Doesn’t Want You to Know!
The campaign exposes a disturbing fact most consumers are unaware of: for years, in Israel and around the world, the meat industry has been feeding calves and cows with feces - known as “poultry litter,” a mixture that includes chicken manure and waste from poultry farms. 
The campaign, launched under the slogan “Eat Less Meat. Eat Less Shit.”, includes hundreds of billboards across central Israel, large digital displays, and a series of videos distributed across Animals’ digital platforms and the web. 
Visually, the campaign presents familiar meat dishes - hamburger, sausage, steak and skewers but instead of meat, they are made of feces. The provocative idea aims to deliver a simple, unsettling truth in the most direct way possible:
we are eating animals that are fed with shit.

records.title: Engine X
records.description:
Engine, the all-in-one corporate travel booking and management platform, just launched an all-new campaign for Engine X, their business travel card, and I’m excited to share it with you! For the new project, Engine worked with Noble People, the award-winning independent media agency, which developed the media strategy behind Engine X's multi-market launch. 

The approach was built around one simple idea: Reach business decision-makers in the moments where managing travel and expenses feels most painful, and put Engine X front and center as the solution.

About the Campaign
The campaign runs on two tracks. The first track is all about making Engine X impossible to miss, placing the brand across the Houston, Austin, Sacramento, and Tampa markets via digital billboards, office building displays, commuter routes, airports, and mall screens along escalators and elevators. 

The marquee activation will include choreographed drone shows over Houston and Austin on July 4th weekend, with 15–20 formations per show visible for up to a mile.

The second track is about reaching those same decision-makers where they already are. Noble People is running video ads across finance and business programming on YouTube, CNN, CNBC, Bloomberg, and MSNBC, plus podcast host reads on business and innovation shows on the Vox network. On the digital side, ads are served in real-time to travelers experiencing flight delays and cancellations via FlightAware, to people connecting to airport WiFi through WiConnect, and to managers on LinkedIn and Meta.

The campaign is projected to deliver approximately 315 million standardized impressions with a 90% reach across key markets.

records.title: Enjoy Together
records.description:
Sham Sham carries 40 decades of presence in everyday life. It is a brand woven into local habits, family tables, and daily routines, familiar not through advertising, but through long term trust built over time.

This campaign marked the first step of a new strategic path for the brand. Rather than looking back, it aimed to move forward with clarity, preserving what people already believe in, while preparing the ground for what the brand is becoming.

Through a combination of OOH executions across the city of Shiraz and a VOD campaign, the brand maintained a strong, composed presence. The communication avoided nostalgia, focusing instead on stability, relevance, and a quiet sense of progression.

This was not conceived as a momentary announcement. It was the opening chapter of a longer transformation, one that will continue to reshape Sham Sham’s brand architecture and communication system in the near future.

records.title: Enjoyment Until the Last Bell
records.description:
“Enjoyment Until the Last Bell” is an integrated Back-to-School content campaign created and produced by Feediper for Pemina. The idea was built around two sides of a lunchbox: the care and effort a mother puts into preparing a school snack, and the enjoyment a child feels when opening it at school.

The first film follows a mother from 6 a.m. as she manages the family’s busy morning routine while preparing a varied and appealing snack for her child. Fast-paced editing turns the pressure of the morning into a visual countdown, making visible the care behind every lunchbox. Pemina appears as a practical solution for preparing an appealing school snack in limited time.

The hero film moves to the classroom. When the bell rings, every student rushes out except one boy, who stays behind to enjoy his Pemina lunchbox in secret. His friends soon return and catch him keeping all the good food to himself, turning the familiar joke of eating without sharing into a playful and memorable product moment.

Three carousel sets extend the idea through colorful, top-down lunchbox combinations featuring a range of Pemina products alongside fruit, vegetables, and familiar school-day sides.

Together, the campaign connects the care behind every lunchbox with the joy of eating it, positioning Pemina as an easy, appealing, and enjoyable part of the school routine—delivering “Enjoyment Until the Last Bell.”

Created and produced by Feediper for Pemina.

records.title: Enough
records.description:
The government has recognised violence against women and girls (VAWG) as a national emergency. In the last year alone, one in every eight women was a victim of domestic abuse, sexual assault or stalking, with abuse among teenagers in relationships reaching troubling levels. In response, the Home Office has worked with FCB London and WPP Media’s Wavemaker team on a new phase of its ENOUGH campaign, to drive recognition and challenge abusive behaviours that have become concerningly normalised.
Developed in collaboration with organisations across the VAWG sector, FCB London’s campaign uses a bold creative device to expose the insidious nature of these everyday behaviours to enable young men and boys to recognise that these are forms of abuse.
The snake serves as a metaphor for the abusive behaviours, from monitoring a partner’s movements, isolating them from friends or sending unsolicited images. Its unsettling presence exposes the creeping and harmful nature of these behaviours, mirroring many women and girls’ experiences of abuse.
The films were created in partnership with director Emma Branderhorst and The Corner Shop, using real snakes to heighten the authenticity of the metaphor. Still photography was shot by Sam Barker whose work helped define the campaign’s visual tension and atmosphere.
Owen Lee, Chief Creative Officer, FCB London, said:
“We were deeply concerned when we uncovered how many abusive behaviours had become ‘normal’ and every day for our audience. We needed a powerful visual device to enable young men to recognise these behaviours for what they are and challenge this normalisation. The metaphor of a snake has long been used as a symbol of a dark presence, from the Bible to Harry Potter. Here, rather than trigging defensiveness, it allows young men to see how their own actions could constitute abusive behaviour and understand the harm they cause.” 
Media strategy and planning were led by WPP Media’s Wavemaker team, deploying a multi-channel approach across display, video on demand (VOD), social, digital audio, TV, and OOH to engage 18–34-year-olds in real-world contexts where violence against women and girls is most visible. The activity was anchored around key cultural moments in time-specific contexts, reflecting audience passions – football, festive socialising, and dating – creating an immediate shortcut to recognising and challenging these harmful behaviours. With research indicating a January to February spike in dating, the campaign will deliver tailored placements across dating apps, online dating content, and OOH near nightlife and transport hubs. Media buying was facilitated by Omnigov.
 Minister for Violence Against Women and Girls and Safeguarding, Jess Phillips, said: “Violence against women and girls is a national emergency and every year it ruins millions of lives.
“If we’re going to halve abuse in a decade, we must drive a generational shift in the societal attitudes and behaviours that underpin it. 
"I wear a seat belt and don't drink and drive because of the public health campaigns I saw growing up. 
"The 'Enough' campaign can have the same impact for violence against women and girls. It will help young men understand which behaviours are unacceptable and prompt the wider public recognition that is vital, and long overdue."
Andrea Simon, Director of the End Violence Against Women Coalition (EVAW), said: “We welcome this next phase of the government’s ENOUGH campaign to tackle male violence against women and girls and are pleased to see it expose harmful behaviours that so often fly under the radar.
“The End Violence Against Women Coalition has long campaigned for multi-year public campaigns that aim to shift the societal attitudes and behaviours that underpin male violence against women and girls, because this is key to preventing abuse.
“We’re pleased to see the campaign focus on reaching men and boys to raise awareness about abusive behaviours, because we can’t end violence against women and girls without engaging men and boys.
“Prevention is always better than acting after harm has been done, which is why it must be a long-term commitment and a cornerstone of the government’s plans to halve violence against women.”

Because these behaviours are so widespread and easy to overlook, the campaign calls on the wider public too, encouraging them to stop accepting excuses or euphemisms that downplay harm. It encourages people to name what they see and condemn these behaviours when they see them.
The campaign is a measure in the government’s Violence Against Women and Girls strategy, which is also published today (Thursday 18th December).

records.title: Eulogy
records.description:
AI is making more of our everyday decisions and when people rely on it without thinking twice, the results can be hilariously human. From a politician accidentally reading AI-generated prompts aloud during a legislative speech to professionals sending emails with chatbot instructions still intact, AI mishaps are quickly becoming a familiar part of modern life.

The timing couldn't be more interesting for Snickers, whose Eulogy spot explores a similar cultural truth: as AI becomes part of everyday life, the line between human and machine is getting blurrier, and sometimes hilariously so.

In the film, a eulogist reads AI prompts verbatim during a heartfelt speech, turning a familiar AI mishap into a classic You're Not You When You're Hungry moment.

records.title: Even While ...
records.description:
Kasteel Rouge? A tasty fruit beer, that gets you drunk a little too quickly.. 

BUT! 

A new, bold campaign from the Kasteel Brewery shows that, Kasteel Rouge 0.0% – the new alcohol-free variant of their 8% Alcohol Rouge beer – can be drunk anywhere and by anyone. 

A pioneer in fruit beers sets the alcohol-free tone. After months of brewing and tasting, Kasteel Rouge 0.0% is now a reality. It really tastes just as full-bodied, fruity and surprising as the original- only the alcohol is missing.

Something that not many other brewers – possibly none – have yet managed.

With this promotion, the brewery wants to show that you can indeed enjoy a beer moment, but without promilles.

records.title: Every Moment Gets Better
records.description:
Feediper created and produced this 30-second cinema campaign for FirePower to build brand awareness and position the energy drink as a natural part of the high-energy moments Gen Z share.

The film opens from inside an ice-filled cooler, placing the product at the center of the story from the very first frame. From there, a FirePower can moves through a connected series of consumption occasions: a camping trip, a football watch party at home, a lip-sync moment, a poolside gathering, an outdoor party with a DJ, and finally a cinema screening. A stylized CGI passage through ice and the inner world of the product connects the live-action environments.

Music was conceived as a narrative device rather than simply added in post-production. Feediper wrote and produced an original Persian-language track in a distinctly Gen Z voice, then built the film’s scenes around its lyrics. Product-led match cuts synchronize every throw, spin, placement, and sip with the beat, transforming separate locations into one continuous, high-energy journey while keeping the FirePower can as the visual anchor throughout.

Built around the message “Every moment gets better with FirePower,” the campaign was released in Iran on July 15, 2026. The film ran as a cinema pre-roll before screenings of Estakhr, a major Iranian theatrical release directed by acclaimed filmmaker Soroush Sehat.

The campaign formed part of FirePower’s broader partnership with Estakhr. FirePower served as an official sponsor of the feature, with the product integrated into selected scenes. Running Feediper’s film immediately before the feature extended the brand’s presence from in-film product placement to a dedicated pre-show cinema experience.

records.title: Every Sparkle Tells A Story
records.description:
THE SHOUT GROUP/FCB SHOUT has been appointed as the creative agency for Le Lumiere, the diamond jewellery brand under the Tomei umbrella, following a competitive pitch for its relaunch campaign. Renowned for its precision, quality, and craftsmanship, Le Lumiere is now repositioning itself to appeal to a younger, more emotionally attuned audience as consumer behaviour in the diamond category continues to evolve.

For the relaunch, FCB SHOUT developed the platform Every Sparkle Tells A Story. Moving beyond traditional jewellery advertising that emphasises aesthetics, the campaign imbues each piece with emotional resonance and personal significance. By reframing diamonds as symbols of milestones, memories, and meaningful moments, Le Lumiere seeks to spark renewed interest among modern consumers and strengthen its relevance with a new generation.

records.title: Everything is Clear!
records.description:
In launching Koala’s Crystal Freezer Bags, the objective was clear and straightforward: show people just how clear “clear” can be. The integrated OOH and video campaign put everyday food into bags so transparent they almost disappeared from view.

The crystal-clear aspect of the product was charmingly brought to attention by the concept, and consumers were also brought to think about its other consumer-friendly attributes such as the writable surfaces for simple product labeling and an eco-friendly design that returns safely to nature.

With "Everything’s Clear" line, Koala turned a functional freezer bag into something bigger:a symbol of freshness, simplicity, and responsibility. The campaign made clarity not just a product feature, but a brand promise.

records.title: Everything Soccer
records.description:
For the FIFA World Cup, Soccer.com came to Athletics with an ambition to stand tall and visualize its place in soccer with a striking brand campaign. As longtime customers and brand loyalists, we jumped at the chance to help tell that story.

Soccer.com is the heart and soul of soccer in America, a brand that broke onto the scene a decade before the ’94 World Cup, when soccer was still, for many people, a European import or a “Eurosport” as their catalog was called then. In the more than forty years since, Soccer.com has helped the sport take root here, where it has developed its own uniquely American culture that powers how the game is played and lived. What do you call that all-encompassing culture? Everything Soccer.

Heart and Soul of Soccer
Everything Soccer doesn’t live in the rarefied air of elite professional soccer, it lives where Soccer.com has made a name for itself and become indispensable, at weekend youth tournaments and five-a-side pickup games. While deeper-pocketed global apparel brands vie for supremacy of the top-tier pro game, Soccer.com wanted to cement its legacy on the ground level, where its constant support and involvement have made the biggest difference.

The Color of Everything
Since our campaign speaks to the game’s range and many kinds of fandom, we designed a punchy color palette that can shift across various geographic and team contexts, as well as draw from product photography. The core colors are saturated takes on classic Olympic colors: blue, yellow, black, green, and red. With these, we can speak to most teams and players in the world. For an especially tailored treatment (such as a new product launch on the website), we developed a system to sample color hues from product photography.

The Many Sides of Soccer
Soccer has many sides that extend beyond the game into culture. You have kit collectors who might not even play the game. There are armchair tacticians, weekend warriors, halftime orange-slice providers, youth academy stars, and more. To equip all of these customers, Soccer.com supplies a wide array of different products: cleats and jerseys, but also goals and pinnies and vintage World Cup apparel. To illustrate this range, we developed a kit (no pun intended) of simple copy constructs and a library of headlines that speak to the variety of products available on Soccer.com.

Campaign as Brand World
As a brand innovation studio, we approach campaigns more holistically than a traditional ad agency might. We don’t just create custom assets to run for a limited period of time. We also build the systems and tools to recreate, scale, and build on those assets. For Soccer.com, this means our Everything Soccer campaign extends beyond digital banners and CTV spots to the brand identity, website, and tools that make creating these branded assets more seamless.

records.title: What Having It All Tastes Like
records.campaign_title: What Having It All Tastes Like
records.description:
Consumers are seeking value in food purchases, but are constantly having to compromise.

Rising food prices have outpaced overall inflation rates in the last year and consumers are feeling it, both at the grocery store and at restaurants. Cooking at home may offer a cheaper/healthier option, but can’t stack up to the convenience of dining out. On the other hand, takeout and delivery come with an ever-growing list of fees and charges. Consumers are yearning for a nutritious, delicious, and convenient option that fits their budget, but it feels impossible to find.

INSIGHT
Outdated perceptions have kept consumers from choosing a meal that checks all of their boxes.
Certain brands/products have distorted consumer views of the frozen category, but a second look at Marie Callender’s and Healthy Choice might surprise many. Quality protein, made-from scratch sauces + pastas, and crisp vegetables - all at a fraction of the cost of dining out.

CREATIVE SOLUTION
Having it all can feel like a superpower - and you may want to see how far you can take it.
In our “Waiter” and “Sven” spots, our characters are surprised by how easily Marie Callender’s and Healthy Choice can deliver on everything they want in a meal. Packed with protein and quality ingredients at an affordable price, it almost feels like a cheat code that breaks the rules they’ve come to expect when buying food. This breakthrough sparks their imagination and begs the question - what else could I ask for if I’m getting everything I want in a meal?

“Phone Smack” and “Bag Smack” bring a tighter focus on the affordability angle of Marie Callender’s and Healthy Choice. With a fictional Delivery Spot as the foil, these spots shine a light on the frustration consumers feel with the rise in quantity and dollar amount of delivery fees we’ve unwillingly become accustomed to.

records.title: Experience your day-to-day in Britânia mode
records.campaign_title: Experience your day-to-day in Britânia mode
records.description:
To stand out in a competitive Air Fryer market dominated by celebrity endorsements and technical specs, Britânia shifted the focus to the consumer's reality. Addressing the critical lack of free time in Brazilian routines, the concept "Experience your day-to-day in Britânia mode" repositioned the product from a simple appliance to a lifestyle facilitator.

Instead of celebrities, the 360° campaign featured real people in authentic family moments, humanizing the technology to build a genuine emotional connection. The strategy delivered massive results: sales grew 83% (vs. a 40% goal), market share increased by 4 p.p., and Britânia consolidated its position as the #2 Top of Mind brand in the segment.

records.title: Factura, Chatea y Gana con Roa (Shop, Chat and Win with Roa)
records.campaign_title: Factura, Chatea y Gana con Roa (Shop, Chat and Win with Roa)
records.description:
What could possibly make people talk about rice? A police stop.

We launched the promotion by showing Mustafá, Roa’s character, being fined with the longest ticket people had ever seen. The internet reacted immediately.

Then we clarified:
it wasn’t a fine.
It was a receipt.

That receipt unlocked Shop, Chat and Win with Roa:
buy COP $20,000 in Roa products, chat on WhatsApp, validate your receipt and get money back instantly — with the chance to win Segway scooters.

By turning a fake scandal into a real promotion, we transformed conversation into conversion and made an everyday purchase worth talking about.

records.title: FAKE OOH OF FRIENDSHIP
records.description:
The Friendship Bridge is a Latin American icon of free trade. 
Its construction aimed to strengthen commerce between the 
Paraguayan city of Ciudad del Este and the Brazilian city of 
Foz do Iguaçu.
To promote the arrival of Brazilian Ipanema footwear models
(Summer 2025) in Paraguay, a CGI campaign was launched, 
showcasing their products "walking" across the iconic bridge.

The campaign was complemented by another CGI piece showing 
the models "flying" into the capital city of Paraguay.

These materials were developed by CGPI: cg-pi.site  
A Paraguayan boutique specializing in AI, combining advertising creativity and visual production through the interaction of a range of AI tools.

records.title: Family Stays
records.description:
The new “Family Stays” campaign reintroduces the organization and shows exactly what they do for families around the world: provide accommodations near hospitals, essential resources, and a community of support. 

The spot signifies the importance of the organization’s role in allowing families to stay involved in their child’s care, which ultimately improves health outcomes. Early family stories from the campaign’s rollout have demonstrated the profound impact of families staying together during their child’s medical treatment. 

The new campaign was inspired by letters from Ronald McDonald House families, and each spot is voiced by a Ronald McDonald House family member. 

These ad spots are a raw and authentic way to tell the world the powerful why and how family stays, which will run on broadcast (PSA, donated media), streaming/digital and social across the US and Canada.

records.title: Fan Life
records.description:
Spotify’s Fan Life campaign returns for its third installment, celebrating the passion, rituals, and unforgettable moments that bring fans closer to the artists they love.

This latest campaign shines a spotlight on the rituals that define the live concert experience – the anticipation and traditions leading up to a show, and the shared moments in the crowd that make being part of a fandom so meaningful. Featuring real fans, the imagery and short films capture the energy and emotion of how communities show up for the artists they love.

The campaign celebrates fandoms for A$AP Rocky, Geese, ROSALÍA, Sailorr, Mary J. Blige, and Zara Larsson, bringing to life the distinct ways each express their devotion – from Sailorr fans getting ready together with black teeth and baby bows in their hair, to Zara Larsson fans dancing the night away in true early 2000s maximalism, to A$AP Rocky fans stepping out in pink hair rollers for a nod to the artist’s signature style.

Beginning Monday, 7/27:
Fans will start to see the campaign roll out across paid social, billboards, and wild postings in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Miami, and Atlanta, with additional launches in Canada, Brazil, and Mexico.
Launching now until September, this installment of Fan Life will also spotlight local artist fandoms that resonate with regional audiences around the world, including AYLIVA and Ikkimel in Germany; Carly Rae Jepsen in Canada; João Gomes, Calcinha Preta, and Matuê in Brazil; Chuyin, El Bogueto, and Bratty in Mexico; EsDeeKd in the UK; and PLK, Helena, Jolagreen23, and Theodora in France. 

At its core, Fan Life celebrates Spotify’s role as the place where fans discover, connect with, and celebrate the artists and communities that shape their lives.

Featuring real fans, the imagery and short films capture the energy and emotion of how communities show up for the artists they love.

The campaign celebrates fandoms for A$AP Rocky, Geese, ROSALÍA, Sailorr, Mary J. Blige, and Zara Larsson, bringing to life the distinct ways each express their devotion – from Sailorr fans getting ready together with black teeth and baby bows in their hair, to Zara Larsson fans dancing the night away in true early 2000s maximalism, to A$AP Rocky fans stepping out in pink hair rollers for a nod to the artist’s signature style.

Beginning Monday, 7/27:
Fans will start to see the campaign roll out across paid social, billboards, and wild postings in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Miami, and Atlanta, with additional launches in Canada, Brazil, and Mexico.
Launching now until September, this installment of Fan Life will also spotlight local artist fandoms that resonate with regional audiences around the world, including AYLIVA and Ikkimel in Germany; Carly Rae Jepsen in Canada; João Gomes, Calcinha Preta, and Matuê in Brazil; Chuyin, El Bogueto, and Bratty in Mexico; EsDeeKd in the UK; and PLK, Helena, Jolagreen23, and Theodora in France. 

At its core, Fan Life celebrates Spotify’s role as the place where fans discover, connect with, and celebrate the artists and communities that shape their lives.

records.title: Fantasy football has never been more cutthroat.
records.campaign_title: Fantasy football has never been more cutthroat.
records.description:
Today, Yahoo Sports is announcing the launch of Yahoo Fantasy guillotine leagues in collaboration with Liquid Death, a killer fantasy football game where fans compete for survival every week. 

In a fantasy guillotine league, the lowest scoring team each week is eliminated.
This means fans are always competing against the lowest scoring team – and the Liquid Death x Yahoo Fantasy guillotine leagues experience reflects this. The match-up screen changes dynamically throughout the week, always pitting a fan against the team in the league with the lowest projected points. The match-up screen also features a survival meter, ensuring fans know what their chances of survival are at any given moment.

When a team is eliminated, its players hit the waiver wire. Surviving teams can then bid to claim these players to bolster their rosters.
Elimination continues until one team is left standing. 
This marks the first time fantasy guillotine leagues are formally available on Yahoo Fantasy. However, fans have been manually running these leagues on Yahoo Fantasy for several years. This required commissioners to customize their league settings, manually remove players from eliminated teams, and lock those teams from making roster moves. Now, the game is fully set up for fans – no customization or manual operation necessary. 
The game brings together the best-in-class Yahoo Fantasy football experience with several hilarious Liquid Death twists.

The game’s logo features a Liquid Death-designed head. Fans can customize their fantasy team avatars with the head, which is available in 18 unique colorways.
Each week, surviving fans can kick the eliminated team’s head through the uprights with a simple flick of the finger (paper football style).
Meanwhile, teams that get the axe are booted out of the stadium and into eternity, with an opportunity to drown their sorrows with Liquid Death along the way. 
Liquid Death branding is embedded in areas such as league invitations, the draft loading screen, and the survival and elimination screens.

records.title: Farmer’s Market Fresh Taste
records.description:
Mateo’s Gourmet, one of the leading brands in the shelf-stable salsa category, is launching a new campaign, “Farmer’s Market Fresh Taste,” created with full-service AOR GSD&M. The new campaign positions the brand as delivering farmers market–quality taste in a jar.

Anchored by the tagline “That Farmer’s Market Fresh Taste,” the campaign brings to life Mateo’s small-batch spirit and never-frozen, slow-simmered approach through a series of playful spots :15 spots as well as :06 cutdowns for social.

In the :15 hero spot “Watch Party,” two fans enjoying a backyard game are interrupted by a larger-than-life farmer who crashes in with fresh vegetables to vouch for the salsa’s farmer’s market inspired flavor. He drives home the punchline: Mateo’s Salsa has that fresh, homemade taste, just like you’d find at a farmers market.

In the :15 “Sunbathing,” two women relaxing poolside with chips and Mateo’s Salsa are interrupted by the same larger-than-life farmer, who arrives bearing an oversized platter of fresh vegetables to underscore the salsa’s farmer’s market fresh taste. As witty banter and sunscreen chatter ensues, he lands the punchline: Mateo’s has that fresh homemade taste, just like you’d find at a farmer’s market.

Designed to reinforce Mateo’s challenger positioning in the shelf-stable category, the work highlights the brand’s blend of fresh taste and high quality with everyday accessibility. The campaign will run across OLV, CTV, social, and various retail media networks. “Farmer’s Market Fresh Taste” marks GSD&M’s second campaign for Mateo’s since being named AOR in 2024.

“We really leaned into the farmer and the fresh mentality when creating this new work. Mainly so this brand could stand out in a very crowded category. Look, everyone says they're fresh, we went with let's say it and show it and do it with a wink and a smile to stand out,” said Wade Alger, Group Creative Director at GSD&M. “I mean if you truly are (and Mateo's is) Farmer's Market Fresh, who better to sell that notion in than THE farmer himself, because hey, it's hard to argue freshness with the guy who harvests what goes into the salsa right?" 

“At the heart of Mateo’s is a commitment to doing things the right way, with slow-simmered, never frozen ingredients, and never cutting corners. This campaign brings that philosophy to life by dramatizing what makes our salsa different: it tastes like it came straight from the farmer’s market,” said Alina Allen, Marketing Director, at Mateo’s Salsa.
