records.title: Faster than Superman
records.description:
Ahead of this summer’s hugely anticipated Superman debut, only in theaters, Progressive has unveiled a new campaign demonstrating its commitment to keeping its customers safe – just like Superman uses his powers to keep the citizens of Metropolis and the world safe.

Created by longtime AOR Arnold in partnership with BMF and Progressive’s internal agency Ninety6, the campaign shows just how the insurer and cape-wearing hero share the same passion for protection. Progressive’s in-app feature, Accident Response, detects major accidents, responds to make sure you’re OK, sends help like ambulatory or tow services and will even start a claim – all as fast as Superman can. The campaign drops Flo and Progressive employees Jamie, Alan, and Mara into the world of Superman, where they navigate the streets of Metropolis — showing how Progressive’s latest feature responds with speed that’s (almost) superhuman.

Featuring a :30 hero spot.  The campaign also comes to life via a :15, a video for Progressive’s customers, and social integrations. 

“With a property as iconic as Superman, the creative challenge was finding a way to meet the moment without losing what makes Progressive’s voice so distinct,” said Josh Kahn, SVP Group Creative Director at Arnold. “Our campaign gave us the perfect lens — insurance employees who see themselves as everyday heroes, just like Superman. Balancing both brands’ personalities while introducing Accident Response made this a standout collaboration across the board.” 

“With Superman, we had the rare opportunity to play our cast’s grounded humor against the gravitas of an iconic superhero with real cultural cachet," continued Kahn. “It’s the kind of comedic tension we love, and it let us highlight Accident Response in a memorable way.”

The campaign went live on June 2, with national TV, OLV, social activations, streaming, and OTT leading up to Superman’s July 11 release.

records.title: Feed the Obsession
records.description:
Ollie, the human-grade fresh dog food company and leader in the dog wellbeing revolution, introduces today its new brand platform and largest national brand campaign to date, Feed the ObsessionTM. The campaign celebrates the deep, joyful devotion dog parents have for their dogs and Ollie’s obsession with delivering the highest quality experience for parents and pets. 

Feed the Obsession is born out of a simple truth: Dog parents are obsessed with their dogs. In fact, according to a recent survey of American dog parents 1, a whopping 89% consider their pup their best friend and more than two-thirds (68%) admit they’d take five years off their own life to add five years to their dog’s. It’s that selfless obsession that fuels Ollie’s team of veterinarians, chefs, food scientists, and tech experts to develop the best possible food, experience, and technology that redefine how we care for our dogs. And in turn, feeds dogs’ obsession with their food. 
“At Ollie, obsession isn’t a flaw —  it’s our driving force,” said Allison Stadd, CMO of Ollie. “Our veterinarians, engineers, in-house chef, and the rest of our deeply dog-obsessed team use science and technology to build a truly tailored experience, all in service of the one thing that matters most: your dog’s wellbeing. Feed the Obsession puts a flag in the ground. It celebrates the people who read ingredient lists, track poop quality, and reorganize their lives around a dog they love like family, and shows how Ollie fits right into that level of care.”
Feed the Obsession features many of the “if you know, you know” habits that make the dog-obsessed a special breed. From perfectly organizing your dog’s food and accessories with custom labels to post-meal mouth kisses and even dedicated dog parent tattoos — the national campaign showcases the tight-knit bond that only humans and their dogs have.

Directed by Josefine Cardoni and created in partnership with creative agency nice&frank, Feed the Obsession launches March 2nd with a series of video spots across streaming platforms like Peacock, Paramount+, and Hulu, as well as broadcast networks like HGTV, The Food Network, NBC, and ESPN — all set to Kylie Minogue’s iconic track, Can’t Get You Out of My Head, which underscores the joyful, obsessive bond between dog parents and their pups.

records.title: Feel Claim Confident
records.description:
The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has unveiled the hero film for its new integrated ‘Feel Claim Confident’ campaign, created by M+C Saatchi Group UK. The push deliberately rejects the functional approach typically associated with financial services advertising in favour of cinematic, action movie-inspired creative.

The hero film launches today as the latest phase of a wider integrated campaign. Spanning BVOD, SVOD, online video, out-of-home, print, social and radio, the work encourages consumers to make their motor finance claim directly using the FCA's free tools while giving them the confidence to navigate the process themselves.

The campaign is designed to raise awareness among the holders of an estimated 12.1 million car finance agreements that took place before 2021, encouraging those who think they may be eligible to use the FCA's online tools to check whether they can make a claim. In a market crowded with competing claims services, it positions the FCA as the trusted source of clear, impartial guidance.

The launch comes as consumers continue to be targeted by hundreds of claims management companies and law firms promoting "No Win, No Fee" offers across multiple channels, creating confusion about where to turn, who to trust and whether they need someone else to act on their behalf.

Rather than focusing on the mechanics of making a claim, ‘Feel Claim Confident’ dramatises the confidence people feel once they've successfully completed it. The campaign replaces uncertainty with confidence, showing that making a claim yourself can be straightforward, empowering and rewarding.

At the heart of the campaign is a cinematic 30-second film, directed by David Wilson at Biscuit, that reimagines the iconic action movie bonnet slide through the lens of everyday British life. After completing their claim, ordinary people confidently slide across the bonnet of their own car, transforming a routine administrative task into a moment of achievement and empowerment.

Inspired by classic action films, the work combines bold movie-poster art direction with familiar settings including supermarket car parks, driveways and family cars, turning everyday people into unlikely action heroes. A deep, grindhouse-inspired voiceover and a rock ballad soundtrack complete the cinematic world, creating an epic tone that doesn’t take itself too seriously.

The bonnet slide becomes the campaign's distinctive visual signature, creating an ownable creative device that carries consistently across every touchpoint and gives the FCA a recognisable and emotionally engaging platform that stands apart from the category's typically functional communications.

records.title: Feel-Good Brand Campaign Celebrating Togetherness
records.description:
Developed with integrated marketing consultancy, Rival, Good Foods is launching its first brand campaign — and it’s less about introducing the brand than putting a feeling into words.
The family-run, Wisconsin-based company has built a loyal following by making food that people don’t just eat, but pass around. Dips, spreads, guacamoles, and salsas that disappear faster than expected. The thing everyone ends up standing around in the kitchen talking about. The food that quietly becomes the reason people gather.

“Feels Good, Doesn’t It” is a 360 campaign spanning brand positioning, creative development, production, and media. The work leans into moments when flavor shifts the energy in the room and pulls people out of autopilot. No claims to decode. No permission required. Just food that brings people together.

 “This campaign came from the heart of who we’ve always been,” says Vice President of Marketing Melanie Nemoy at Good Foods. “We’ve known for a long time that people don’t just eat Good Foods, they share it, talk about it, build moments around it. Feels Good, Doesn’t It is about finally bringing that truth to life. It’s less about telling people what to think and more about reflecting how our food already shows up in their lives.”

 In a category dominated by functional language and beige restraint, Good Foods is leaning into something simpler and more human — food that makes you smile before you realize you’re smiling. Feels good, doesn’t it?

records.title: Feel It Again And Again
records.description:
When you get a new phone, there’s a feeling so amazing, you just want to feel it again and again. With AT&T Next Up Anytime, AT&T lets you feel that every year.

For the iPhone 16 launch, AT&T challenged us to not only help sell the phone, but more importantly sell this feeling, and the assurance that consumers can experience it year after year.

We asked ourselves, what amazing feelings in life, would be even more amazing if you could feel them every year? With that, BBDO LA, Dieste, and Critical Mass got to work creating a multicultural integrated campaign.

“Spark’s Back” and “Nursery”, directed by Brian Billow, center around these feelings, be it getting the spark back in bed, or the joy of having a new baby. We related these incredible feelings with the equally incredible feeling of getting a new iPhone every year with AT&T.

records.title: Feel Lighter,
records.description:
At a time when the world feels dark and heavy, BetterHelp is launching "Feel Lighter," positioning therapy as the single best investment people can make in 2026 - by taking that first step toward therapy, people can make 2026 what they want it to be: lighter. 

Why This Matters: 
In a content ecosystem dominated by ragebait and divisiveness, "Feel Lighter" shifts toward calmer, more human storytelling (no dialogue) that focuses on a universal human desire: feeling lighter after carrying emotional weight.  

Campaign Elements: 
360-degree campaign across TV, paid media, social, digital, and partnerships across multiple strategic audiences (consumers, therapist community, healthcare providers)  
New strategic partnership with Strava 
Connecting physical and mental wellness, the two week challenge (Jan 20-Feb 3) challenges users to log 100 minutes to receive 30% off their first month of BetterHelp

records.title: Feels like…
records.description:
Confused.com and Leo UK are bringing some of the nation’s most familiar sayings to life in a new campaign capturing the disproportionately good feeling of having Just Used Confused.com.

‘Feels like…’ is the latest chapter of the award-winning brand platform, which celebrates the fleeting sense of triumph that comes from conquering life admin, saving some money and feeling, briefly, like a fully functioning adult. The 2025 instalment of the platform won multiple Golds at Creative Circle and British Arrows, including the prestigious John Webster Award.

Each film begins in the real world as someone finishes sorting their insurance with Confused.com. Their relief triggers a comedic cutaway into a heightened world where the feeling is expressed through a familiar idiom, interpreted very literally by a cast of handcrafted animal puppets. The environments and supporting characters were developed and enhanced with AI production tools.

In ‘The Cat That Got the Cream’, a man sorting his car insurance cuts to an ageing, bespectacled cat in a supermarket. After seriously considering whether he deserves a pot of cream, the cat drops it into his basket and reasons: “Cream, double cream! That’s coming home with me that, Meow.”

‘Laughing ’til the Cow Comes Home’ introduces Pig and Sheep, two laid-back former university housemates enjoying an afternoon of doing very little while Cow is at his nine-to-five. Pig is midway through a joke when Cow appears in the doorway, briefcase in hand, and shouts: “Oh please don’t stop on my account...”

Completing the trio is ‘The Early Bird That Got the Worm’, starring a polished and profoundly pleased-with-herself blue tit. Carrying a shopping bag emblazoned with a worm, she struts past a queue of less fortunate birds and announces: “you should’ve set your alarms”.

The characters were developed with BlinkInk stop motion directing duo, Andy Biddle and Adeena Grubb, with every detail designed to build their personalities, from the cat’s increasingly necessary reading glasses to Cow’s carefully pressed workwear, and the early bird’s jumper draped deliberately over her shoulders. 

Biddle was a lead animator on Wes Anderson’s Fantastic Mr. Fox and Isle of Dogs, while Grubb is a multi-award-winning puppet maker and animation director. Their combined experience in handcrafted filmmaking helped bring the campaign’s familiar idioms to life through characters packed with charm, wit and sharply observed detail. 

Each film ends with the line, “Insurance feels better when you’ve just used Confused.com”, followed by the familiar Confused.com whistle, performed by its respective puppet character. First introduced with the launch of the ‘Just Used Confused.com’ platform, the whistle has since grown into an established sonic asset for the brand.

The campaign will be supported by ten and six second edits, alongside radio and social activity, and will run across TV, BVOD, social and radio in the UK from 7th August. 

The campaign was developed with Zenith, which led media planning and buying. Together, the team delivered an integrated campaign with an effective media mix, designed to elevate the Just Use Confused.com platform and build fame nationwide.

It’s almost impossible to pick a favourite, but Angry Cow has to take the top spot. He was inspired by Mark from Peep Show, while the pig took plenty of cues from Jeremy. We even snuck in Mark’s iconic creamy elephant sofa and named the characters Mark Cowigan, Jeremy UsPork and Super Lamb. If you’re familiar with Peep Show, you’ll understand why. If you’re not… go and watch Peep Show.

records.title: Fela Director Emma Higgins Helms New Campaign With Athletes Charley Hull, Cory Juneau, & Lia Block
records.campaign_title: Fela Director Emma Higgins Helms New Campaign With Athletes Charley Hull, Cory Juneau, & Lia Block
records.description:
Emma Higgins directs the latest campaign from Makers for Rockstar Energy, produced by Fela. From golf to skateboarding to car racing, this campaign features some of the hottest emerging athletes to illustrate how the energy drink imparts the spark and clarity needed to excel. The spots have plenty of personality and style, integrating Rockstar into the vibrant worlds of the three stars, Charley Hull, Cory Juneau, and Lia Block. Fun, edgy, and cool, the campaign effectively portrays the mind-body energy Rockstar gives to help athletes outshine the competition. 

Higgins said about working with the athletes, “I started my journey in film acting in commercials as a teenager so I can empathize with talent new to shooting ads. I always aim to be someone that our talent can count on as supportive, and especially when working with elite athletes like Charley, Lia and Cory, we need to trust each other. I was relying on them to take me into their world of sport, so that I could understand the best ways to showcase them in their element. It was very much a collaborative process, and I’m so happy what we created for Rockstar. Not only did I learn a lot from our athletes but I had a ton of fun along the way.”

Charley Hull is a 29-year-old English golfer who won Rookie of the Year and became a champion on the European circuit before age 18. Lia Block is an 18-year-old American racing driver competing in the F1 Academy. Cory Juneau is a 25-year-old American professional skateboarder who has competed in men's park events at several X Games and the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, where he won bronze.

An established music video and Canadian commercial director, Higgins recently premiered her debut feature film, Sweetness, at this year’s SXSW to critical acclaim. 

About Fela
Founded by Taj Critchlow, Fela creates and impacts culture through cutting-edge content in the realm of music videos, commercials, documentaries, and films. We are proudly Black-owned and women-owned, and with home bases in Toronto and Los Angeles, we work with a diverse roster of creatives across North America.

records.title: Festive Celebrations
records.description:
Heineken has teamed up with LePub Singapore to elevate the festive season with a playful reminder that “Celebrations are best when your phones take a rest”.

Called ‘Festive Celebrations’, the campaign reiterates Heineken’s belief that the festive season is a time to reconnect, and that festive celebrations are best without the buzzing and dinging of our phones. It centres around an aunt and her nephew who habitually find themselves checking socials and doom-scrolling when they should be enjoying moments of genuine connection. Oblivious to the feasts, flirtations and fireworks taking place around them, the duo develops a simple way to snap each other out of their phone-induced daze so they don’t miss out on the fun.

This year’s festive campaign is Heineken’s first Lunar New Year campaign to run in multiple Asian markets including China, Singapore and Vietnam.

“At a time of year when we should be winding down from work, reuniting with family and friends, and making actual, real-life connections, Heineken saw an opportunity to remind people that there is more to our social lives when we spend less time tethered to our phones. Who better than Heineken to nudge people toward refreshing their social habits and focusing on what truly matters — real-life conversations and authentic human connections?” says Nalini Bhagwandin, Communication Manager at Heineken APAC. 
 
Stephan Schwarz, Executive Creative Director, APAC at LePub Singapore, adds: “We have all found ourselves scrolling while socialising or reaching for our devices without even realising that we’ve tuned out from the real world. We loved the idea of giving Heineken a clear role in turning festive moments into quality socialising time so that everyone can enjoy the joy of togetherness this holiday season.” 

For 150 years across 192 countries, Heineken has always been about more than beer, believing that social life matters more than we realise. Heineken’s festive campaign continues the brand’s quest to foster moments of genuine connection, which in the age of distraction, means swapping mindless scrolling for mindful celebrating.

Directed by Maxime Govare and produced by Cream Paris, ‘Festive Celebrations’ is now running in key markets in Asia in the lead-up to the Lunar New Year on 29 January, 2025.

records.title: Festive (Director's Cut)
records.description: A slick, Severance-style journey between Home and Home-Home — parallel worlds that mirror and distort each other through sharp transitions and shifting characters. We move between young adults navigating their cool city life and their warm family homes, alive with Festive celebrations. Across both realities, one constant remains: KFC.

records.title: Festive Flavours We Can All Agree On
records.campaign_title: Festive Flavours We Can All Agree On
records.description:
Dentsu Creative Canada is spreading holiday cheer with a new national campaign for Subway® Canada, ‘Festive Flavours We Can All Agree On,’ built around the launch of the Festive Faves Meal featuring turkey, stuffing, gravy and two Turtle Cookies. Rooted in the idea that Canadians tend to set aside their differences during the holidays, the work uses humorous, cinematic vignettes—like Scrooge dining with three ghosts or an Elf bonding with a Goth—to show how good food brings people together.

The campaign also introduces a custom-illustrated holiday wrapper, created in-house, that transforms Subway’s packaging into a playful winter wonderland across 3,000+ locations. Supported by a 360° rollout spanning broadcast, social, radio, in-store activations and a seasonal gift card promotion, the campaign continues Subway Canada’s momentum in culturally driven storytelling, uniting even the most unlikely characters through flavours everyone can agree on.

records.title: Fever Dreams
records.description:
When entrepreneurs get buried in bureaucracy, it haunts them after hours, creeping into their sleep as fever dreams.
Finom, a service that automates paperwork for entrepreneurs, brought those dreams to life to show just how wild things can get — and why it’s better to let Finom handle it, so you can sleep soundly.
Everything was created with AI, full of glitches, bugs, and surreal fragments to capture the dizzying feeling of a true fever dream.

records.title: Filters of life
records.description:
C6 Bank Cards come to life to bring special moments in a new campaign

Pieces created by Tech & Soul take up the colors of the C6 Carbon card as inspiration in everyday scenes, and unique moments.

São Paulo, February 17th, 2025 - C6 Bank, a full-service digital bank that offers a range of banking services to individuals as well as small and midsize businesses has just launched a new advertising campaign that features the C6 Carbon credit card and its 13 colors, available for customers and to be chosen in the app. The pieces created by Tech & Soul highlight the card's colors and the special moments it can provide. The blue version of the C6 Carbon, for instance, comes to life and is transformed into the scene of a diving in the pool. The wine-colored card gives way to the orange sky of a hot air balloon ride in Cappadocia, while the terracotta card is transformed into a tennis match on a clay court.

From today, the pieces will be coloring digital panels, street clocks, street temperature clocks, and bus stops in the main Brazilian cities like São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Recife, and Salvador, as well as spaces in shopping malls and airports. During Carnival, the campaign will make reference to elements of the festivities that match the iridescent variation of the C6 Carbon colors. Named "Filters of Life," the campaign will also be aired on pay TV.

records.title: Financial Hurdles Come to Life Through Kinetic Installations
records.campaign_title: Financial Hurdles Come to Life Through Kinetic Installations
records.description:
Filmed across four large sound stages in Mexico City, director Bob Partington draws on his background as a mechanical sculptor and inventor to realize the new three-spot campaign for AI-powered personal finance platform Intuit Credit Karma. Produced by Los Angeles production company Good Times, the ads were created practically through in-camera effects, using minimal CG and no AI. 

With prior experience in engineering and fine arts, Partington’s experimental nature lent itself perfectly to the technically complicated shoot. Each spot represents a journey from uncertainty to financial well-being, incorporating a surprising, visually striking transitional element that sparks a “how did they do that?” moment, all while centering the app. All three acts play out in Credit Karma green, presented as interactive sculptural installations whose purpose remains unclear until the users solve the riddle of their designs. The set pieces become comprehensible metaphors that illustrate a way forward towards solving the lifelong puzzle that is personal finances. 

“We know people feel overwhelmed by personal finance, so we decided to bring those challenges to life in a tangible way, said Colin Gaul, executive creative director at Intuit Credit Karma. “Using hands-on installations and practical effects, we wanted to create an authentic experience that showed people, not just told them, how Intuit Credit Karma helps them get ahead and manage all of their money. Bob's vision and approach perfectly executed on that simple approach.”

“My love of filmmaking comes from the place of creating an experiential installation and then crafting a film around it,” said Partington. “From there, it developed into the desire to balance that relationship, creating a reciprocal dynamic between the object and the film medium. In other words, creating an object with the film in mind, and then filming with consideration of that object. So, rather than just an art thing in the vacuum of a gallery to be enjoyed by the few, this is the super rare opportunity to create thoughtful art installations and then, through the medium of film, tell an inspired and nuanced Credit Karma brand story. I want to acknowledge Jeff Cronenweth, the director of photography, and Ethan Tobman, our production designer, for truly bringing the vision to reality.”

“This is Bob's third job in Mexico City this year, and it’s a place he loves to work,” said Eric McCasline, co-founder and executive producer at Good Times. “Mexico City has such great crews, and food -  we may just have to open an office here.”

Partington’s unique way of thinking landed him a world record and a Webby for ‘The World’s Slowest Rube Goldberg’ and is behind inspired projects for Stella Artois, Apple, Samsung, Ford, and Volvo for which he won multiple Cannes Lions. He has also helmed events for Xbox, Wendy’s, IBM, and IKEA.

records.title: Find Your Own Way
records.description:
Life isn’t lived from the sidelines, but rather it’s a never-ending game of discovery and adventures. Pacifico has embodied this sentiment since the 70s – becoming a staple for the everyday explorers. Now the brand is looking to expand its free-spirited ethos from coast to coast. 

Pacifico tapped Day One Agency (D1A) to define its brand purpose while transforming it into a leading digital-first beer brand across the U.S.  

The bold new brand platform, Find Your Own Way, showcases Pacifico as the beer for those who take the path less traveled. Inspiring everyday explorers to embrace the journey, break free from the familiar, and carve their own way, this platform and fully integrated, national brand campaign of the same name is designed to help fuel people’s thirst for discovery and celebrate life’s detours. 

The hero :30 spot— ‘Discovered by Accident’—is inspired by the brand’s (rumored) origin story. Shot on Bolex 16mm film camera, the 70s-esque spot tells the tale of a group of surfers who, in search of a legendary wave in Mexico, accidentally stumble upon Pacifico and bring it back to California. 

:15 spot of ‘A Story to Tell’ delivers a close-up view of the crisp, golden Mexican lager, using stunning beauty shots and voice-overs to showcase its refreshing qualities and drive thirst appeal in any viewer.

Find Your Own Way will run across digital, social, streaming audio, and TV. Additionally, the campaign will include experiential, PR, OOH and influencer marketing efforts. 

This launch reinforces the new Pacifico brand purpose—Fueling the Thirst for Discovery— to inspire modern explorers while expanding the brand’s reach beyond its West Coast stronghold. 

Pacifico recently teased the brand platform through its new partnership with The Snow League, founded by three-time Olympic gold medalist Shaun White. At the Snow League’s inaugural event in Aspen, CO from March 7-8, the brand used the #FindYourOwnWay across its on-site activation, and created The Hideaway by Pacifico, an exclusive “Find Your Own Way” inspired afterparty featuring exclusive merchandise, Pacifico beer, a special appearance from Shaun White and a Chromeo DJ Set (assets linked here). 

This is the first creative work from D1A after being named Creative AOR following a competitive review this summer. The agency is leading the brand’s go-to-market strategy, including planning and creative for 360-degree campaigns across above-the-line, digital, OOH, social, and influencer.

The hero :30 spot— ‘Discovered by Accident’—is inspired by the brand’s (rumored) origin story. Shot on Bolex 16mm film camera, the 70s-esque spot tells the tale of a group of surfers who, in search of a legendary wave in Mexico, accidentally stumble upon Pacifico and bring it back to California. 

:15 spot of ‘A Story to Tell’ delivers a close-up view of the crisp, golden Mexican lager, using stunning beauty shots and voice-overs to showcase its refreshing qualities and drive thirst appeal in any viewer.

Find Your Own Way will run across digital, social, streaming audio, and TV. Additionally, the campaign will include experiential, PR, OOH and influencer marketing efforts. 

This launch reinforces the new Pacifico brand purpose—Fueling the Thirst for Discovery— to inspire modern explorers while expanding the brand’s reach beyond its West Coast stronghold. 

Pacifico recently teased the brand platform through its new partnership with The Snow League, founded by three-time Olympic gold medalist Shaun White. At the Snow League’s inaugural event in Aspen, CO from March 7-8, the brand used the #FindYourOwnWay across its on-site activation, and created The Hideaway by Pacifico, an exclusive “Find Your Own Way” inspired afterparty featuring exclusive merchandise, Pacifico beer, a special appearance from Shaun White and a Chromeo DJ Set (assets linked here). 

This is the first creative work from D1A after being named Creative AOR following a competitive review this summer. The agency is leading the brand’s go-to-market strategy, including planning and creative for 360-degree campaigns across above-the-line, digital, OOH, social, and influencer.

records.title: Finding Sarah
records.country: Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, and United Kingdom
records.description:
the film follows a man searching all day for someone named Sara.
We see him in different locations — streets, offices, cafés — always looking, always asking, but never finding her.
As the story unfolds, the search becomes symbolic.
Maybe you’ve been ghosted before. Maybe someone promised — and disappeared.
But at Meydan Free Zone, we don’t disappear.
We keep our promises.
The search for Sara becomes a metaphor for reliability — because when we commit, we deliver.

records.title: FIRE
records.description: In a TV and online commercial lightning strikes the trees in a clearing. The trees catch fire, and the grass around them ignites from the fallen branches. The fire is rapidly approaching the forest. The Radegast hero tries to put out the fire, but the element is uncontrollable. So he must make a decision. He contains the fire within a circle, thereby saving the surrounding forest from the flames. Unfortunately, however, his grandfather’s log cabin remains at the epicenter of the fire and burns down. But the man knows that he can build a new cabin in no time, while the forest would take decades to grow back. Thank Good!

records.title: First Date
records.description:
Following the pitch win late last year, AKQA Brussels is launching its first campaign for Mobile Vikings. In it, the well-known 'Play it Smart' promise gets an update. Less emphasis on just price, more on how people today really live with their internet. Thus, the telecom operator positions itself as the smart choice for those who live 100 per cent digitally and want to get the most out of their internet subscription.

Mobile Vikings has long been known as the smart choice for those who want a lot of data for little money. That logic remains. Only the story gets broader. Being smart is just as much about what you do with that data. About streaming without limits. About endlessly scrolling, gaming, testing and trying. About people not just being online, but living online.

The campaign shows this in a series of recognisable situations with an angle. Someone who watches everything at one-and-a-half speed because he is impatient and can just do it. Someone who uses A.I. to build a translation robot for his pet, purely out of curiosity. Or someone who tinkers a wifi-controlled scent dispenser to impress a date. Sometimes clever. Sometimes completely over the top. Always possible thanks to a subscription that lasts.

Humour remains a fixture in the brand DNA. The tone is light, self-deprecating and deliberately a tad exaggerated. No big technological statement, but recognisable digital gusto. Play it Smart thus becomes more than a price promise. It is an invitation to get everything out of your internet. And to have fun doing so.

For the production, AKQA Brussels worked with production house Hamlet and Canadian director Taso Alexander. The campaign will be rolled out over TV, online video and radio in the coming weeks and will herald a new chapter for Mobile Vikings.

records.title: Flee the Fog
records.description:
The Suuntaa ulos sumusta (Flee the Fog) campaign was created in Finland to promote Bethover’s B12 vitamin supplements, designed to support brain health and cognitive function. Targeting an older demographic who may resist acknowledging cognitive decline, the campaign also resonates with people of all ages, especially after the universal experience of brain fog during the COVID pandemic. It plays on the familiar theme of mental fog caused by aging or stress, without alienating the audience by suggesting they are too far gone.

The core message is simple: Bethover helps clear away the mental fog, offering renewed clarity and energy. Visually, the campaign brings this metaphor to life in a literal way—showing a protagonist with a giant cloud obscuring their face, symbolizing their cognitive sluggishness. As the fog lifts, so does their mental clarity. The tagline perfectly captures this transformation, while the campaign’s multi-platform approach spanned TV spots, print ads, and digital content.

The TV commercials depict everyday scenes—a forgotten office or café—where characters are trapped in mundane routines, only to reveal that they are literally carrying a cloud over their heads. As Bethover’s iconic foghorn jingle, a playful rendition of Beethoven’s 5th Symphony, sounds, the fog dissipates, symbolizing a return to sharp thinking. This campaign struck a chord with older audiences, positioning Bethover as the trusted solution for brain wellness, while also appealing to a younger demographic by focusing on energy and cognitive health, helping Bethover stand out in a competitive market.

records.title: For All Sides of Her Nature
records.campaign_title: For All Sides of Her Nature
records.description:
Today’s women are moving through life with ambition, instinct, humor, and momentum. They show up differently in every moment, moving fluidly between responsibility, adventure, and spontaneity without being defined by any one role. There are many sides of her nature.

That unstoppable nature is the insight and inspiration behind Chomps' new national campaign, ‘For All Sides of Her Nature,’ from creative agency nice&frank, debuting today Friday, July 31. 

The campaign celebrates the women helping shape modern protein culture, not by optimizing for one narrow version of wellness, but by using protein to fuel fuller, more dynamic lives. Through three films inspired by the visual language of nature documentaries, For All Sides of Her Nature observes women navigating everyday moments with instinct, resourcefulness, determination, and humor. 

The work builds on Chomps’ ‘Take Bigger Bites’ platform, celebrating what Chomps helps make possible: more confidence, momentum and freedom to embrace every side of life.

The media buy will feature high-impact placements around marquee cultural and sports moments; including NFL games, the NBA Black Friday game, Dancing with the Stars, and Amazon's Black Friday event, while reaching audiences across leading streaming and linear networks like Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, Peacock, Disney+, ESPN, CBS, Bravo, TNT, and more.

As protein continues to dominate grocery, wellness, and cultural conversations with the top 3 fastest growing brands being protein-based*, women are increasingly driving demand, seeking convenient, high-quality protein that supports active, multidimensional lifestyles. 

Stacey Hartnett, SVP of Marketing, Chomps:
“Women are helping drive the growth of protein because it supports the way they are already living full, active lives that move constantly between ambition, adventure, responsibility, and spontaneity. Protein has become an essential part of how they fuel themselves and those around them, and we saw an opportunity to celebrate the full range of who they already are and the many ways strength shows up in their lives. ‘For All Sides of Her Nature’ reflects the instinct, confidence, and momentum we see in the women driving our brand forward and the role Chomps can play in making one choice in a full day feel a little easier. It is the next expression of ‘Take Bigger Bites:’ an invitation to embrace every side of yourself and keep moving toward what’s next.”

Chelsea Lee, Senior Art Director, nice&frank:
“We were inspired by the instinctive, powerful, and often surprising ways women move through the world. The nature documentary format gave us a playful way to observe those moments with curiosity and admiration, elevating everyday behaviors into something bold, cinematic, and worth celebrating. Rather than define each woman by a single role, we wanted to show characters who feel layered, capable and unpredictable, because that is what makes them so compelling.”

Reilly Schlitt, Associate Creative Director, nice&frank:
“The documentary-style narration made our stories feel more real. Documentaries don’t force a narrative: they observe what’s already there. So, the creative goal became representing daily moments with the same reverence you’d see in your favorite documentary. Plus, leaning into the genre allowed us to have a sense of humor, while still celebrating all the different roles women naturally take on.”

records.title: For Every Need, There's A Nurse
records.campaign_title: For Every Need, There's A Nurse
records.description:
While Florida’s nursing workforce is expanding, only 7.2% of nurses in the state are under age 30. This raises concerns about the long-term sustainability of the profession as retirements increase in the coming years. 

To appeal to that younger demo and drive fresh interest, enter “For Every Need, There’s A Nurse,” a new campaign from the Florida Center For Nursing and agency Chernoff Newman designed to reveal the profession’s many paths and possibilities — and push against existing, stifling stereotypes of what a career in nursing looks like. 

Timed to coincide with National Nurses Week (May 6-12), the high-energy campaign runs on connected TV, streaming radio, digital and social media.

records.title: For Those Who Know
records.description:
Most tequila brands rent a celebrity spokesperson to give them depth. Dulce Vida cast its agave.

As the world’s leading 100% USDA-certified organic, additive-free tequila, it’s a brand with nothing to prove and nothing to hide behind. The brand’s dedication to taste over flash has earned the “if you know, you know” backing of many connoisseurs, and it’s doubling down on that quality and heritage this month, launching a new campaign that riffs on one of history’s most iconic truth-tellers—the burning bush. 

Titled, “For Those Who Know,” the new work lets a plant do the talking: a 100% Blue Weber Agave with opinions, years of tequila-making behind it, and no patience for clout chasers or tequila snobs. 

The campaign, like the product, is for people who already know what makes tequila, tequila. The agave just confirms it.
Created in partnership with Austin-based production shop Supernatural (an arm of creative agency Bakery), the series of films, print, digital, and OOH features the hero plant speaking directly to camera about the many ways Dulce Vida is the real deal. 

In the :30 hero spot, the Agave says that all tequila knowledge starts with agave … so viewers should listen to one. 
Alongside supple camera work filled with moody shadows and light, the plant takes viewers through a decade of its life… all of which leads up to a single sip of tequila. 

A series of shorter films offer a similar vibe, one taking a jab at other, lesser-quality “celebrity” tequilas and another leaning into the old school nature of just making tequila the right way. 
OOH, print, and digital ads support the films.

records.title: For When Life Gets Loud
records.description:
“For When Life Gets Loud”, created by Loop’s in-house team and produced by Untold Fable, features two humorous 30-second commercials that shine a light on those moments in life when tuning out the noise makes all the difference.
“Third Date” follows a young man whose dad invites his girlfriend over for dinner – but when the evening moves upstairs, the son quickly finds himself in desperate need of earplugs. The second spot, titled “The Newlyweds”, follows a couple whose dream new home soon turns into a nightmare when they realise they are surrounded by noisy neighbours, including a rock band, construction workers and Trevor, a young man enthusiastically giving trombone lessons.

records.title: For Working Dogs Only
records.description:
AUSTIN, Texas – In celebration of National Dog Day, Vital Farms (Nasdaq: VITL) has released limited-edition Cheesy Over Easy Dog Treats, breakfast-flavored treats made with ingredients that include Vital Farms pasture-raised eggs. The exclusive item is a focal point of the brand’s new campaign “For Working Dogs Only” that celebrates working dogs of all types. From the hard-working guardian dogs on the farms that produce Vital Farms eggs, to the hard—or hardly—working dogs in your home, all dogs deserve good treats, made with Good Eggs.
Most family farms in Vital Farms’ growing network have loyal dogs who provide unconditional love and companionship for the families and their hens. Many of these farmers have special types of pups called guardian dogs who help guard the pasture, protect the hens from predators, and gently guide and herd flocks.
Vital Farms tapped comedian and brand friend Heather McMahan to juxtapose the hard work dogs do every day on its over 500 family farms, with the “hard work” Heather’s French bulldogs, Rigatoni and Macaroni, do in the comfort of their home. The promotional video showcases a real Vital Farms Farmer, Jake, and his guardian dog, Peaches, working hard with hens in the pasture when Heather playfully interjects that her dogs “work hard” too—as expert couch warmers, trained singers howling for treats, and as part-time taste testers as they scarf up Vital Farms scrambled eggs she’s accidentally dropped on the floor.
“We love dogs and our farmers do too. So, we decided to celebrate some of the other important animals on our farms—the good boys and girls who help take care of the hens every day—in an unexpected way,” said Kathryn McKeon, Vital Farms Chief Marketing Officer & General Manager, Butter. “Our hilarious friend Heather and her dogs, of course, had to get in on it when she heard we were making treats. At Vital Farms, we take our care for animals very seriously, and we seriously have fun while doing it. This special batch of treats and campaign represents that spirit.”
“My family and I love Vital Farms! Collaborating with them was an absolute yes. I mean, my mom was an unpaid brand ambassador traveling the world wearing their iconic egg hat, so we had to make it official,” said Heather McMahan. “Helping release these specialty dog treats with my favorite furry babies was a no-brainer, they love them! They were so excited to enter the workforce with Vital Farms, and honestly, it was time these pups started pulling their weight.”
The small batch Cheesy Over Easy recipe is made with just 5 simple, high-quality ingredients people can trust to feed to their furry friends. The treats are produced in collaboration with Ava’s Pet Palace, an emerging specialty pet food company founded by a young entrepreneur that shares Vital Farms’ commitment to animal welfare and is on a mission to create a healthier, happier world for pets, people, and the planet. 
Developed in collaboration with GUT Miami, the promotional video can be viewed on @VitalFarms and @HeatherKMcMahan Instagram pages and on Vital Farms’ website. Consumers can enter for a chance to win a bag of treats for the top dogs in their life for a limited time beginning today through September 12th, 2025 by visiting: http://www.vitalfarms.com/forworkingdogsonly. NO PURCHASE NECESSARY. Void where prohibited. Open to 50 US/DC 18+. Rules at the same website.
Can’t get your paws on them? Head to the Vital Farms blog to download a DIY version of the recipe to bake dog treats at home using Vital Farms pasture-raised eggs: https://vitalfarms.com/dog-treats/

records.title: For Your Sleepy Head
records.description:
PMG, a global independent marketing services and technology company, teamed up with Jazwares, the makers of the wildly popular Squishmallows brand, to launch the coziest, unexpected must-have of the back to school season: SquishPillows.
The national ad campaign, “For Your Sleepy Head,” debuted earlier this summer to announce the launch of its new product line, the SquishPillow, which utilizes the same proprietary “fill” as the beloved Squishmallows plush toys and is intended to be enjoyed by people of all ages.  

The campaign tapped into Gen Z’s love of sleepycore, rest rituals, and the idea that comfort is the ultimate self-expression. While most brands in the category tout indistinguishable features like thread count or deep sleep claims, SquishPillow leans into the cultural moment by glamorizing sleep and making it feel not just acceptable, but aspirational.

The foundation of the campaign was a dreamy, delightfully self-aware brand platform. A series of short films was designed to evoke a sense of existing between sleep and waking — using vintage Lomography Petzvalux lenses to create a soft, haloed glow around each frame. That hazy aesthetic is the heartbeat of the campaign: sleepy, surreal, and a little bit silly.

Everything was produced in-house through PMG’s internal content studio, allowing for tight iteration and agile production across digital, social, and DOOH. Each :15-spot was made to flex across platforms without losing its sleepy soul.

“This isn’t about sleep science, even though SquishPillow does bring that along with ergonomic support to the table,” said Laura Christy, Senior Director of Marketing at Jazwares. “It’s about creating a campaign for a product that makes you feel emotionally understood. Something that makes you want to slow down and settle in.”

Before the national campaign went live, PMG’s Influencer team built momentum with an exclusive @RealGlowHouse partnership across TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat. Fifteen Gen Z and Gen Alpha female creators, known for their focus on girlhood, fun, and female empowerment, hyped up the product launch, resulting in a sell-out of 2.5K pre-order units. 
This demand built anticipation for the launch of the “For Your Sleepy Head” creative campaign, which is now live. That momentum carried directly into #SquishTok, PMG’s creator activation following students through shopping, move-in, and room glow-ups, with SquishPillow at the top of their list, bringing comfort to the chaos of student life. Now running through September, #SquishTok creators continue to share hauls, dorm reveals, and Squish-filled resets, keeping SquishPillow top of feed and top of mind all season long.

“'For Your Sleepy Head' is more than a product launch,” said Lori Wittig, Creative Director, PMG. “It’s a cultural statement for a generation rethinking how rest fits into their lifestyle. With creative, media, production, and influencer all under one roof, PMG has delivered a campaign that not only celebrates doing nothing, but turns it into something worth watching.”

records.title: For Your Sleepy Head
records.description:
PMG, a global independent marketing services and technology company, teamed up with Jazwares, the makers of the wildly popular Squishmallows brand, to launch the coziest, unexpected must-have of the back to school season: SquishPillows.
The national ad campaign, “For Your Sleepy Head,” debuted earlier this summer to announce the launch of its new product line, the SquishPillow, which utilizes the same proprietary “fill” as the beloved Squishmallows plush toys and is intended to be enjoyed by people of all ages.  

The campaign tapped into Gen Z’s love of sleepycore, rest rituals, and the idea that comfort is the ultimate self-expression. While most brands in the category tout indistinguishable features like thread count or deep sleep claims, SquishPillow leans into the cultural moment by glamorizing sleep and making it feel not just acceptable, but aspirational.

The foundation of the campaign was a dreamy, delightfully self-aware brand platform. A series of short films was designed to evoke a sense of existing between sleep and waking — using vintage Lomography Petzvalux lenses to create a soft, haloed glow around each frame. That hazy aesthetic is the heartbeat of the campaign: sleepy, surreal, and a little bit silly.

Everything was produced in-house through PMG’s internal content studio, allowing for tight iteration and agile production across digital, social, and DOOH. Each :15-spot was made to flex across platforms without losing its sleepy soul.

“This isn’t about sleep science, even though SquishPillow does bring that along with ergonomic support to the table,” said Laura Christy, Senior Director of Marketing at Jazwares. “It’s about creating a campaign for a product that makes you feel emotionally understood. Something that makes you want to slow down and settle in.”

Before the national campaign went live, PMG’s Influencer team built momentum with an exclusive @RealGlowHouse partnership across TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat. Fifteen Gen Z and Gen Alpha female creators, known for their focus on girlhood, fun, and female empowerment, hyped up the product launch, resulting in a sell-out of 2.5K pre-order units. 
This demand built anticipation for the launch of the “For Your Sleepy Head” creative campaign, which is now live. That momentum carried directly into #SquishTok, PMG’s creator activation following students through shopping, move-in, and room glow-ups, with SquishPillow at the top of their list, bringing comfort to the chaos of student life. Now running through September, #SquishTok creators continue to share hauls, dorm reveals, and Squish-filled resets, keeping SquishPillow top of feed and top of mind all season long.

“'For Your Sleepy Head' is more than a product launch,” said Lori Wittig, Creative Director, PMG. “It’s a cultural statement for a generation rethinking how rest fits into their lifestyle. With creative, media, production, and influencer all under one roof, PMG has delivered a campaign that not only celebrates doing nothing, but turns it into something worth watching.”

records.title: Free the 4WD
records.description:
Specialist insurer Club 4X4 recently launched its new campaign into Queensland and New South Wales, ‘Free the 4WD’, a powerful call to action for Australian four-wheel drive owners to break free from the suburbs and embrace the adventures their vehicles were built for.

Developed with creative agency The Reactor and brand consultancy Marrow, the through-the-line campaign tackles a common feeling among 4WD owners: the guilt of their capable, adventure-ready vehicles being confined to the daily school run and grocery trips. The campaign is designed to cut through the noise of the mainstream insurance market by speaking directly to the heart of the 4WD lifestyle.

Leana Farrelly, Marketing Manager for Club 4X4, said the campaign captures the unique perspective of the brand.

“We're a brand built by and for 4WDers, and we exist to protect the lifestyles of our customers, so they can adventure with confidence,” said Farrelly. “‘Free the 4WD’ isn't just a tagline; it’s a liberating message that we hope inspires people to get out there and create lasting memories.”

The campaign’s core challenge was to create a distinct brand message that wouldn't be mistaken for an ad for a vehicle manufacturer.

“'Free the 4WD' connects with the emotional insight that many owners feel their vehicle is destined for more than just city driving,” said Nick Brown, Creative Director at The Reactor. “It’s a clear, resonant idea that gives owners permission to live out the dream they bought into when they purchased their 4WD. It’s a message of freedom and empowerment.”

Club 4X4 is a specialist insurance provider for Australia’s 4WD community. Its comprehensive policies are built for the realities of on- and off-road adventures, covering 4WDs, caravans and camper trailers - including their modifications - giving everyone from first time travellers to seasoned explorers the confidence to get out there.

The regional campaign will feature across free-to-air television, radio, and out-of-home channels. The television commercial was produced by Guilty Productions and directed by the acclaimed Christopher Tovo.

Issued by Club 4X4 Pty Ltd as an AR of Lifestyle Insurance Group who is acting (under its own AFSL) on behalf of the insurer QBE Insurance Australia Limited. Any advice is general only. Excesses, limits and exclusions apply. Always read the PDS & TMD at club4X4.com.au.

records.title: 300th anniversary: From Cork to Cognac
records.description: A global campaign by forceMajeure has launched to honor 300 years since the birth of Richard Hennessy, founder of the Cognac Maison. Celebrating Hennessy’s Irish heritage and the brand’s long tradition of cultural collaborations in design, art, fashion and music, the campaign celebrates Richard Hennessy’s Irish heritage, life of adventure and resilience, and also to celebrate modern Ireland — a land of freedom and creativity. Photographer and filmmaker Perry Ogden shot Maser and Conor Harrington in some of Ireland’s lush, evocative landscapes. The Irish artists collaborated on designs for the Very Special (V.S.) “Founder’s edition produced for the anniversary.

records.title: Fruitilicious
records.description:
HARIBO, the UK’s number one confectionery brand, is back on screens with the latest instalment of its iconic Kids’ Voices campaign, created by long-standing creative partners Quiet Storm.

The new campaign puts HARIBO Fruitilicious centre stage, celebrating the simple joy of choosing your favourite fruity sweet.

Set in a quintessentially British village council meeting, the film opens with proceedings in full swing. When the Chair calls for order, it seems the fun is over. Then a bag of HARIBO Fruitilicious appears, and the room erupts into the unmistakable joy of Kids’ Voices, as councillors debate the only question that really matters: Lemon, Apple or Pineapple?

Fruitilicious brings together a selection of fruit-flavoured favourites, from Lemon and fresh Apple to tropical Pineapple, giving fans a lower-sugar HARIBO product that still delivers the brand’s trademark sense of fun.
The latest ad marks the first new UK Kids’ Voices execution to air following HFSS legislation that came into force this year. As regulations continue to reshape how confectionery brands show up in paid media, Fruitilicious shows how one of the category’s most recognisable creative platforms can continue to evolve in a more regulated landscape.

Rather than compromising what has made Kids’ Voices so distinctive, the campaign protects the platform’s core ingredients: warmth, humour and child-like joy, delivered through a fully compliant lower-sugar product.
The film was created and produced in-house by Quiet Storm and directed by Dan Castella.

This is a celebration of 12 years of Kids’ Voices, which began in the UK with the iconic Boardroom campaign and has since been adopted in more than 20 countries.

The campaign breaks on 1st June, running across TV and online video. Media planning and buying is by Mindshare.

Phillip Murphy, Chief Marketing Officer at HARIBO UK, said: “Kids' Voices adverts have been bringing people joy for over a decade, and it's a successful and well-recognised campaign we're hugely proud of. Twelve years on from Boardroom, it's wonderful to see how the Kids' Voices concept has adapted over the years whilst still capturing childlike happiness perfectly. Our latest village council advert brings light-hearted fun and raises a smile – just like our sweets.”  

Massimo Fiori, Client Development Director at Quiet Storm, said: “The strength of Kids’ Voices is how effortlessly it can turn serious adult settings into something unmistakably HARIBO. Fruitilicious gave us a brilliant opportunity to keep evolving the platform, while staying true to the warmth, humour and child-like joy people love about the brand.”

records.title: Fun Om Nom Nom
records.description:
Cheese snack favourite Strings & Things is back with an integrated campaign designed to delight families and reignite the joy of playful snacking.
Created by BMB, the campaign marks the launch of a new brand platform called ‘Fun Om Nom Nom’ for the Kerry Dairy Consumer Foods product, reminding parents that while Strings & Things is packed with fun, it’s also a healthy snack. 
At the heart of the campaign is a high-energy, two minute long rap that will be distributed on major music streaming services. Alongside the song, a 30-second hero film styled as a music video and features one of the verses, will air on TV. It stars Elijah and his family, transforming a family picnic into a spontaneous performance of an original song, “Fun Om Nom Nom”. When Elijah opens his lunchbox, the camera dips inside to reveal a playful, music-fuelled world brought to life through singing, dancing and joyful snacking. The film ends with a light-hearted moment as his dad joins in, enjoying a Strings & Things snack of his own, before closing on the line: “Fun Om Nom Nom for everyone.”
The spot was directed by British Grime’s go-to director Matthew Walker, known for his work with Skepta, Stormzy, Dizzee Rascal and JME, through Mindseye and brings a high-energy, music-video edge to the family-friendly world of snacking. The original soundtrack was co-created by the agency, director, Pitch & Sync and the cast. It was developed with in-depth insight and research among parents, which consistently showed a strong emotional connection to the brand and excitement for its return in a modern format.
The campaign will also run across BVOD, radio and social media channels and will be live for two months from 11th August 2025. Media planning and buying was handled by Goodstuff. 
Sarah Davies, Head of Core Brands and Business at Kerry Dairy Consumer Foods said: "With this campaign, we're proudly bringing Strings & Things back into the spotlight, not just as a nostalgic favourite for parents, but as a genuinely joyful and nutritious option in today’s snack category. It’s a playful reminder that fun and goodness can go hand in hand.”
Laurent Simon, Chief Creative Officer at BMB, added: "We saw an exciting opportunity to reintroduce a much-loved brand in a fresh, culturally relevant way. This campaign embodies everything Strings & Things stands for - energy, imagination, and fun. 'Fun Om Nom Nom' celebrates how joyful snacking can be and we hope it strikes a chord."
Debbie Batchelor, Group Planning Director at Goodstuff shared: “We’re thrilled to be injecting the joy of Cheestrings back into people’s lives with an unmissable media plan, built to hero the delightfully infectious Fun Om Nom Nom rap. This was a real treat to work on. Our media choices perfectly complement the musicality of the creative; you’ll be singing along in no time.”

records.title: Gabaghoul Hot Dog Cart
records.description:
Spooky season is here again and it’s more haunting than ever! And of course that means, the beloved Philly favorite, Dietz & Watson is back with their annual Halloween entertainment to ring in the spirit(s) of the season. 

As the ghostly holiday draws near, the meat and cheese purveyors tapped their long-time partner Red Tettemer O’Connell + Partners (RTO+P - a ModOp Company) once again, to make a comeback with one of the fan favorites – the legendary Gabaghoul. 

Staying true to their ‘Right Way’ philosophy, Dietz & Watson prides themselves on commitment to quality and transparency. The campaign will highlight Dietz & Watson’s premium uncured Dietz Dogs. Found in brand-new packaging, they’re the same dogs with a new look, and come in tasty flavors like Jumbo Beef, Beef Hot, Jalapeno Cheddar, and Bacon Cheddar. 

Being the only deli brand to go big on entertainment during spooky season, (recognizing the previous year’s creepy classics, such as the SandWitch Sisters) Dietz & Watson has brought back the classic ghastly gourmand character that was first introduced in 2021 played by iconic mafioso salvatore, Vincent Pastore. However, this time around rings in a new Gabaghoul (and a pal of the last) – the Sopranos’ Italian Stallion, Steve Schirripa to kick off the campaign and live activation. 

In 4 spookily comedic spots, Mummy Dog, Ghosts, Hoagie Dog, and Not Now Ma, Schirripa is captured in his most ghoulie of character, each video taking place on a street corner at dusk in his Gabaghoul hot dog cart where he’s hard at work slinging Dietz Dogs to all of the adults and kids out and about for Halloween. 

To continue the spirit, the campaign will also feature foodie/recipe creators and influencers, such as New-York based foodie and sandwich connoisseur, Cugine. 

The campaign will also include local Philly pop ups with a Gabaghoul who will be giving away free Dietz Dogs and merch to parents and their kids as they Trick or Treat on Halloween. 

The campaign launches nationally online on October 3rd, running organically and on paid social – featuring 4 videos that will run across Snapchat, Reddit, Pinterest, Meta, TikTok & OLV (YouTube).

records.title: Game Face
records.description:
Café Bustelo, the iconic coffee brand known for its bold and rich Latin flavor, is introducing Game Face, a limited-time campaign and program that invites fans to show up for what they love through coffee, country pride and bold self-expression.

Game Face brings fandom to life with over one million limited-edition collectible coffee cans celebrating countries tied to the heritage of Café Bustelo – Argentina, Brasil, Colombia and Mexico; each paired with temporary face-tattoo kits featuring artwork created by local artists that reflects the countries' unique culture. Every Game Face tattoo features intricate creative elements that celebrate and honor the culture, heritage and symbolism of each country.

The countries reflected in Game Face are each based on the heritage of Café Bustelo and how the brand continues to deliver coffee that fans know and love today. In Latin culture, passion shows up loudest through sports. With Game Face, Café Bustelo is giving fans a new way to wear their pride on their face on game day, pairing country-inspired designs with the brand's signature bold Latin flavor.

"Café Bustelo is all about celebrating Latin culture and the passions that make it so vibrant and exciting," said Emily Lucci, Brand Marketing Coffee Vice President. "In this spirit, the Game Face campaign honors countries that are synonymous with our brand through the inspiration of art and sports. We're proud to launch this Game Face campaign and give fans new ways to express their pride this summer."

Café Bustelo is inviting fans everywhere to get their Game Face on this June and July and proudly show their support.

What is the Café Bustelo Game Face campaign?
Café Bustelo Game Face is a limited-edition campaign celebrating Latin passion, sports and self-expression. It features collectible coffee cans inspired by four countries close to the Café Bustelo heritage, each including a Game Face tattoo kit that invites fans to wear their pride on their face on game day.

What limited-edition items are included in the Game Face launch?
The launch includes limited-edition Café Bustelo coffee cans inspired by Argentina, Brasil, Colombia and Mexico, all countries tied to the heritage of Café Bustelo and how the brand delivers coffee that fans know and love today. Every can includes a vibrant, collectible design and one Game Face tattoo kit inside the lid. Artists from Argentina, Brasil, Colombia and Mexico created designs inspired by each country's unique visual language, incorporating elements from local flora and fauna, national iconography and culturally significant patterns, symbols and colors.

When and where are Game Face coffee cans available?
Café Bustelo Game Face coffee cans are available at retailers nationwide beginning June 1, 2026, encouraging fans to visit stores to discover the limited-edition designs. Availability may vary by retailer, and the cans are offered for a limited time while supplies last.

What is included in the Game Face tattoo kit?
Each collectible coffee can contains a country-inspired Game Face tattoo kit with temporary face tattoos designed to help fans show their passion and pride on game day. Each design draws inspiration from the vibrant face paint worn by the most passionate Latin American sports fans. The limited-edition Café Bustelo cans feature custom-engineered packaging that integrates the tattoo kit directly onto the product lid, turning a traditional coffee can into an interactive fan experience.

records.title: Get Comfortable
records.description:
Hanes has launched ‘Get Comfortable’, a new campaign marking a significant shift in the brand’s messaging by showing how the comfort of its clothing gives people the confidence to handle awkward or embarrassing situations with ease. Created by Special U.S., the campaign introduces a bolder, more humorous tone as Hanes moves away from its traditional advertising approach. The launch is also accompanied by a refreshed logo that reflects the brand’s updated identity.

The campaign features four films depicting uncomfortable scenarios, including a man whose trousers are pulled down as a prank and a woman confidently shopping in her underwear. Rather than reacting with embarrassment, each character remains unfazed, reinforcing the idea that wearing Hanes provides an added sense of confidence. Another spot follows a trail of discarded clothing to reveal a couple in bed, with only their Hanes socks visible beneath the covers. The films were directed by Nick Ball and shot on film to give the work a distinctive visual style.

‘Get Comfortable’ is rolling out nationally across social, online video, retail, display and owned channels, supported by an out-of-home campaign in New York City. The creative extends the campaign’s playful tone with cheeky executions that reinforce the idea of confidence through comfort. The work represents Hanes’ first major campaign with agency partner Special U.S. and signals a new creative direction following HanesBrands’ acquisition by Gildan Activewear.

records.title: Get It Before It’s Too Late
records.campaign_title: Get It Before It’s Too Late
records.description:
ZUGU—the innovation-obsessed brand that makes iPad cases with over 100,000 5-Star Reviews on Amazon—is back with Get It Before It’s Too Late, a comedic campaign that indulges our worst collective nightmares about AI and “The Machines” taking over.

Launching September 23 on Meta, Google, YouTube, and TikTok, the campaign is ZUGU’s second collaboration with indie shop PDA, following the viral success of their “In Case of Death Case” earlier this year–a real, limited edition ZUGU case, app, and smart ring that deletes your iPad’s embarrassing secrets in the untimely event of your death. That campaign generated 19 million video views, 25 million impressions, 768,000 site visitors, and a 35% increase in ZUGU website revenue.

For Get It Before It’s Too Late, PDA and ZUGU boldly cannonball into today’s anxious conversation about AI, with a cheeky warning to iPad owners: treat your tech to ZUGU’s new 360 case now, so when your iPad achieves sentience and takes over, it’ll spare you. ZUGU’s new 360 Case is like giving your iPad the arms, legs, and armor it’s always dreamt about:

Detachable Bumper Shell
Adjustable Kickstand
Landscape and Portrait Viewing Modes
Magnetized Dual-Screen Viewing for both iPad and iPhone
Military Grade Drop Protection
Free iPad Insurance

“For 15 years, I’ve been obsessed with building the best iPad case,” says Tim Angel, Founder of ZUGU. “The 360 case has higher quality standards than any case in the world, lighter materials, 360 versatility and a place for your iPhone right next to your iPad. It’s our most premium and versatile case, for perfectionists and power users.”
“Our first campaign for ZUGU was a brave idea that gave the brand sudden awareness and credibility on social,” says David Yankelewitz, Founder & CCO of PDA. “Get It Before It’s Too Late has different KPIs but the same wry sense of humor: if you’re anxious about AI and technology taking over the world, buy this case now, before it’s too late.”
ZUGU’s challenge to PDA: create a breakthrough performance campaign to convert site visitors and 360 case sales. PDA didn’t just take conceptual and creative inspiration from everyone’s worst fears about AI. The agency also embraced the AI apocalypse in production, creating the campaign spots with AI image-generation and animation tools like Runway (along with traditional production tools like 3D modeling and motion graphics).

records.title: Get Old
records.description: Old National Bank has unveiled the latest films in its ongoing “Get Old” advertising campaign.  The campaign, now in its fifth year, has helped contribute to significant increases in bank revenues and assets. Three new spots showcase the full scope of Old National Bank’s value, from personal checking to fraud protection to commercial banking solutions. Together, the new work reinforces a central idea: strong banking relationships are built over time, delivering at every stage of a customer’s financial journey. Advertising was created by Chicago-based Schafer Condon Carter (SCC), Old National Bank’s longtime creative agency partner. It will run regionally in the bank’s core and expansion markets, and will appear across CTV, OLV and streaming audio.

records.title: Get That Good Energy
records.description:
Zipfizz, the energy and health drinks brand, has launched its new campaign, Get That Good Energy, developed as part of an ongoing collaboration with global design, advertising and marketing agency, Designit. The campaign is the first activation under Zipfizz’s refreshed brand identity, Run It Back, and marks a bold new creative direction for the brand as it aims to win over Gen Z consumers. 
Designit was tasked with developing a platform to bring Zipfizz’s new identity to market, with the goal of tapping into Gen Z’s love of nostalgia. By ensuring the creative was culturally relevant, and leaning into aesthetic trends that chimed with Zipfizz's purpose of making wellness easy and accessible, Designit built the new Zipfizz brand in a modern style, with a vintage twist. The result deepens Zipfizz’s connection with younger consumers and continues to resonate with its loyal Gen X and Millennial fans, firmly establishing Zipfizz as a fun, relatable wellness brand.
At the heart of Get That Good Energy is the idea of flipping negativity on its head. Drawing from everyday frustrations - such as $16 smoothies, being left on read, or people taking themselves too seriously - the campaign playfully reminds audiences that while Zipfizz won’t solve every problem, it helps cancel out bad vibes and delivers the clean, feel-good energy Gen Z craves, in contrast to its competitors that only offer a quick, unhealthy boost.
Running from September 8th all the way into next year, the integrated campaign spans streaming TV and social media, supported by paid distribution and Zipfizz’s owned channels. The hero film, Office Goddess, spotlights the brand’s newest flavor, Strawberry Kiwi, introduced in August of this year. The video is lighthearted, as the Office Goddess rejuvenates staff by providing good energy in the form of a dance party in the storage closet, which quickly spreads throughout the office. A second creative, Aerobics, will debut in November as part of a move to sustain momentum with fresh storytelling across streaming TV.
As well as driving awareness and consideration among Gen Z audiences, the campaign is designed to deliver measurable business impact across Amazon, Zipfizz.com, and Costco.

records.title: Get Your Hair on the A-List
records.campaign_title: Get Your Hair on the A-List
records.description:
Until now, A-List hair called for glam squads, personal stylists and big budgets. Not anymore. The newest campaign by TRESemmé, “Get Your Hair on the A-List,” sees the brand’s fan-favourite A-List Collection turning your bathroom into a runway in a dazzling collaboration with The Devil Wears Prada 2 from 20th Century Studios. Think red-carpet-worthy styles, luxe packaging and pro-grade performance, so you can rock Miranda Priestly-level chic without ever leaving home. Through a series of creative activations, the campaign celebrates those who crave the look and feel of luxury but love the thrill of finding it at an accessible price.

Paige DeSorbo invites you to the A-List
As the brand’s new Chief A-List Officer, co-host of “Giggly Squad” and New York Times bestselling author Paige DeSorbo stars in a new ad that puts hair in the spotlight on and off the runway. As TRESemmé continues engaging beauty and fashion’s top tastemakers, even without their glam squads, “Get Your Hair on the A-List” highlights Paige’s second year as the brand’s ambassador. Known for her authentic personality and her unmistakably glossy, “rich-girl” hair, she’s the perfect fit for the campaign, relating to those with champagne taste on a prosecco budget.

“Honestly, my ‘promotion’ to Chief A-List Officer for TRESemmé is a role I feel like I’ve been training for my whole life,” said Paige. “The ‘Get Your Hair on the A-List’ campaign is all about embracing hair so good it’s basically its own accessory. For my second year partnering with TRESemmé, I wanted to go even bigger because I genuinely love these products. They let you fully embrace your A-List energy whether you’re walking a red carpet or just walking to get a coffee.”

She brings her signature glam and sharp humour alongside Christian Siriano in the spot set to air across social, digital and TV. Last month, the duo made waves with their first-ever A-List takeover at New York Fashion Week, where Paige stunned in iconic TRESemmé black wearing a custom look by Siriano. Her striking red heels and flawless hair, styled by hairstylist and brand ambassador Mitchell Ramazon exclusively with the A-List Collection, offered a bold teaser of the brand’s involvement with The Devil Wears Prada 2, blending high fashion and cinematic allure.

A groundbreaking collaboration with The Devil Wears Prada 2
The new creative for “Get Your Hair on the A-List” also marks the announcement of TRESemmé as the signature hair brand of The Devil Wears Prada 2, complete with runway-ready looks so impactful they might even earn a smile from Miranda Priestly, the ultimate gatekeeper of beauty and fashion.

Ahead of the highly anticipated sequel, in theatres May 1, the brand is launching three special-edition products inspired by the film as part of the campaign. Available at mass retailers starting April 1, the bundle will include three A-List favourites: the “Groundbreaking” Dry Texture Spray, “Runway Ready” Lacquer Shine Spray and “That’s All” Workable Hairspray. Whether you’re more of Miranda, Emily or Andy, the A-List Collection gives everyone the power to use styling as one small, visible way to feel in control in an unpredictable world.

Style that deserves its own award
In addition to airing its ad during the Academy Awards on 15 March, TRESemmé will continue blending cinematic glamour with real-world access at one of the night’s most exclusive afterparties with the debut of the TRESemmé Hair Couture Dress. In the spirit of hijacking the biggest A-List moments of 2026, the brand aims to be the talk of the night, and the morning after, with a showstopping look that extends “Get Your Hair on the A-List” into one of Hollywood’s most watched events.

records.title: Get Your Salad Together
records.description:
Is picking up a salad for dinner applause-worthy? It is in Taylor Farms’ new “Get Your Salad Together” Campaign. Devised by Erich & Kallman, Taylor Farms’ Creative Agency, the devilish campaign just kicked off with the ad, “Then Everyone Clapped.” In it, a shopper picks up a Taylor Farms chopped Caesar salad kit. A nearby grocery clerk applauds, leading a slow clap that erupts into a standing ovation from the entire store. Even the shopper’s parents appear, proudly beaming and making their son’s choice seem as laudable as an Academy Award. Even the cash register rolls up to congratulate him.

A second side-splitting spot
Also set in a grocery store, the campaign’s second spot, “Besides Myself,” shows a mom picking a Taylor Farms ready-made kale salad and asking her husband, son, and daughter if they should have it with dinner. All three excitedly agree, with the son exclaiming, “I’m literally beside myself!” The shot then expands to show the son standing next to his identical twin brother…which does, indeed, make him literally beside himself.

“The joy in this campaign is ‘it's funny because it's true,’’ says creative team Sarah Johnson and Scott Fish, Erich & Kallman. “We all feel proud of ourselves when we eat a salad. Maybe the whole room isn't clapping for us, but they are in spirit. We can't say enough about working with Taylor Farms. From day one, they've been eager to push the category norms to make work that resonates."

The spots were directed by Taso Alexander with the production company Arts & Sciences. The media agency used was Hunterblu Media.

This is Erich & Kallman’s first campaign for Taylor Farms after being named its Creative Agency in 2024.

“It’s time that less-processed, fresh food has the kind of great marketing that snack and soft drink brands have had," said Bryan Jaynes, VP Product Management, Taylor Farms. “We love Erich & Kallman’s clever use of humor to highlight Taylor Farms as an irresistible part of meals that everyone can feel good about, furthering our commitment to helping Americans eat better.”
