records.title: Gimme That Golden
records.description:
After almost 60 years of serving up the best chicken in the business, regional chain Golden Chick has built a solid fan base of loyal guests who are obsessed about their hand breaded Golden Tenders, amazing fried chicken, battered fries and fresh-baked Golden Rolls — just to name a few menu items. We needed to show chicken lovers that we were a better, bolder alternative to the basic chicken they were settling for at the national chains. To stand out in a cluttered category, we needed to tap into the existing fandom, boldly claim our superiority, and show the uninitiated what they were missing in a way that would make a visit to Golden Chick feel like an upgrade.

Leaning into the power of music for memorability and communication, we created a brand anthem that would challenge our audience to step up their chicken game, featuring a rally cry that doubled as an ownable call to action.  GIMME THAT GOLDEN is the demand of full-on chicken fanatics who lock in on chicken so good it makes you want to slap the colonel and kick the bucket.

Built on a track from Grammy-winning producer Tre Nagella — with a percussive vibe and just the right amount of swagger — the campaign makes the experience of going to Golden Chick as craveable as the mouthwatering food. It shouts it out loud that this place knows how to do chicken right.

records.title: Global multi-channel campaign gets to the root of frizz
records.campaign_title: Global multi-channel campaign gets to the root of frizz
records.description:
McCann has unveiled a global integrated campaign for the new Remington® AIRvive™ hair styling collection, turning top hair frustrations into moments of creative expression.

Inspired by global research from Remington, which found that individuals with wavy and curly hair often see frizz as their biggest challenge – and one that’s long been portrayed negatively by the beauty industry - McCann Bristol developed a creative strategy that moves away from the traditional “taming” frizz narrative. 

Rather than promoting the “effortless perfection” narrative that is typical to the category, the campaign highlights the extreme lengths consumers often go to in trying to prevent frizz – from over-styling to using harsh treatments; the fear of frizz keeps them trapped in an endless cycle of “safe” styles. It demonstrates how, with the Remington AIRvive™ styling tools, consumers can achieve their desired looks while working with their hair, not against it.

Kathryn Folan, global brand manager for Remington, said: “The AIRvive™ collection empowers individuals to love styling their hair again, showing that it’s not something to be tamed and controlled, but a feature they can celebrate. Our latest campaign embodies our commitment to celebrating individuality and relatable hair moments with our audience.”

“This campaign challenges outdated industry norms by talking about frizz as a natural and beautiful part of hair styling,” said Jake Pole, deputy creative director at McCann Bristol. “For too long, frizz has been framed negatively, limiting confidence and discouraging experimentation. With this campaign, we wanted to shift the narrative - showing that hair isn’t a problem to solve but a canvas for creativity. By empowering consumers to style their frizz rather than just tame it, we’re inspiring confidence and encouraging self-expression with the AIRvive™ collection.”

Aiming to drive significant interest in the new AIRvive™ collection, the creative positions Remington as the go-to brand for consumers seeking innovative hair styling tools. The campaign is currently being rolled-out across TV, cinema, OOH, digital, and social platforms around the world, including the UK, Germany, France, Spain, Australia, New Zealand, and Mexico.

records.title: Glow
records.description:
Today sees the launch of Three UK’s latest integrated campaign ‘Glow’, created to champion the everyday wins that come with being a Three customer.

The brand campaign brings to life that people experience a real, tangible ‘glow’ when they redeem special offers and rewards, available from Three – including discounted coffee and cinema tickets, plus the option to upgrade to the latest handset anytime during their contract.

Developed by Wonderhood Studios and directed by Marie Shuller, the ad opens at a bus stop, where a mysterious warm light suddenly dazzles everyone. As onlookers shield their eyes in disbelief, we meet Amy, a Three customer, who radiates a captivating glow after redeeming her £1 coffee with her Three+ rewards app. Her luminous presence turns heads wherever she goes, inspiring others to join Three and enjoy the same benefits.

The ad was shot in Walthamstow Village and features a soundtrack which has been exclusively composed for the campaign. The ad also features a teaser cameo of TikTok comedy star and actor Henry Rowley, who will be working with the mobile network on a forthcoming social media campaign.

‘Glow’ premieres on TV today across UK channels and has a multi-channel strategy with a mix of AV, OOH, DOOH and radio, alongside integrating Three’s own channels, including retail stores, social media, customer and internal communications. With each channel amplifying the campaign’s core message - demonstrating the joyous feeling from being a Three customer.

Andrew Foy, Director of New Products and Propositions at Three UK, said: “At Three, we understand that the little things can make a real difference. Whether that’s getting your hands on the hottest gig tickets, upgrading to the latest phone, or simply picking up your favourite coffee for just £1. We’re proud to offer our customers everyday benefits and rewards, creating feel-good moments designed to brighten their day and leave a lasting glow.”

Aidan McClure, CCO at Wonderhood Studios, said: “‘Life Needs a Big Network’ has always been about elevating its customers’ everyday relatable behaviours. This is the next chapter, which captures that slightly smug glowy feeling that Three customers get when they bag yet another deal.”

Media planning for ‘Glow’ has been implemented by Zenith Media, whilst social content was created by Three’s in-house agency Generation and Wonderhood Studios. Generation also delivered the content across Three’s owned channels, including retail, customer and internal communications.

records.title: GLP-1 Gallon by Lord Disick
records.description:
MilkPEP and its agency of record, GALE, are tapping into one of the most talked-about cultural trends of the year -- the rise of GLP-1 use. 

In their latest tongue-in-cheek campaign, the team introduces The GLP-1 Milk Gallon by Lord Disick — a $1,000 limited-edition collectible crafted for discretion, refrigeration, and high-quality protein.

The idea was sparked by an episode of The Kardashians, where Disick was spotted with a GLP-1 pen in his fridge. GALE and MilkPEP took that viral moment and elevated it, turning the iconic milk jug into an object of status and satire, complete with a sculpted matte-white finish, minimalist silhouette, and “Lord Disick” detailing.

A launch video, which you can see here, shows Disick doing what he does best — winking at culture. From driving to golfing to shopping, he’s seen carrying his milk gallon everywhere, ending with the reveal that ten fans can actually buy one for $1,000.

This follows MilkPEP and GALE’s recent Protein Puffer Jacket collaboration with Skylar Diggins, which generated 645M+ impressions in 72 hours and helped cement the brand’s position at the center of the “protein craze.”

records.title: Go Backstage with Katy Perry
records.description:
Bi-coastal production company Honor Society unveils its latest campaign, a bold and energetic spot directed by Melissa Bolton-Klinger, featuring pop icon Katy Perry. The campaign highlights Milka Mmmax's exclusive promotion, offering fans who purchase the candy bar a chance to win a behind-the-scenes experience with Katy Perry during her The Lifetimes Tour.

Designed with the European market in mind and shot on a stage in Los Angeles, the spot brings fans closer to Katy Perry through comedic backstage vignettes. The narrative follows a superfan who gets the rare chance to meet Katy Perry in her green room, where she enjoys a Milka Mmmax bar while the team prepares for the concert. 

Director Melissa Bolton-Klinger collaborated closely with the agency and Katy Perry to bring the concept to life, capturing the excitement of spending time with the star, and how it was filled with unexpected and humorous moments. Reflecting on shoot, she shares:

“Directing Katy Perry for Milka Mmmax with David/Hogarth was one of those rare shoots where everything just clicks. The agency and client were hilarious, collaborative, and totally game—my kind of people. Katy crushed it, the chocolate was flowing, and honestly, still not sure if I was directing a commercial or just living inside a chocolate dream. She’s the global pop star, I’m just a director—but for a minute there, we made a pretty great team.”

The campaign will run across multiple platforms, with various lengths offering different, intriguing moments. From glitter cannons to floral head busts, this spot provides a fun peek into Katy Perry’s world—possibly even hinting at surprises in the upcoming tour.

records.title: Go For It
records.description:
Pizza is more than just food. ​

It's a mood-lifter, a deal-sealer, a peacemaker, and a party-starter. From first dates to final exams, moving day to movie night, there’s something magical about opening a box and seeing that cheesy, saucy perfection. At Panago, we believe in the true power of pizza. It brings people together, saves the night, and turns the ordinary into something unforgettable. ​

records.title: Go from Ayyo to Ohhh!
records.description: Based on a simple yet very Indian middle-class insight, this film captures the exact moment when the fear of a hospital bill outweighs the injury itself. Told entirely through familiar Indian expressions—"aiyyoo," "ohhh," and "ohhoo"—the story unfolds without dialogue, making it instantly relatable. As the father anxiously anticipates the cost of treatment, every reaction builds suspense, immersing the audience in his perspective. The film’s music and treatment reflect his inner turmoil, pulling from the references of his time. Then, the big reveal—insurance covers the bill. "Aiyyoo" seamlessly turns to "ohhh," shifting the narrative from panic to pure relief in a way that’s both entertaining and deeply resonant.

records.title: Go grab the Butterkist
records.description:
KP Snacks brand, Butterkist, settles into its seat in a new campaign which draws the viewer into tense dramatic cinematic moments and – just as dramatically - signs off with its trade-mark humour. The latest “Go grab the Butterkist” campaign, which is created by St Luke’s sees the brand take full ownership of movies, and will appear across VOD and social.

The new campaign uses the strapline: ‘For every movie moment: go grab the Butterkist’; and launches with two films from 17 March, as well as bespoke social content.

‘Romance’ opens at the climactic scene of a period drama when a woman is reunited with the lover she believed to be dead. Suddenly the perspective switches, interrupted by a couple enjoying movie night on the sofa. While the man quietly wipes away a tear, his partner declares triumphantly “I knew he was still alive!” – but they are united in agreement that Butterkist is the perfect companion for any type of film, no matter the genre.

In the second film, ‘Horror’, a man is running through a dark forest scene, chased by a terrifying monster off screen, as we hear its animalistic screams - only for him to come to a sudden stop and desperately hide behind a tree. Much to the consternation of the three flatmates sharing the sofa - and a bag of Butterkist - who reflect on the fact he has stopped.

The campaign also introduces a new travelling brand device – the Butterkist Red Sofa – which connects to the brand’s colours and many people will associate with movie night. The films feature the added dimension of the deep, booming voice of Redd Pepper aka “Mr Movie Trailer Man” as voice-over artist.

Rachael Rayner,Brand Manager at KP Snacks, said: “We know that Butterkist is the nation’s favourite popcorn brand, and we are keen to reinforce the brand's position as the must-have snack for movie nights in with family and friends. What better way to bring this to life than building on classic movie moments and the reactions of those enjoying it from their sofa with Butterkist!”

Richard Denney, Joint Chief Creative Officer at St Luke’s, said: “When it comes to watching a movie at home with friends or family, the nation is full of plot second-guessers and running commentators. And when those memorable movie moments arrive, of course, you have to Go Grab the Butterkist—the nation's favourite popcorn. After all, it's all part of the experience.”

The campaign breaks on 17 March, running until 19 July, and is being rolled out across VOD with 20- and 10-second spots appearing on SKY+, Disney and ITV. Along with the hero films, St Luke’s has created several pieces of highly meme-able content, also associated with movies and Butterkist, which will run on TikTok and Meta.

records.title: Go Mad - Tiempo
records.description: The latest film for Nike Tiempo. The goal for Tiempo was to tell the story of a boot built for the modern playmaker, where agility, movement, and control are everything. Built through experimentation, thermal cameras, VHS textures, mad simulations and one very patient cat.

records.title: Go Mad - Aero-FIT
records.description: The latest work for Nike Aero-FIT shirts for the FIFA World Cup 2026. A journey from heat to ice, designed to bring Nike’s pinnacle cooling technology to life for the SP26 Go Mad immersive experience at Nike HQ.

records.title: Go the Distance
records.description:
Today, Coca-Cola is debuting a new fan-centric 360-degree fall sports marketing campaign showcasing how Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar are helping refresh fans of all kinds, so they can pour their energy into every moment and get back in the game. 

Fan Work Is Thirsty Work: To continue to celebrate the “Best Fans Ever,” Coca-Cola is tackling the mighty thirst of college football fans by bringing the great taste of Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar to campuses across the country this fall.   
Go the Distance: The new fall football TV creative titled, “Go the Distance,” celebrates the passion, energy and commitment of those doing the thirstiest work—away team fans. The TVC spot will run throughout the college football season on ABC, NBC, FOX, FS1, BTN, TNT, ESPN, ESPN2, TNT, TBS, TRUTV and across social and digital platforms. 

THE CAMPAIGN: Additional elements that will run as part of the campaign include:  
On-Pack & In-Stadium: The Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar on-pack promotion will take fans to coca-cola.com/us/en/offerings/fan-work/football where they will have the chance to win prizes including custom merch, gift cards or even an all-expense trip paid to see their favorite team play! Fans can also order Coca-Cola or Coca-Cola Zero Sugar at participating stadium food service stations to receive an exclusive Coca-Cola fall football cup or scratch card for another chance to win prizes.   
Onsite Experiential Activations: To celebrate fans and the most energetic fanbases across the country, the Fan Work is Thirsty Work Tour will visit 53 different partner school campuses throughout the college football season.  

THE CREATIVE: The TVC spot features several of Coca-Cola’s NCAA partner schools, spotlighting the passionate fandom of an away fan’s journey—from the road to their seat—and the refreshing role Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar play along the way.

records.title: Goat Gummies
records.description: Goat Gummies, the organic, vegan gummy snacks developed by seven-time World Champion Tom Brady, have launched exclusively on Gopuff. Made with real fruit and free of artificial sweeteners, dyes, and flavors, the gummies reflect Brady’s commitment to better-for-you indulgences. “Goat Gummies hit that sweet spot,” said Brady, noting their great taste and clean ingredients. In collaboration with Gopuff, Brady helped perfect the flavors and textures to meet his exacting standards, creating a game-time snack with no compromises—just greatness in every bite.

records.title: Can't Contain -- Spicy Tenders
records.description: People love Golden Chick’s famous Golden Tenders, but not everyone realizes you can order them Spicy. Sprinkled with the brand’s signature Lotta Zing seasoning, they’re a tasty option that dials up the flavor with a bold kick. To spread the word, we took a meta approach to our 15-second media placement, giving viewers a glimpse at what happens inside the mind of someone trying Spicy Tenders for the first time.

records.title: Golden Chick "Sandwich Senses"
records.description: Golden Chick’s new Pimento Crunchwich has a combination of crave-able tastes that begged to be romanced. By giving each ingredient a customer reaction, we built anticipation for the completed sandwich, while sound design connected this new creation to our classic mnemonic sing out. All together, it’s a sense-sational experience packed into one delicious 15-second spot that leaves the viewer hungry for more.

records.title: Golden Chick "Shanty"
records.description: When it's shrimp season, nothing hits the spot like Golden Chick's crispy, crunchy Butterfly Shrimp. And when seafood is this delicious, it makes you express your love for it in . . . interesting ways.

records.title: Goth Happens
records.description:
Goth Happens is a darkly different running shoe campaign by FLUORO® with R.A.D®. The running market is loud. Neon, slogans, the kind of relentless optimism that wants you buzzing (read: exhausted) before you've even left the house. R.A.D®, the disruptive performance footwear company, wasn't interested in any of that. So for the all-black colourway drop of their running shoe, the UFO they went the other way. ‘Goth Happens’, a deadpan nod to 'shit happens', became the brief to their creative partner, East London studio FLUORO®. 
Sport doesn't always have to feel like a pep talk, so FLUORO® built the campaign around darkness: liberty spike subculture, glitch-distorted film and a big ol' 'f**k you' attitude. Teaser film, social carousels, website banners, a full lookbook. Turns out not everyone runs toward the light.

Liquified metal ident
The ‘Goth Happens’ ident becomes a graphic anchor for campaign. The liquified chrome bubble type loosely bridges the gap between 90s retro sport and genre-specific metalcore. The ident has two different treatments across the campaign: monochrome and violet glitch. These two options gave the rollout deliberate flex,  rather than just being a single static asset. A monochrome palette with a single, neon violet hit is true to the goth lens.

Subculture-specific styling
The casting and movement direction leaned into tension and the specifics of emo / goth subcultures, rather than dynamic action poses typical of running campaigns. So it felt more editorial than competitor-aligned sport. Jewellery details – the R.A.D charm necklace and studded soles – were treated as unexpected hero moments in their own right. 

Retro-futuristic post-production
The VHS-shot footage, as well as a contact sheet-style lookbook, lo-fi stop motion gifs developed in-post were deliberate nods to Tumblr and zine subcultures. The campaign leans into high contrast and degraded glitch textures to pull more from the specific subculture aesthetic without losing R.A.D’s overarching retro-futuristic brand aesthetic.

The Goth Happens campaign ran across R.A.D® socials and website; and running retailer socials. It sits within a stream of creative work for the brand by FLUORO® that draws on subcultures and nods to the 1990s, incorporating visual artifacts from that era into the R.A.D identity. Through vibrant mash-ups of analogue and digital aesthetics, R.A.D is situated within a world much broader than training and gym culture. The brand is distinguished from the hyper-glossy, hyper-competitive aesthetic that has largely defined fitness culture in recent years, and R.A.D is positioned as a footwear brand for more than fitness fanatics alone.

records.title: GP Access – Tap it, type it and we’ll take care of it
records.campaign_title: GP Access – Tap it, type it and we’ll take care of it
records.description:
NHS England has launched GP Access – Tap it, type it and we’ll take care of it, a new multichannel national campaign created by M+C Saatchi Group UK, designed to encourage people to contact their GP practice via its website rather than automatically picking up the phone.

The campaign supports a wider NHS ambition to recover access to primary care by reducing pressure on GP phone lines for those who need them most, particularly during the 8am rush, and by helping patients get the right help in a more convenient way. It focuses on increasing awareness, understanding and use of online forms available through GP practice websites, improving both access and overall patient experience.

At the heart of the campaign is a significant behavioural shift. For many people, the deeply ingrained belief is that the ‘best’ and ‘right’ way to contact a GP is by phone, and that calling is how GP practices want to hear from them. The work is designed to challenge that assumption and create a new memory structure for audiences, reframing online access as an easy, practical way to get help.

With that in mind, the creative needed to connect with a broad range of people while clearly demonstrating the ease and convenience of the service. The campaign centres on everyday members of the public tapping away on laptops and mobiles as they enter their symptoms on their GP practice website. This simple, familiar action is shown in different settings and situations, making the process feel quick, accessible and achievable.
 
As the campaign unfolds, the sound of typing gradually builds into a recognisable rhythm, forming a shared melody that reflects a nation coming together and embracing a new way of accessing care. The edit and tempo begin slowly before building in pace and energy, culminating in a flurry of synchronised tapping. A 30-second film, directed by Simon Ratigan at Rogue Films, brings together sound, picture and emotion to challenge perceptions and, ultimately, help change habits.

Tonally, the work is warm, emotive and relatable. The simple two-finger “Chopsticks” piano piece, familiar to most audiences, is used to symbolise ease and simplicity, helping to dispel concerns about using a website to contact a GP practice.

records.title: Graduate Financially
records.description:
Millennials have come a long way from the bygone era of hipster mustaches, shutter shades, and sepia filters. They’ve graduated from first jobs, first apartments, and first loves. Yet, an Ally study found that nearly half still use their first bank account—with roughly 3 in 4 reporting they opened the account as a teenager. 
That insight sparked the finance company’s strategy of addressing “banking inertia,” the tendency to stick with the same bank long after it makes sense. After all, as life moves forward, so should your bank. Developed in partnership with Anomaly, the new “Graduate Financially” campaign reframes switching banks as a life upgrade—on par with moving to a new city, changing jobs, or getting a new apartment—and one that’s long overdue.
The :30 second spot taps into early 2010s nostalgia — think Harlem Shake — to unlock core Millennial memories and invite reflection on how far they’ve come. With Ally, they can mark another major milestone. Not just growing up, but growing financially. Two 15-second cuts accompany the campaign; you can have a look here, and here.
To further ground the campaign in its Millennial roots, Ally teamed up with teen heartthrob of the era, Taylor Lautner, for an Instagram and TikTok campaign, reinforcing just how long ago many opened their first account. Ally is the bank built for “what’s next,” aligning with how people manage money today. Being digital-first goes hand-in-hand with being customer-first: no branches, no waiting rooms—just intuitive tools that fit seamlessly into modern financial life.
Ally isn’t like your first bank. It’s a smarter, mobile-first platform with tools tailored to Millennial habits — automated savings, budget visibility, and frictionless usability for those who expect everything to just work. The work launches today, June 2, across linear, CTV, OLV, paid social, and influencer content — perfectly timed to evoke nostalgia for the spring graduation season.

records.title: GRANDPARENTS
records.description:
Milka, the iconic chocolate brand belonging to Mondelēz International, and official sponsor of LALIGA, is launching a campaign that connects with the emotion of football in a very special way. The brand's objective was to find out if there was room for tenderness, its most essential value, in the king of sports. And the affirmative answer was found in its maximum exponent outside the field, in families, and, specifically, in the figure of GRANDPARENTS.

Recognizing the fundamental role they play, Milka is launching an initiative -conceived by Ogilvy- that celebrates the role of grandparents as unconditional support for their grandchildren's dreams; as that haven where ambition finds support and fear dissipates with a hug. While the world rushes and demands results, grandparents typically offer their grandchildren the time and patience needed to nurture their earliest hopes and aspirations, becoming a great emotional support that allows a young person to leave home to pursue their destiny.

This bond transcends any material value, as it is based on simple values and unconditional love that celebrates every step of the way. There is no purer pride than that of a grandmother who sees her grandson succeed, demonstrating that behind every great achievement there is always a family history that made the flight possible.

In the words of Sofía Brás, Senior Brand Manager Milka Iberia, "With this campaign we celebrate the figure of grandparents, who play a fundamental role in supporting the Spanish family; they are that inspiration of effort and dedication that connects directly with the tenderness of a brand like Milka."

A campaign created from emotion

To illustrate this concept, Milka has sought a pair within the football world that represents this connection, this mutual dedication and devotion between a player and their grandparent, and has opted for the story of Fermín López and his grandmother Loli. They are the protagonists of the brand's new campaign, created by the Ogilvy agency, which launches today.

Fermín López Marín, a promising Spanish offensive midfielder for FC Barcelona and the Spanish national team, is known for his fighting mentality on the field, technical quality and powerful shot from outside the box. He has been an absolute international and gold medalist at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. But what is not reflected in his resume or his sports profile is the special relationship he has with his grandmother Loli.
With this campaign, Milka provides a closer look at their connection, demonstrating the profound and emotional bond they share, based on family pride and unconditional support. Throughout the spot, Loli expresses her immense pride in her grandson's effort and achievements, remembering him as a brave boy who pursued his dream from a young age.

The story of Fermín and Loli is a reflection of a love that transcends the brilliance of professional success. Behind the great player, there is a grandmother who today overflows with happiness seeing the simple values her grandson possesses and the career he is forging. Loli embodies that purest family pride, demonstrating that true triumph is found in the recognition of a life dedicated to fulfilling a dream under the protection of one's roots.

This campaign further strengthens the bond between Milka and LALIGA, taking the sponsorship to the tenderest ground in football, as it focuses on the relevant family values that unite them, giving visibility and paying tribute to the figure of those unsung heroes who sustain and provide tenderness and support to the family.

records.title: Guac Guru
records.description: In the run-up to Super Bowl LX, Avocados From Mexico has launched the Prediction Pit, a digital platform where fans can interact with an AI-powered Rob Riggle avatar known as the “Guac Guru.” The mystical character offers customized guacamole recipes while predicting playoff and Super Bowl outcomes using real-time data from SportsDataIO. Visitors enter their name, team, and prediction type, and can even compete against the Guru for a chance to win a year’s supply of avocados, blending entertainment, personalization, and game-day food inspiration.

records.title: Halftime Hunger
records.description:
What happens when hunger hits hard? Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen starts popping up in the most unexpected places.What happens when hunger hits hard? Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen starts popping up in the most unexpected places. 

SNICKERS and SNICKERS ICE CREAM have teamed up with star quarterback Josh Allen to tackle fans’ halftime hunger because, for NFL fans, halftime isn’t just a point in time; it’s a crucial turning point where you either refuel and reset, or risk letting hunger take over. The humorous spots explore how hunger can throw everyday moments completely off track — leading to serious distraction and a warped sense of reality. 

“Bedtime” (SNICKERS): Everyday moments can quickly go off the rails when hunger takes over, causing distraction. In the first commercial, a hungry dad reading his son a bedtime story suddenly imagines Josh Allen as his son in a racecar bed “Construction” 

(SNICKERS ICE CREAM): In this spot, a construction worker loses focus and hallucinates Josh Allen as his coworker on a construction site. Luckily, in both scenarios, SNICKERS is there to bring them back to reality and help them stay focused in these turning point moments. The campaign also features a series of quick-hit :15 and :06 cuts, where even Josh Allen isn’t immune, fumbling lines and forgetting sponsors until he gets his SNICKERS fix. Whether it’s an everyday moment or a high-stakes NFL play, the message is clear: you’re distracted when you’re hungry. records.title: Handshake
records.description:
Famous Footwear is on a mission to help everyone feel famous in their own shoes. And there’s no time like back to school to show off new kicks. Focusing on value for this season based on the current economy, Famous once again partnered with its creative AOR THE MAYOR to create a new campaign focused on its ‘buy one, get one half off’ offer. 

The hero spot titled ‘Handshake’ emphasizes the charm and excitement of back to school for kids, while bringing new energy through an on-trend, TikTok-ready ‘Famous Shake’ routine featuring twins. The shoes (and their fancy footwork) are the stars of the show, and are quite helpful in deciphering who’s who, while highlighting individuality through style. The campaign also features a social component, where the twins teach audiences how to do the ‘Famous Shake’, which was filmed in the Famous Footwear store in NYC.

‘Handshake’ is currently running as :30s and :15s spots across TV and social. This is THE MAYOR’s third seasonal effort and second back to school campaign in partnership with Famous Footwear, following the award of the business in spring of 2024.

records.title: Happy Applecore
records.description:
Leading cider brand, Crumpton Oaks is celebrating the summer months by turning back the clock to the electric energy of the 1990s and partnering with electronic music pioneer DJ Hixxy for a brand-new campaign, Happy Applecore, by McCann Birmingham. 

Far from the typical idyllic country scenes, this electric new campaign celebrates the brand’s unique position as a category disruptor and builds on the success of their last hip-hop-inspired campaign, Straight Outta Crumpton, by McCann Birmingham.  

As part of the new Happy Applecore campaign, Crumpton Oaks has teamed up with legendary British DJ, Hixxy, to produce an original, feel-good track, recorded by MC Whizzkid.  Known for shaping the UK Happy Hardcore scene, Hixxy adds authenticity and infectious energy to the campaign.

The campaign for Aston Manor’s leading cider brand was designed to help retail trade connect with customers by transporting consumers back to the neon brights and high energy of the 90s. It also features original lyrics that put Crumpton Oaks firmly in shoppers’ minds as ‘the raver with flavour’. 

The work will run across TV, VOD, social, and a unique OOH campaign throughout the summer. Alongside fly posters and 48 sheets in prominent sites, the OOH will feature on-theme psychedelic neon projection of Crumpton Oaks cider.

records.title: Harvest Snap out of it
records.description: In an exciting new campaign developed in partnership with Hook Creative Studio, Harvest Snaps is bringing wholesome snacking to life with the return of their much-loved mascot, Penelopea. The ad, set to launch across multiple platforms, combines humour and health in a light-hearted commercial where Penelopea appears—almost out of nowhere—to guide our hero talent toward making the smart choice: Harvest Snaps Multi-packs.

records.title: Hay algo hermoso que nos une
records.campaign_title: Hay algo hermoso que nos une
records.description:
Deprati celebra la belleza real en su Semana de la Belleza

En un mundo donde la belleza ya no se define por estándares únicos, Deprati presenta Semana de la Belleza con un mensaje claro y cercano: “Hay algo hermoso que nos une”. Una campaña que entiende la belleza como un acto cotidiano, espontáneo y profundamente humano.

Creada bajo la dirección creativa de la agencia independiente BBA, en colaboración con el equipo de Deprati, la campaña pone en el centro una verdad simple pero poderosa: la belleza sucede en los momentos más reales, no en los más perfectos.

Una belleza que se vive, no que se impone

El insight que da vida a la campaña nace de una escena universal: el auto como espacio de complicidad, ese lugar donde nos miramos en el espejo retrovisor, nos retocamos el maquillaje, arreglamos el cabello y, sobre todo, compartimos risas, confidencias y tiempo juntas.
Porque antes de llegar al evento, al trabajo o a una cita, la belleza ya ocurrió: ocurrió en el camino, entre amigas, siendo una misma.

El spot de la campaña retrata a mujeres diversas, de distintas edades, estilos y personalidades, compartiendo ese instante tan reconocible: arreglarse juntas dentro del auto. No hay poses forzadas ni discursos grandilocuentes. Hay alegría, autenticidad y libertad.

Las vemos felices, cómodas con quienes son, celebrando su individualidad mientras forman parte de algo más grande: una comunidad unida por la experiencia compartida de la belleza cotidiana.

Con esta campaña, Deprati eleva la Semana de la Belleza a un espacio de celebración y pertenencia. No se trata solo de maquillaje, fragancias o cuidado personal, sino de  de reconocer que la belleza también vive en la amistad, en el camino y en los pequeños rituales diarios.
Porque al final, hay algo hermoso que nos une: ser auténticos.

records.title: Hay Grido (There´s Grido)
records.description:
As part of it´s brand positioning, Grido wanted Uruguayans to perceive it as a local brand. To keep building on this, we uncovered an undeniable truth: wherever you go, there’s a Grido nearby. With 87 ice cream shops, it´s the only ice cream brand with presence all across the country.
However, this wasn’t something the brand had been communicating, so we decided to bring it to the forefront in this campaign.

records.title: He'll Be Back
records.description:
Creative studio Plural delivers a moving campaign for pet nutrition brand NutriSource, directed by Plural’s Stash Capar and led by Rise and Shine and Partners. 

The spot follows a young girl reassuring her dog as her father leaves for work each morning, explaining that he helps deliver dog food so dogs everywhere can stay healthy and bring comfort to people in need. As her narration unfolds, the story reveals a deeper, emotional layer, culminating in a hospital filled with thank you cards from children supported by emotional support animals during their recovery. Among them is the daughter, who was once comforted by a therapy dog herself, reframing the father’s routine as a quiet act of care and connection.

“This is exactly the kind of project I love - something that’s grounded in human truth,” shares Stash. “Rise and Shine and Partners wrote one of the best scripts I’ve read in a long time and were a joy to work with. The client was equally engaged which made the whole process even more meaningful.”

“I had a very personal connection to the script," he continues. “While living in a refugee camp as a little kid I had to be admitted to a hospital where I had surgery on my leg. I had no idea what was going on, I didn’t understand the language that any of the doctors or staff spoke. My parents, and especially my father, visited me daily during recovery and always made me smile. My earliest childhood memories were formed here. The life parallels were too close to ignore. I remember being that child in recovery and having an unshakeable faith in my parents, but I also felt a connection to the father and the idea that “he’ll be back” to be with his daughter.” 

Built around heartfelt performances from the cast, the campaign focuses on emotional authenticity, letting the story unfold through human moments while the product is woven naturally into the narrative. Stash approached directing children and animals as the emotional core of the project.

“Some people see kids and animals as challenging,” adds Stash. “For me, that’s the best part of filmmaking. You can’t direct emotion mechanically. You have to create an environment where real moments can happen. Emotionally authentic moments aren’t a checklist. They’re something more ethereal than that.”

Director of Photography Alejandro Wilkins helped shape the campaign's visual language.

“Alejandro was the perfect choice. His background in narrative served us well as he understood the essence of the film — that we were there to capture a human moment, and that all visual choices would exist to serve the story, not distract from it. He not only brought the planned shots to life, but elevated them in very smart and subtle ways, allowing me to stay focused on story and emotional authenticity. It was a great pairing and the beginning of something new. I can’t wait to work with him again.”

Stash’s early years shaped a lifelong, nuanced understanding of childhood, family, and the human condition — one that followed him across Canada, the U.K., Scandinavia, the Middle East, and ultimately the United States. He began his career as an editor and creative producer before stepping into the director’s chair in 2015. His early projects were immediately recognized at the Cannes Young Director Award and the SHOOT New Directors Showcase. Since then, Stash has directed award-winning campaigns for AncestryDNA, Durex, Fujifilm, Gerber, MadeGood, Tylenol, and others.

Plural partners closely with brands and agencies to build the right production team around each objective, maximizing every dollar and putting more on screen. For this project, the alignment between Plural and director Stash made it a seamless fit.

As Founder & EP Steve Holm explains, “We are pretty crazy about dogs at Plural, so that had us from word one – but this stood out because this is a deeper story than the everyday bonds between people and pets. Stash, with his tasteful, classically cinematic approach and deep understanding of how to tug at those emotional heartstrings, was the perfect director to bring this idea to life and the collaboration with both the agency and brand made it possible to deliver something we are all proud of. Great partnerships make great work and this is a perfect example of that.”

records.title: He’s not just delivering pizza...
records.description:
Set to launch nationwide on March 26 and with a grand debut during the NCAA Sweet 16® on March 27, Peter Zahut kicks off Pizza Hut’s latest brand campaign, embodying the energy and excitement that comes with every Pizza Hut order. Peter Zahut is the ultimate delivery legend who never shows up empty-handed. Whether he’s dropping off a hot pizza or setting up the perfect alley-oop, Peter has a knack for making every moment bigger, better, and a lot more fun. He’s not just delivering pizza—he’s delivering the kind of good times that Pizza Hut is all about.

“This campaign is about more than just shining a spotlight on our great pizza; it’s about spotlighting the good times and big and small moments of joy that come with adding pizza to any occasion,” said Melissa Friebe, chief marketing officer at Pizza Hut. “Just like our campaign, our latest culinary innovations are equally as fun. As we launch Cheesy Bites Pizza and the Ranch Lover’s Flight, it's more than great pizza and dip. It's about letting basketball and pizza fans dip, dunk and have fun with our iconic Original Stuffed Crust® and bold flavours.”

Ryan Lehr, co-chief creative officer, Deutsch said, “When Pizza Hut shows up you know you are in for a good time. So, we wanted to embody that energy in a person. The ultimate delivery guy who always rolls up with Pizza Hut in hand, and a trick or two up his satin jacket sleeve. He’s not meant to be the center of attention, but the straw stirs the drink. Dishing out the pizza (and alley oops in this case), instigating good times with a flair for the dramatic, and a knowing wink.”

In addition to the new campaign, Pizza Hut is bringing back a fan-favorite menu item: Cheesy Bites Pizza. This pizza features 28 pull-apart, cheese-filled bites in place of a traditional crust—perfect for dipping, dunking, and sharing.

And for the first time ever, Pizza Hut is introducing The Ranch Lover’s Flight*, a trio of bold, exclusive dipping sauces that take the dipping experience to the next level:

* Chipotle Ranch – Smoky and spicy with a bold kick
* Ultimate Ranch – Creamy and rich, the MVP of the bunch
* Pepperoni Ranch – A perfect blend of pepperoni flavours and ranch
* Pepperoni Ranch is flavoured with signature pepperoni spices, flavours, and herbs (does not contain pepperoni).

records.title: Hello it’s your Farm Bureau agent
records.campaign_title: Hello it’s your Farm Bureau agent
records.description:
Ending a nearly decade-long hiatus, the Virginia Farm Bureau presents its latest work. The insurance provider partnered with Two Tango Collaborative to launch a campaign focused on what matters most – the people. 

In a category known for touting price point or coverage features, “Hello it’s your Farm Bureau agent” is the first campaign of its kind to focus on the agents as the differentiator — by highlighting that Virginia Farm Bureau agents are local and rooted in their communities. Unsurprisingly, the brand tapped a local creative agency to highlight the human connection.

Two Tango leaned into animation, as the creative medium, to give the creative a distinctive edge. All of the work — from the font to the illustrations to the music — was completely custom and made by humans. 

“We believe in the power community and putting people first, so this partnership has always felt very true to our ethos,” shared Erin Sarro, executive creative director, Two Tango Collaborative. “When you need help, being able to trust the person on the other end of the phone is essential, so we wanted to highlight that with Virginia Farm Bureau, you absolutely can.”  

As part of the campaign, the insurance provider is also debuting a new tagline, “Always there. Always have been.” The messaging focal point serves as a reminder to Virginians that they can count on the Virginia Farm Bureau brand.

records.title: Here for First Steps to World Bests
records.campaign_title: Here for First Steps to World Bests
records.description:
ASB has launched "Here for First Steps to World Bests", a new campaign celebrating its partnerships with the New Zealand Team and Athletics New Zealand. Created by Droga5 ANZ, part of Accenture Song, the campaign uses sport as a symbol of steady progress, showing how every achievement begins with a single step. It connects grassroots participation with elite competition, supporting everyone from children discovering athletics through to athletes preparing for the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

The campaign highlights running as one of the clearest expressions of progress, whether it is a child taking part in Athletics New Zealand’s Run Jump Throw and Get Set Go programmes or an elite athlete pursuing international success. The hero film follows this journey from first participation to world-class performance, while supporting spots focus on children entering the sport and athletes progressing towards the Commonwealth Games.

The campaign extends across out-of-home, digital and social media, with large-format advertising raising awareness of ASB’s sporting partnerships and local executions reinforcing the bank’s support within communities. Together, the work positions ASB as a long-term supporter of progress at every level, helping New Zealanders take their first steps in sport while backing those who go on to represent Aotearoa on the world stage.

records.title: Here for Good
records.description:
Prisma Health’s new “Here for Good.” campaign expands the definition of care, spotlighting the ways compassion moves through both patients and the communities around them. From exam rooms to living rooms and the quiet moments in between, the work shows that care doesn’t start or stop at the bedside — it radiates across families, neighborhoods, and everyday life.

Directed by Voyager’s Brandon Kapelow and edited by Kauai of Leap Year, the campaign brings this message to life with an intimate, observational approach. Developed by creative agency BRAINS, it reframes care as an ongoing relationship that extends far beyond appointments and clinical settings.

Through simple, human moments, the campaign honors the village behind every patient: the nurse who remembers your name, the friends and family who rally around you, the specialist who catches what others might miss, and the quiet acts of kindness that shape the journey. It’s a portrait of a health system woven into the fabric of its community, present not only for the critical moments, but for all the small ones in between.

records.title: Here for Life
records.description:
After naming Gus its lead creative partner across brand and campaigns last month, Lovesac today launched its first work with the agency under a new brand platform, “Here for Life." The campaign is built around a simple truth: real life at home is a little chaotic, and furniture should be able to grow and adapt alongside it - and stand up to anything that life throws at your sofa.

"Here for Life" reframes the couch not as a pristine centerpiece, but as something built to live through whatever happens around it. It’s a shift away from disposable, fast-furniture culture toward pieces designed for people settling into homes they plan to grow into.

It also pushes against the category’s reliance on perfectly staged interiors, instead leaning into real-life scenarios and even casting real couples and friends. Each spot was built around situations we’ve all experienced but rarely see reflected in home interior advertising.
In “After the Party,” the morning after a house party reveals total destruction, from drinks everywhere to a phone buried in a birthday cake, as a modular couch flexes to handle the aftermath.
“THAT corner” showcases a real-life couple struggling to make an awkward “cozy nook” work, only to realize the furniture needs to adapt to the space, not the other way around.
“Cookie” features a young kid unleashing chocolate-covered chaos across a couch, only for the moment to be shrugged off thanks to washable covers.
Across all three, the product shows up through real scenarios rather than demonstration – highlighting modularity, flexibility, and durability without feeling like a product demo.

The campaign is running across CTV (including buys surrounding MLB), YouTube, programmatic, audio, video and display, and national and local digital out of home and was directed by David Helman of Iconoclast - hand-selected by Gus.

The work also reflects how Gus operates: small, senior teams staying close to the idea and building creative rooted in real behavior, not category conventions. It has the irreverent edge that’s become a hallmark of Gus’s work, with a willingness to let things feel a little messy and unexpected.

records.title: Here for the Sauce
records.description:
McDonald's and Leo UK are launching 'Here for the Sauce', a new campaign that invites fans to participate and co-create in their shared love of McDonald’s sauces.

The campaign is built on the fan truth that for many McDonald’s customers, the sauce is not the side, it’s the main event. Launching alongside three new sauces - Korean BBQ, Ranch and Hot Honey - the six-week campaign will run across social, creator content, live activation, TV, OOH, radio and CRM across the UK and Ireland.

From 14th July, sauce will takeover McDonald’s Social channels, spotlighting the real sauce-related behaviours seen across our feeds - from people stockpiling sauce pots to the fans who simply cannot resist licking the lid. The campaign also invites fans to co-create in the campaign via social led moments, including The Sweet Curry Suitcase, based on real fans taking McDonald’s sauce on holiday. The Sweet Curry Suitcase is a limited-edition suitcase shaped like the iconic sauce pot. Content creator and sauce superfan, Luke Hamnett, will co-create content that shows off his very own Sweet Curry Suitcase.

The fan campaign also comes to life in the real world through The Sauce Stop, a live activation built entirely around sauces, giving fans a physical way to participate in their shared love of McDonald’s sauces by building a destination dedicated to their favourite part of the McDonald’s experience.

At the heart of the Here for the Sauce campaign are five TV spots, where Stephen Graham’s voiceover attempts to keep the focus on chicken, but the cameraman is a big fan of sauce. A really big fan of sauce. Directed by Oli Beale, the sauces repeatedly steal the spotlight, with different camera techniques - from pans to focus shifts - pulling attention away from the food and back to the sauces. The result is a playful nod to what McDonald’s fans have always known - the sauce is the real star of the order.

OOH strips the idea back even further, using bold, colourful visuals that hero the sauces in their own right. Rather than showing sauce as an accompaniment, the posters place the dips front and centre, creating a distinctive sauce-led look and feel across nationwide placements. Radio extends the same tension, with 20-second spots that play where Stephen Graham is just your regular sauce-obsessed superfan.

The campaign also heroes McDonald’s limited-time Hot Honey range, the new Hot Honey sauce taking centre stage with the Hot Honey McCrispy, Hot Honey Sausage & Egg McMuffin, Double Hot Honey Sausage & Egg McMuffin and Hot Honey Mini McFlurry.
James Hodson, Creative Director at Leo UK, said: "Whenever I go to McDonald’s, I always think: should I get some food with my sauce? And I am not alone. This campaign is all about letting fans participate in their shared love of sauces, giving them the platform to co-create with the brand. It’s a big idea that’s poured across every possible channel and touchpoint, like sauce over McNuggets.”

Hannah Pain, Marketing Director at McDonald’s UK, said: “McDonald’s fans have always had a special relationship with our sauces – for some, they’re the best part of the order. With Korean BBQ, Ranch and Hot Honey joining the line-up, this felt like the perfect moment to put sauces centre stage and celebrate a part of the McDonald’s experience our customers really love. For fans who can’t get enough of Hot Honey, they’ll find it popping up across a selection of menu favourites for a limited time this summer too.”

The campaign was a collaboration by McDonald’s agency partners: creative was handled by Leo UK. Media planning and buying was managed by OMD. PR, event and influencer management was handled by Red Consultancy. Production was handled by DROOL.

records.title: Hero Behind the Heroes
records.description:
FCB London has created a new Christmas campaign for Intuit QuickBooks for Accountants, celebrating the invaluable—but often overlooked—role they play in steering complex businesses to success.
Breaking this week, the campaign will run for 2 weeks and is composed of TV, including 30", 20" and 6" films, and social media.

The film shows Santa's elves working at full capacity to hit their Christmas deadlines, while CEO Santa is in his office taking a call from his accountant, Alice. Thanks to the suite of tools that Alice can access through QuickBooks for Accountants, she can see exactly what Santa needs to prepare for the busy season ahead – more reindeer to hit his targets.

Michael Benjamin, Director of Marketing Intuit QuickBooks UK said:
“Accountants, bookkeepers and small businesses are the backbone of our economy and their vital work, often behind the scenes, doesn't stop during the festive season! We wanted to show the role the Intuit QuickBooks platform plays in enabling seamless collaboration between businesses and their accountants during this very busy time of year. What better way to do this than with the owner of a very special, complex international business - Santa himself!

“Santa’s workshop is fun but it’s also a great example of some of the clients we serve, he has a need for elf payroll, payments and automated expense management, and his accountant helps him get ahead of the year. We’re so excited to launch this magical new Christmas campaign.”

Ben Perez Usher, Creative Director at FCB London said: "We wanted to show that for Santa, Christmas is a year-round business. If you think about it, he’s the CEO of one the biggest present delivery networks in the world, and his heroic accountant uses the power of QuickBooks to realise his vision.”

records.title: Hoist the Cone
records.description:
PNC Bank is tapping into an organic fan movement at PNC Park in Pittsburgh by serving up limited-edition ice cream (traffic) cones to Pittsburgh Pirates fans on select game days this season.

Created in partnership with AOR Arnold, the promotion pays tribute to the now famous “Hoist the Cone” rallying cry, which originated from a misprinted shirt reading “Hoist the Cone” instead of “Hoist the Colors.” Pirates fans embraced the unexpected slogan, and the orange traffic cone has become a recognizable symbol of Pittsburgh Pirates team spirit and local pride since.

With real traffic cones recently disappearing from city streets as fans hunted for gear to hoist at games, PNC stepped in to give the hometown crowd a safer, smarter, and far tastier way to join the celebration.

The activation brings PNC’s “Brilliantly Boring” brand platform to life in an unexpected way: as traffic cones began disappearing from Pittsburgh streets, longtime Pirates and PNC Park partner PNC -- and a known champion of avoiding unnecessary risks -- stepped in with a safer, smarter and far tastier way for fans to hoist the cone.

The collectible cone holders will be available inside PNC Park on August 16, September 6, and September 20, 2026, free with every waffle cone purchase, while supplies last.

records.title: Home You vs Road You
records.description:
GEICO just rolled out their largest creative slate ever: eight new campaigns across seven lines of business, including Auto, Home, Boat, Motorcycle, RV, Renters, and two Commercial Auto segments (Truckers and Small Business Owners). The work has been dropping throughout the summer, and now that everything's live, it marks a return to major creative scale for the brand, all with a sharper focus on value. It’s all about getting more for your money: more ease, more peace of mind, more benefits (not just lower prices). That’s the whole “Get more with GEICO” promise 

There’s a big difference between Home You and Road You. But there is nothing Road You can’t do with the support of GEICO’s RV specialists and 24/7 Emergency Roadside Service. The campaign comically compares “Home You” to “Road You” using quick cuts between two versions of the same character to show how confident, supported and generally fun you can be when GEICO RV insurance keeps you in the driver’s seat.

records.title: Honestly, good.
records.description:
Did you know four out of five people effing hate their bank? So getting them to switch to a credit union should be easy, right? We thought so too. But turns out, people are lazy — and you’ve really got to remind them just how much of a jerk their big national bank actually is.

The term “banking” often conjures memories of hidden fees, infuriating customer services, and a general sense of being taken advantage of. Why is that? It is your money, your security, your life after all. Well we couldn’t tell you. But we do know that there is another way, a better way, to get everything you need from banking—without the big bank mentality.

Credit Union of Colorado
Honestly, good.

records.title: Honesty Is Our Policy
records.description:
Insurance is everywhere. On your commute, in your streaming queue, in every commercial break. Yet despite its visibility, many people still struggle to understand what coverage they have.

Farmers believes that confidence starts with understanding. That's why the brand is leaning into what it does best: helping people navigate insurance with clear explanations, practical information, and straightforward communication. By making it easier for customers to understand their options, Farmers is empowering people to make more informed decisions about protecting what matters most. 

"Honesty Is Our Policy," created with Dentsu Creative, is a new brand platform, part of a larger rebrand, built on a simple belief: helping customers understand their insurance is one of the most important things an insurance company can help them do. What your policy covers. What it doesn't. What the fine print actually means. Explained clearly, openly, and in language people can actually use. Because when it comes to insurance, confidence comes from understanding. And honesty looks different depending on what customers need. 

Across every touchpoint, Farmers is continuing to raise the bar on clarity and transparency. Interactions and communications are designed to help customers better understand their coverage and feel more confident in their decisions. 

The Creative Approach
To bring this platform to life, the campaign introduces a new voice for Farmers: direct, confident, and refreshingly candid. And because saying we’re different isn’t enough, Farmers will also look distinctly different – from its past and from the category – with an impossible-to-ignore pink. And lots of it.  

The hero :30 speaks directly to the audience against a bold pink backdrop, establishing a new expectation for the brand. No distractions. Just a clear commitment to continuing to help people better understand insurance. 
 
Before the spot is over, it addresses the elephant in the room and introduces a new brand asset built to reinforce that commitment: the Choir. 

The rebrand also marks a new chapter for one of advertising's most recognized sonic assets. "We Are Farmers" becomes "You Have Farmers," shifting from a brand declaration to a customer benefit. It's no longer just about knowing the name. It's about having confidence and clarity.  

Beginning July 13, "Honesty Is Our Policy" will come to life across broadcast, digital, social, out-of-home, and experiential, demonstrating how Farmers continues to bring greater clarity, transparency, and understanding to the customer experience.

records.title: House Hot Sauce Lentil Chips
records.description:
PROPER, the UK’s fastest-growing major snack brand, has launched its new House Hot Sauce Lentil Chips with a brand artifact instead of a campaign. The independent creative studio Small W•rld has produced a  first of its kind limited-edition House Hot Sauce candle for the brand. Sold on TikTok Shop alongside the bottled sauce; once burnt through, it turns into a warm, dippable hot sauce.

Unlike most spicy snacks, which tend to deliver either intense heat with little flavour, or plenty of flavour without meaningful heat, PROPER set out to do things differently. The brand started by creating the perfect hot sauce, balancing heat with tang and depth of flavour, and then built the Lentil Chips around it. The result is a flavour profile designed around pleasure rather than punishment.

That product truth became the foundation for the creative platform. Rather than leaning into the bravado and endurance that typically defines spicy food culture, PROPER and Small W•rld reimagined spicy snacking through the lens of flavour, pleasure and desire, bringing a softer, more feminine perspective to the category.

To bring that world to life, Small W•rld identified a cultural moment, one it describes as the "era of yearning;” a female-leaning audience defined by an intensity of connection, romantic revival, and who have a renewed appetite for sensory experience - from audio erotica and sexual wellness, to the current wave of sweeping romantic adaptations.

The House Hot Sauce Candle is the physical expression of that idea. Designed to set a sensual scene, whether for enjoying alone or sharing with a partner, it gradually melts into warm hot sauce, made for dipping with PROPER's House Hot Sauce Lentil Chips.

The launch also connects to Practice PROPER Snacking, PROPER's masterbrand platform, which subverts wellness culture to reframe snacking as an act of self-care. As self-pleasure is increasingly recognised as a form of self-care in its own right, the edible candle and the ritual around it become a playful exaggeration of that idea, turning a spicy snack into a slow, sensory, fully indulgent moment.

The launch is earned-first and social-first, led by three cinematic shorts plus teasers that playfully subvert the visual language of romance, sensuality and fan edits - dialling up the pleasure of the dipping ritual and turning the candle into an object of desire. This is supported by creator partnerships in the sexual wellness space and sommelier-style food accounts promoting the hot sauce, with no traditional media at the centre.

The current spicy offerings on the market either deliver heat without flavour, or flavour without the heat. We wanted to create a hot sauce that delivered both – the perfect balance of heat and tang, rooted in pleasure rather than punishment – whilst bringing a more feminine edge to spicy snacking. The House Hot Sauce Candle is the ultimate expression of that thinking and a playful way to Practice PROPER Snacking by turning a spicy snack into a sensory ritual of self-care." said Astrid Simpson, Comms and Campaign Manager, PROPER Snacks.
Sadia Noor, Creative Partner, Small W•rld added "Everything our audience wants from a brand is already out in the open. We know what trends they’re invested in, what they share with their community, what they want more of. So we didn't start with the brief - we started with the cultural codes people are already yearning for, and landed on innovative brand artifact worth the burn.”
PROPER's House Hot Sauce (£7, 100ml) is available exclusively via PROPER's TikTok Shop from 25th June, alongside the brand's House Hot Sauce Lentil Chips, also stocked at major retailers. The ultra-limited House Hot Sauce edible candle (£30) will be available via TikTok Shop from 6th July.

records.title: How It Feels to Chew 5 gum
records.campaign_title: How It Feels to Chew 5 gum
records.description:
Mars Wrigley is taking “How It Feels to Chew 5 gum” to a new dimension, inviting Gen Z TikTok fans to help regain their senses by channeling their love for meme culture and the weirdest parts of the internet, and taking it to social media.   

Building on the brand’s legendary campaign, the Co-Creation series transforms real fan responses into surreal, sensory-driven animations – turning the internet’s weirdest “how it feels” takes into a modern, multi-sensory social experience. 

From “becoming a human air conditioner” to “smashing a watermelon so hard it breaks reality,” this chapter is all about letting fans drive the feeling across a 12-part installation.  

Mars Wrigley: "At Mars Wrigley, we’ve always celebrated the creativity and passion of our consumers, and 5 gum’s legacy of ‘Stimulate Your Senses’ is a perfect example of how we connect with people on a personal level,” said Maria Urista, Vice President, Gum & Mints at Mars. “Seeing how fans have brought their humorous, vibrant perspectives to life over the years has been nothing short of inspiring. With this campaign, we’ve taken their creativity and put it on a bigger stage, turning their incredible ideas into content that’s as bold and refreshing as 5 gum itself.” 

Energy BBDO: “Sometimes the answer lies in the space your brand occupies in culture. For 5 Gum, that space just happened to be a bizarre and hilarious corner of the Internet,” said Josh Gross, Chief Creative Officer at Energy BBDO.

records.title: World, Unfolded.
records.description: This 30-second product film reimagines Huawei’s Mate TV, a groundbreaking smart screen that transforms the essence of the smartphone experience. Bringing every function from the palm of your hand to the vastness of a television unfolds the digital world once confined within a phone. The screen becomes more than a display — it’s an awakening, expanding the world back to its true scale, right before your eyes.

records.title: Husky Tools
records.description:
Voyager director Marcus Tortorici puts a range of cinematic tricks to use in the latest campaign for The Home Depot’s house brand, Husky Tools, via creative agency LERMA/. With cutting-edge visuals and relatable storytelling, the campaign exemplifies Tortorici’s ability to transform ideas into compelling narratives that resonate with audiences while celebrating the quality, innovation and range of offerings Husky provides. 

"From the very first call with LERMA/, it was an explosion of creative ideas—from the look and feel of the images to the specific sound design elements driving the spot's momentum,” shares Tortorici. “We had a lot of fun dreaming up ideas and the freedom to run with them was a blast. Our goal was to make each of these tools look and feel as powerful as possible, and I'm happy with how that was translated onto the screen."

The campaign unfolds through potential-filled narratives brought to life by precise, dynamic camera work and a meticulous visual approach. Tortorici utilized choreographed transitions, intricate lighting and the Bolt Motion Control system to create four unique spots in just three days. Using a combination of Scorpion cranes, fixed perspective hard mounts, POVs and probe lenses, macro close-ups of the tools captured the satisfaction of hands-on projects, showcasing the craftsmanship and attention to detail in each scene. The result is a visual narrative that elevates the tools as more than just objects but as an extension of one's skills.

records.title: Hyperbuxton
records.description:
Audible, a leading creator and provider of premium audio storytelling, today unveils a launch campaign for Adam Buxton’s new podcast, Successpod, by Audible.

Created by Fold7, the work drives excitement for the new title, which is the antidote to hustle culture and about Adam's paranoia around ageing and becoming irrelevant in this modern landscape.

To prick the pomposity of podcast culture, Fold7 identified what it is that makes audiences suspicious about modern hustle culture. Namely how over-engineered it is; flashy graphics, exaggerated SFX, clickbait statements, gimmicks, camera trickery and podcasting hosts doing anything to remain relevant to audiences.

This led to the idea of ‘Hyperbuxton’: two promos that start out taking cues from the slick, overly produced modern podcasting landscape, before the façade begins to unravel. In the first film, Buxton films himself in a private jet, saying: “Hi Adam Buxton here, welcome to the private jet that podcasting bought.” The camera pulls back revealing it’s just a DIY set-up.

A second film sees Buxton filming himself against a picture-perfect backdrop of a tropical beach. “Sup bro, Adam Buxton here. Yeah, I’m one of the most successful podcasters in the world. Why else would I be on a private beach.” An interruption by a local neighbour reveals he’s standing in front of a green screen in a local park by a dog waste bin.

Both films end with the line: “Successpod, my desperate quest for relevance.”
Dave Billing, Executive Creative Director at Fold7, said: “I’ve long been a fan of Adam’s, all the way from the Adam & Joe Show through to his hugely successful podcast. So, working with him was a bit of a treat, all the more so because this new podcast touches on a subject never far from the mind of any creative person over the age of forty: how do you stay relevant and at what price does success come? As you’d imagine, there was a lot of co-creation on this project as we needed to leave room for Adam’s unique comedic brain to roam free.”

James Finn, Global Head of Brand & Content Marketing at Audible said: "Adam Buxton's comedy works because it's honest about the thing nobody admits: the desperate quest to stay relevant. We didn't want a campaign that sat next to the show – we wanted one as funny, self-aware and absurd as Adam himself. Working with Fold7, that's exactly what we made: something authentically Adam."

The campaign breaks today on paid social and YouTube pre-rolls, DOOH and radio. Media planning and buying is by GoodStuff.

records.title: IBM Global Campaign by Matt Blease & Niceshit
records.campaign_title: IBM Global Campaign by Matt Blease & Niceshit
records.country: Spain, United Kingdom, and United States
records.description:
A series of animated spots for the global IBM campaign by Matt Blease & Niceshit.

Classic comedy, bold scripts, and expressive characters - we couldn’t ask for more (says Niceshit).

We love creating work that aims to connect rather than impress, and this campaign is all about that: grabbing attention, building tension, then releasing it, making you feel awkward for an instant and making you laugh right after.

These spots were designed to be quiet, clever, and disruptive in their placement. We are firm believers that cutting through the noise is the way to actually get noticed.

It is curious, for a campaign about AI, it was one of the most human creative processes we’ve been part of. 
Scripts were loose and open, and we spent hours brainstorming with Matt and the teams at IBM and Ogilvy, speaking freely and letting the best idea win.

Both Matt and everyone at Niceshit love joyful, confident and smart comedy so it was very fun to push on awkward framings and silences, pauses and empty spaces without being afraid of losing the viewers attention, quite the opposite.

Massive thanks to IBM for the trust and freedom to be bold, be witty, and make something funny.

records.title: Si es pizza es La Especialista (If it´s pizza it´s)
records.campaign_title: Si es pizza es La Especialista (If it´s pizza it´s)
records.description:
We had to launch our new brand line of frozen pizzas. In a market saturated of competitors, how could we stand out? 
Well, we found that pizza itself as a food brings a lot of questions. Is it eaten with your bare hands or with fork and knife? When do you eat it? And most important, how do you pronounce it? Pizza, picsa or pitza?
We didnt find the answer but we know for sure that if you are going to eat pizza...it has to be La Especialista.

records.title: In Britânia Mode
records.description:
Britânia turns the streaming ad break into entertainment with “Mini Moments,” a genre-driven campaign for its 4-in-1 Air Fryer 

The idea adapts each film to match the genre viewers are watching — from comedy and crime to romance and horror — mirroring the tone, pacing and visual language of the content. Instead of interrupting the binge, the brand becomes part of it.

A 30-second hero film introduces the concept, positioning the Air Fryer as the ultimate binge companion, supported by 15-second genre-specific cutdowns built around one simple insight: every marathon needs a snack moment.

Running across platforms including Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max and YouTube, the campaign reinforces Britânia’s positioning, “In Britânia Mode", proving that contextual relevance is what keeps audiences watching.

records.title: Incognito by Afflelou
records.description:
A stylish gentleman inserts a virtually invisible hearing aid and proceeds to dance around his apartment to the beat of popular French 80s track, “De bonne humeur ce matin” (A good mood in the morning) by Tristan.

When the music cuts unexpectedly, he bangs on his ceiling in disappointment, revealing that the music was coming from his upstairs neighbour all along.

With the aid of Incognito by French optical and hearing aid retail chain Alain Afflelou, customers are able to hear their favourite sounds.

The 20s and 30s TV and online spots from BETC are directed by Rémi Danino with Executive Creative Director Antoine Choque.

records.title: Institute Director Jackie van Beek Helms New Campaign for Tea
records.campaign_title: Institute Director Jackie van Beek Helms New Campaign for Tea
records.description:
Jackie van Beek has directed the latest spots for Gold Peak Tea, produced by Institute. The campaign features the funny, relatable, and beautifully dry ‘spokes-sipper,’ Norm, advertising the original Gold Peak Tea along with Simply Gold Peak, which mixes the premium ready-to-drink tea with Simply Juice’s lemonade.    

Expanding upon earlier campaigns with Norm, the brand humorously celebrates the real moments that make life golden. Van Beek’s artful worldbuilding and clever comedic timing bolsters this theme, while the golden atmosphere unites and grounds the campaign.

The witty, if a bit silly, Norm comes to life across the five ads while he perfects his golf swing, looks to strike gold, and enjoys a tea party hosted by Mother Nature, all with a playful twinkle in his eye. Van Beek’s background in dual-reality comedy, like The Office Australia on Prime and What We Do in the Shadows on FX, is apparent throughout the expertly crafted campaign. 

“Being an actor myself, I have a deep understanding of the highs and lows of the job,” said van Beek. ”I’ve found my acting experience invaluable in directing other actors. Norm is fantastic - we love inspirational characters, but we love flawed, inspirational characters even more! I’m so happy with how the campaign turned out, and it was so great to work on.” 

Jackie van Beek is a multi-hyphenate director, writer, and actor from Aotearoa, New Zealand, with a sly sense of humor that fuels her creative work across film, television, and commercials. Her recent work includes the highly talked-about campaign for California Pizza Kitchen with Busy Philipps and other brand clients, including Tourism New Zealand, Electronic Arts, and SkyGo.

About Institute
Institute is an award-winning production company founded in 2019 by acclaimed filmmaker and photographer Lauren Greenfield and producer Frank Evers. With offices in the United States and the United Kingdom, Institute is known for its artist management of world-class visual storytellers and award-winning photographers, and for producing high-quality, multi-platform productions. http://institute.pictures

records.description:
The Guard Brothers, who are represented for commercial work through Merman, have directed the latest campaign from fiber internet provider Kinetic with McCann/Detroit. The campaign includes an anthemic hero spot highlighting its “Internet Better” brand promise and a comedy vignette, “Problems,” that humorously goads users who are still using cable online services instead of updating to fiber. The latter features a technician visiting a home that is tangled in wires with nerdy businessmen (the old cable company providers) hiding in a closet and camouflaged “hidden fees” lurking in bushes in the front yard. 

Tom and Charles Guard (The Guard Brothers) are highly sought after by advertisers and are well known for telling stories with scale, charm and a lightness of touch that has characterized their most iconic campaigns. They approach commercial-making with a cinematic eye and an uncanny ability to create narratives that are heartfelt, soulful and emotional. They have directed campaigns for Onstar, Toyota, Lexus, Sony Playstation, Nike, Nokia, Stella, Chevy, and GM among many others. Their work has been celebrated on many top advertising lists, and has garnered top prizes at industry award programs. Their Audi spot “Prom” was ranked among the most popular on the USA Today Ad Meter.
