records.title: Saved by the Box Tops
records.description:
Box Tops for Education is heading back to Bayside High with the cast of "Saved by the Bell" to celebrate 30 years and nearly $1 billion raised for schools nationwide. General Mills, in partnership with Universal Products & Experiences, is reuniting the iconic cast for Saved by the Box Tops, a feel-good back-to-school campaign inspired by the beloved television series and the everyday impact of Box Tops for Education.

Now real-life parents, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani Thiessen, Mario Lopez and Elizabeth Berkley Lauren are back together at Bayside High, this time celebrating how Box Tops for Education has helped support classrooms across the country for the past three decades and encouraging families and community members to get involved.

"Any time the four of us get back together, it feels just as fun as meeting up at our lockers back in the day," said Gosselaar. "Since we're all parents now, getting to celebrate something that helps schools and students across the country makes it that much more meaningful."

Bringing the campaign beyond the halls of Bayside, General Mills will award $10,000 each to 30 schools in need to help fund programs and resources for the upcoming 2026–2027 school year. Families can also join in by earning cash for their schools and scoring free snacks through eligible Box Tops purchases.

"I've always admired Box Tops for Education's mission and its commitment to supporting students," said Elizabeth Berkley Lauren. "Heading back to the hallways to help a new generation of students access meaningful resources for the year ahead makes being part of Saved by the Box Tops even more special."

Since 1996, Box Tops for Education has helped families turn everyday grocery purchases into meaningful funding for their schools, contributing nearly $1 billion along the way. What began as a simple clip-and-send program has evolved into a modern digital platform, making it easier than ever to give back with a quick receipt scan.

"For 30 years, Box Tops for Education has helped schools access critical resources and opportunities to ensure students everywhere are set up for success," said Blake Holman, Senior Director of Brand Building at General Mills. "Reaching this milestone is a chance to celebrate everything Box Tops has helped make possible for schools over the years while reminding families how easy it is to give back with the products already in their carts."

The campaign comes to life through an ad campaign featuring the cast, and retro-inspired packaging on select General Mills products, including Annie's and Cheerios.

"What I love about Box Tops is that it fits into routines families already have like buying snacks, packing lunches and getting ready for the back-to-school season," said Thiessen. "It's nice knowing those everyday habits can also help give back."

Parents can easily earn cash for their schools — and even score free snacks for their families — by scanning receipts from participating products, turning everyday grocery trips into real support.

"I grew up on Cheerios — my family used to call me the 'cereal king,' so now as a parent being able to help families turn their own kids' love of cereal into an opportunity to give back to schools is incredible," said Lopez. "Fusing products I've loved since childhood with a reunion of some of my favorite people, made this experience special."

Fans can learn more about Saved by the Box Tops, explore participating products and download the app at BoxTops4Education.com. Follow along on Box Tops For Education (@btfe) on Instagram for updates and more throughout the back-to-school season.

records.title: Savor More
records.description:
fairlife is launching a new campaign that spotlights the ritual of enjoying a milk moment. This campaign invites consumers to rethink milk and shift the perception that all milk tastes the same.

The campaign highlights how fairlife’s richer taste and enhanced nutrition elevate daily rituals and shared moments with loved ones. To crystalize this strategy, the campaign tells the stories of the milk moments consumers engage with most often: slow motion pours over a bowl of cereal; the ultra-close up product macro shot of a creamy plume of coffee; and the delicious satisfaction of a glass of chocolate milk.

Developed in partnership with its creative agency of record, Doner, the work arrives as fairlife continues its momentum as the fastest growing value added dairy brand, surpassing legacy competitors and becoming the category leader in 2025 and the #1 most trusted value added dairy brand. 

Four :15 spots sit at the center of the “Savor More” campaign. You can view “Berry Smoothie,” “Cereal,” “Chocolate Milk,” and “Coffee” here. The work is live today, February 11, across TV, OTT, social, and ecomm and shopper.

records.title: Schedule the Sun
records.description:
Magnum is once again challenging the ice cream category’s winter slowdown with the launch of the latest evolution of its ‘Find Your Summer’, created by LOLA Madrid, part of Omnicom Advertising Group.  

This winter, the brand goes further, introducing “Schedule the Sun” a simple way for people to capture sunny moments: by booking them directly into their calendars. Through a discount, the campaign tempts consumers to allow calendar events every time the sun is forecast to be out in their areas, turning a fleeting winter craving into a scheduled indulgence. 

Rolling out across the UK, France and China, the campaign spans print, social, digital and DOOH, as the brand continues its mission to drive ice cream sales during the winter months and challenge entrenched perceptions of seasonality.

Originally conceived by LOLA Madrid as a proactive challenge to the ice cream industry’s long-accepted winter sales decline – and the belief that ice cream is strictly seasonal – Find Your Summer reframed summer as a feeling rather than a temperature, positioning Magnum as an all-year source of indulgent pleasure. The 2024 campaign went on to win the Outdoor Grand Prix at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity, recognised for its striking simplicity and craft.

With “Schedule the Sun”, Magnum evolves the platform while maintaining the distinctive visual identity that defines it. The new campaign comprises six films and six photographic executions, developed in collaboration with acclaimed photographer Leslie Zhang. Produced entirely in black and white, the work uses light and shadow to create elegant, intimate scenes in which rays of winter sunlight fall across a diverse cast of characters, forming shapes that subtly evoke the iconic Magnum silhouette.

The creative builds on the insight that consumers often deny themselves simple pleasures in colder months due to the perception that ice cream is reserved for summer. By visually linking a fleeting beam of sunlight with the sensory pleasure of biting into a Magnum, the campaign reinforces the idea that “summer” can be found in small, everyday moments – regardless of the season.

The campaign launches across leading fashion and lifestyle media, film, social channels including Instagram, YouTube and Pinterest, and DOOH placements in the UK, France and China. In France, activity coincides with Paris Fashion Week, reinforcing Magnum’s longstanding connection with fashion and culture and ensuring visibility during one of the season’s most influential moments.

records.description: Secret Agent parodies high-stakes spy thrillers to showcase travel management. A suave agent in a tense interrogation room avoids a crisis, not with gadgets, but by effortlessly booking a flight and vegan meal via the platform. records.title: See how we can cut your bill.
records.campaign_title: See how we can cut your bill.
records.description:
Consumer Cellular and Ted Danson are back—and this time, they’ve brought oversized piggy banks, a money-blowing machine, even golf legend Fred Couples, and a whole lot of savings.

On May 19, the wireless brand is launching a new campaign in partnership with creative AOR THE MAYOR featuring the ever-affable Ted Danson, aimed squarely at helping Americans 50+ save on their wireless bills.

Including three national spots running across CTV and socials, the campaign helps potential and current customers realize that CCI offers a smarter, more affordable alternative to traditional wireless carriers.

In spots like “Money Blower,” “Piggy Bank,” and “Date Night,” Ted Danson uses oversized props and playful scenarios to dramatize the savings message with a visual punch. A giant piggy bank flows with a never-ending wave of quarters from savings. A swirling money-blowing machine showers a cargo shorts-wearing customer with savings. With his signature mix of warmth and wit, Danson begs the question that consumers stuck in carrier cruise control must ask themselves: “What am I even paying for?”

Consumer Cellular has also tapped golf icon Fred Couples to get in on the fun, targeting golf enthusiasts specifically with ‘Save Your Greens for the Greens’, showing consumers in two national spots that switching to CCI could mean saving enough for an extra round of golf each month.

In “Extra Round,” Fred Couples gets his solo moment to celebrate all the joys of golf while explaining that switching wireless carriers means saving green, for the green. 

The spot titled “Ted & Fred” shows Fred transported to Ted’s orange-hued CCI world via golf cart and tries out Ted’s role of CCI spokesperson in his best announcer voice, which Ted graciously gave his blessing for, to share that switching from Big Wireless to Consumer Cellular could save enough for extra rounds of golf each month. The two then cement their newfound friendship with matching Ted & Fred T-Shirts (and presumably drive off together into the sunset).

‘Save Your Green for the Greens’ comes on the heels of CCI’s recent NASCAR “Half-Suit” campaign which seamlessly merged the wireless carrier’s product benefit into NASCAR culture and fandom. 
Together, all five executions bring to life the campaign’s unifying message: “See how we can cut your bill." And the work is grounded in real consumer insight. While the 50+ audience is savvy about saving in most parts of their lives, they often overlook their phone bill. With 63% of Big Wireless customers having stayed with the same carrier for over five years—and 71% saying they “probably won’t switch”—Consumer Cellular is making the case that it's time to rethink the default. 

THE MAYOR and CCI’s ongoing partnership once again showcases a successful celebrity-based campaign that feels both aspirational and relatable. THE MAYOR has worked in partnership with CCI since early 2024 to support the brand in their mission to be the most beloved wireless company in the nation.

records.title: See Where Music Takes You
records.description:
TikTok has partnered with AKQA’s São Paulo studio AKQA Casa to launch its first-ever large-scale campaign dedicated to the music experience on TikTok: "See Where Music Takes You."
“See Where Music Takes You” is an immersive campaign that reinforces TikTok’s role as the world’s leading destination for music discovery and cultural connection. As well as being a platform which helps fans discover their new favourite artists and tracks, TikTok invites users to shape music trends in real time - reviving classics, launching breakout artists, and creating viral moments that resonate globally. The campaign celebrates TikTok’s transformative power to turn everyday listeners into active participants in music culture, amplified by features like 'Add to Music App', which helps you save music you discover on TikTok to your favorite music streaming service, making discovery feel personal, intuitive, and endlessly shareable.
At the heart of this campaign is TikTok’s undeniable influence on the global music landscape. Since the global launch of the 'Add to Music App' in 2024, the feature has been used to save over a billion tracks to music streaming services - and generated billions more streams - cementing its role as the industry's engine driving music discovery and engagement. In fact, 84% of all songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 Chart last year first gained traction on TikTok.
The campaign spotlights how TikTok users are music superfans, connecting with each other through content, discovering emerging talent, fueling viral hits, and outspending the average listener on merchandise and paid streaming. It’s more than a platform - it’s where music movements begin.
AKQA led the campaign concept, tagline development, and the creation of supporting digital and social assets, along with a hero film directed by Nabil Elderkin, known for his work with prominent artists such as Dua Lipa, Tyla and Kendrick Lamar. The campaign features Ravyn Lenae’s hit “Love Me Not” which takes center stage in the campaign, having gone viral on TikTok, launching her career and propelling her into the charts worldwide.
Renato Zandoná, CCO AKQA, said: "We are incredibly proud to have partnered with TikTok on this project. This campaign isn't just about showcasing music; it's about illustrating the profound, interactive relationship users create with music on TikTok. We aimed to capture the unique energy of the platform – where a sound can spark a global trend, and every user can be a part of shaping music culture. It's a testament to TikTok's innovative spirit and its commitment to fostering genuine connection through sound."
Zuber Mohammed, Global Head of Consumer Marketing at TikTok, said: "TikTok is where music comes alive, where trends are born, and where artists and their fans connect directly with each other in truly authentic ways. With 'See Where Music Takes You,' we are celebrating the vibrant, inclusive music culture that our global community has built. This campaign reinforces our commitment to being the leading destination for music discovery and the ultimate launchpad for artists, music and trends."
"See Where Music Takes You" marks a significant milestone for TikTok, reinforcing its commitment to being the ultimate destination for music discovery and a vibrant ecosystem where music is not just consumed, but created, shared, and lived.
"See Where Music Takes You" launches today on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube.

records.title: Seems harmless
records.description: This campaign, developed for the City Hall of Joinville, Santa Catarina, Brazil, shows the other side of electronic cigarettes, the side that no one sees or pays attention to, the harmful side. We counter the glamorization of their use. We deconstruct the idea that electronic cigarettes are safe or fun, with the aim of directly influencing the behavior of young people, encouraging the public to reflect and reconsider their choices.

records.title: Send Face Pics Instead
records.description: MANSCAPED®, the global men’s grooming company and lifestyle consumer brand, is encouraging men to raise their cameras and think twice before hitting send with its newest campaign, “Send Face Pics Instead™.” As the company continues to expand its product line beyond the groin, it’s helping men do the same – equipping them with the tools to mancare their everywhere™ and the confidence to love the results. In the past, guys felt more comfortable taking a “down there” pic than showing their faces. The message now? With the right tools, men can confidently Send Face Pics Instead.

records.title: Serious Wine. Unserious Name.
records.description:
When it comes to luxury wine, Cupcake Vineyards is serious. When it comes to their name, some consumers might just think otherwise. 

Which is why Erich & Kallman – the independent, award-winning agency recently appointed to oversee Cupcake and Franzia Wine’s creative – used their first campaign to humorously address the elephant in the room. Employing their signature wit, a series of three vignettes perfectly encapsulates Cupcake’s new tagline: “Serious wine. Unserious name.” 

A Clever Juxtaposition 

Each vignette features a suave, charismatic wine expert strolling through Cupcake’s lush vineyards, loftily describing its award-winning craftsmanship to triumphant music. And each time, an eavesdropper confused by the name “Cupcake” stops him in his tracks. In the spot “Really?,” for example, the record-scratch moment comes from a surprised vineyard worker who asks, “Sorry, what’d you say the wine is called?” Holding up the bottle, our expert awkwardly replies, “Cupcake, Cupcake Vineyards.” The worker doesn’t stop there. “They seriously call it Cupcake? Really? That’s got to be the silliest name for a wi—” Before he can finish, we cut to a glorious panoramic shot of the vineyard, our expert proudly touting the product.

“The name gave us so much to play with and we loved that the Cupcake team was game,” said Eric Kallman, Founder and Chief Creative Officer, Erich & Kallman. “Our campaign made self-deprecation a superpower, while driving the point that Cupcake’s quality is extremely serious, made from the highest quality grapes from the best wine regions worldwide.”

Three-part rollout 
The campaign includes two additional vignettes entitled “Horse” and “Name.” All three just went live via digital video, connected TV, and social media. They were directed by Andrew Laurich and produced by Contagious LA.

“Keeping in line with our promise of sparking joy, Erich & Kallman created a fun, light-hearted, tone, while demonstrating Cupcake’s award-winning craftsmanship and quality,” said The Wine Group CMO Helen Kurz. “These vignettes strike just the right balance of levity and seriousness. We love the new tagline and the campaign and we’re excited for what’s next.”

records.title: Sharing Leads to More Sharing
records.description:
Red Baron is expanding its 'Sharing Leads to More Sharing' platform with a fresh campaign celebrating the launch of its Stuffed Crust Pizza. Rooted in the idea that pizza naturally brings people together, the new spots focus on the joy, connection, and even surprising revelations that can arise from sharing a slice. Rather than spotlighting only the product, the brand continues to highlight the heartfelt and humorous human moments that unfold around a communal meal, reinforcing pizza’s role as a catalyst for authentic connection.

Building on the platform’s record-breaking ROAS and Red Baron’s four-year streak as the top-selling frozen pizza in the U.S., the campaign uses comedic twists to amplify its message. The new ads feature unexpected groups — such as 'UFC-Based' fighters and 'Ghost Hunters' — who, once gathered around pizza, drop their guarded personas and share personal truths. In the 'UFC-Based' spot “Octagon,” a post-fight gathering turns from a show of toughness into an unexpectedly tender exchange, illustrating the campaign’s core belief: sharing pizza leads to sharing more of ourselves.

records.title: Crema Collection
records.description:
From production company Good Times comes a new campaign for Starbucks’ Crema Collection Premium Instant Coffee. Directed by Shelley Lewis, the ads highlight the answer to any afternoon slump. 

The campaign illustrates how Starbucks Crema is a beautifully simple and delicious solution to a universal problem. Beyond the usual, functional mid-day lift, Crema is a little touch of velvety joy to bring anyone back to themselves, and back to the task at hand. The campaign and the product are both deliciously simple and satisfying and Lewis delivers the narrative with a contemporary spin and an authentic spirit. 

“This script was a rare opportunity to bring character and style together, with a universal moment of humanity,” said Lewis. “I loved building this strong, simple story in a playful and contemporary way. It’s also special because it’s my first official campaign with my new production company, Good Times.” 

Shelley Lewis takes a striking visual approach to directing, often incorporating humor. Her intuitive approach to understanding brand ethos and audience sentiment has earned her partnerships with top-tier brands across multiple industries. Driven to tell stories about characters that defy norms and showcase diverse voices, her work has earned recognition from Cannes Lions, One Show, Clios, shots, and the Webbys, among others.

Production company Good Times brings a stylish yet comprehensive approach to innovative content creation, non-traditional/experiential exploration, and fully integrated campaign executions. With a diverse creative community of talented directors, digital creators, writers, tech innovators, and marketers, Good Times produces work that transcends boundaries, from documentaries and independent features to fashion shows, live events, and traditional commercial production. More than a name, Good Times is a mantra, and that spirit of resourceful positivity helps continue the company’s impeccable reputation for successfully and efficiently executing projects of all sizes.

records.title: Shining for Halloween
records.description: For Govee’s "Shining With Govee" Halloween 2025 campaign, we brought a full cinematic flair to the world of smart lighting. Across four themed films, our team transformed ordinary homes into eerie, movie-ready showcases—where every flicker, hue, and glow told its own spooky story. From fog-filled driveways to dancing spectral lights, the series celebrates Govee’s wide range of outdoor and indoor lighting, proving that with the right setup, you can turn your home into the ultimate haunted spectacle.

records.title: Shocking. In a good way.
records.description:
To close the year with impact, Fizz leaned into one of its most iconic symbols: the lightning bolt. A natural metaphor for speed, power and simplicity, it became the backbone of a campaign that made one thing clear: Switching to Fizz is shockingly easy. The campaign focused on three core messages:

- A striking phone offer, with savings of up to 60% on mobile plans for 24 months.
- Reliable coverage at a low price, especially in provinces outside Quebec.
- A rewards program that keeps hitting with more perks.

With bold, repurposed visuals, short-form bilingual videos and targeted digital executions, Fizz delivered a cohesive, high-energy campaign that stayed true to its offbeat, fun-loving brand signature.

records.title: Simply Sweet
records.description:
Here is the creative for Gay Lea Foods Co-operative Limited’s newest product launch: chocolate whipped cream! 

The inspiration behind the spot was to illustrate how sweet things can be integrated in one’s everyday life simply - because treating yourself doesn’t need candlelight and couture, just a spoon and a can! 

Everything from the set location to the outfits screamed luxury; we open in a lavish living room of an apartment with orchestral music playing in the background. We cut to between dreamy, soft-focused, slow-panning shots of our lead actress draped elegantly on a chaise lounge. We see the elegance of the room, her dress, hair, and earrings. 

Then, we cut to her in her real kitchen, a less extravagant but still aspirational room. She’s now wearing trendy athleisure wear, she's still holding the spoon and can, and we see her enjoy the treat. The contrast between the high fashion “treat for the senses” scenes and the relaxed kitchen scene underscores that sweet indulgence doesn’t need to be grandiose or fancy, it’s for everyday moments, and those moments are the kind we can’t wait to return to.

records.title: Smart Moves
records.description:
Did you know Franzia Wines have the most consumer loyalty among alcoholic beverage drinkers, topping power brands like Bud, Coors, and Hennessey? That’s just one of the little-known facts about Franzia, the #1 wine brand for 28 consecutive years. But how to inform and reach today's younger generation of imbibers – who are presented with countless options in the wine aisle?

To make the best choice crystal clear, Erich & Kallman—the award-winning agency recently appointed creative lead for The Wine Group, which includes Cupcake and Franzia—produced a series of witty new spots that demonstrate why choosing Franzia is a “smart move,” followed by a hilarious second choice that’s, well, “not as a smart.” (One box of Franzia holds six bottles worth of wine and costs about the price of one.)

Sidesplitting decisions
For example, in the:15 spot “Lasagna,” a man pours two glasses of Franzia during an intimate dinner with his beloved. “Smart move,” comments a narrator. Realizing with horror that she has cleaned her plate entirely, exclaiming, “All done!” the narrator then explains: “Hiding an engagement ring in your girlfriend’s lasagna? Not as smart.”

“Clearly, Franzia has a large, loyal following who keep making the smart decision to choose it,” said Eric Kallman, Co-Founder and Chief Creative Officer at Erich & Kallman. “How better to showcase just how smart it is than following it with a really terrible not-so-smart move? Working with The Wine Group has been a delight and we're thrilled they’re letting us have fun with it.”

Two additional spots, “Parrot” and “Game Night” express similar humor. 

“Nothing works harder than humor to make consumers interested and engaged,” said Helen Kurtz, CMO at The Wine Group. “And no one does humor better than Erich & Kallman. We love the work they’ve done with both Franzia and Cupcake – bringing to life the benefits of these brands with their signature, clever ideas.”

records.title: Smell Goes a Long Way
records.description:
Old Spice, the iconic personal care brand, today launches its most significant UK brand campaign, “Smell Goes a Long Way.” This isn’t just about smelling good; it’s Old Spice showing that a truly great long-lasting scent gives young men an unexpected edge in life, transforming everyday challenges into triumphs. 

Created with RCP, the campaign shows that manhood is a mindset, not a milestone you simply reach. It champions the underdog, injecting relatable, UK-centric humour to connect with the British experience. 
Exclusive Films: Smell Goes a Long Way in British Summer

Old Spice kicks off with two exclusive UK film shorts demonstrating scent's game-changing power, directed by Fatal Farm’s Jeffrey Max and produced by Agile:

"Smell Like It Went In": Our hero shanks a crucial penalty. But he smells so good with the Old Spice Sport Power collection, the ref thinks he must have scored. It’s a comedic take on turning blunders into triumphs.

"Smell Like You Found the Right Tent": Navigating the chaos of summer festivals? With the Old Spice Rockstar Collection, our hero instantly belongs with his surprising new crew. The ultimate festival life hack, keeping him fresh all day and all night.

These high-impact films debut during the World Cup in July, igniting a comprehensive TV, digital, social, and influencer blitz. Further football and festival-themed content will follow throughout summer.

Ella Salkeld, UK Personal Care Brand Director at Procter & Gamble, said: “Old Spice is building real momentum in the UK and ‘Smell Goes a Long Way’ gives us a brand platform to connect with young men in a culturally relevant way. It celebrates the confidence that comes from knowing you smell fresh 24/7 and shows how that small advantage can make a big difference. We're proud to be the UK's #1 men's deodorant stick, reflecting our strong connection with consumers and our significant contribution to the category's growth with our perfume quality scents.”

Mike Plumridge, creative director at RCP, added: “Life doesn’t always go smoothly. But when you smell great, you carry yourself differently, and that can change how others see you. We loved the idea that something as simple as smelling fresh can quietly tip the odds in your favour. Young men don’t need to have everything figured out, but they can smell like they do.”

Availability: NEW Old Spice Sport Power and Rockstar Collection, and other ranges are available now at major UK retailers (Tesco, Boots, Amazon, Sainsbury's, Morrisons) and online.

records.title: Smell Like Your Ex(foliating Body Wash)
records.campaign_title: Smell Like Your Ex(foliating Body Wash)
records.description:
Suave has launched Smell Like Your Ex(foliating Body Wash), a new social-first campaign created in partnership with global social-first creative agency Born Social. The push supports the launch of Suave’s new exfoliating body wash collection, marking the 89-year-old brand’s inaugural social-first campaign.

The campaign signals a clear evolution in Suave’s marketing playbook to social- and culture-first storytelling to power the launch of its newest Exfoliating Body Wash. The work spotlights the brand’s commitment to quality and accessibility, bringing Suave’s There’s More To It positioning to life within this fast-growing product category.

Built on a cultural insight gleaned from social listening, the campaign plays into the shared experience of exes and the lingering clothing and scent that instantly brings old relationships back to life. The central idea encourages letting go of your ex - starting with their hoodie - and replacing it with a scent that’s actually worth keeping. It sits at the intersection of emotional baggage, Gen Z’s interests in thrift culture, and the exfoliating, scent-led benefit of the product. The thrift concept also nods to Suave’s long-standing focus on everyday affordability.

“This campaign marks an important moment for Suave as we launch our new exfoliating body wash collection and take a modern approach to connecting with Gen Z by hacking into their feeds through entertainment,” said Tina Ghory, Senior Director, Consumer Engagement at Suave. “Smell Like Your Ex(foliating Body Wash) reflects how we’re evolving as a brand and showing up differently, speaking the language of this audience and bringing our There’s More To It positioning to life in a way that feels relevant, accessible and native to social.”

The campaign launches with a hero social film and three vignettes set inside a local thrift store called The Ex-Change. Shot like a throwback, homemade thrift-store commercial, the film follows a deadpan store representative as she wanders the aisles addressing the camera. Customers line up clutching items left behind by their exes, from stained overalls to oversized novelty items, as tongue-in-cheek sections categorize different “ex” archetypes. The film culminates with a customer trading in her ex’s hoodies and receiving a fresh hoodie and Suave Exfoliating Body Wash, ending on a knowingly awkward product reveal that positions the body wash as an empowered upgrade to smelling like your ex.

Directed by Tessa Greenberg, selected for her comedy and improv experience, the campaign prioritized casting social comedians rather than traditional actors, with time built in for ad-libbing and freestyling. The talent reflects a diverse range of backgrounds, relationships and expressions, with Greenberg closely involved in casting and performance shaping throughout the process.

“This campaign shows what it looks like when social leads the thinking from the start,” added Paddy Smith, Chief Creative Officer at Born Social. “By treating social as a space for brand building, not just content distribution, we were able to ground the idea in Gen Z culture and shape the work in a way that feels native to how people actually engage with brands today.”

Visually, the work is defined by heightened color drawn from the four product fragrances – Strawberry Delight, Citrus Blossom, Pistachio Cream, and Vanilla Suede - with the different scents amplified through art direction, color and texture. The campaign includes a launch film for social, and a suite of supporting social-first assets.

records.title: Smile Üp
records.description:
To bring a global brand into South Korea, GUT Singapore didn't import a campaign, but built an entire brand world using a mark sitting inside NÜTRL's name all along.

The idea started with an untapped detail: the umlaut (Ü) in NÜTRL’s name. Reinterpreted as a smile, GUT Singapore transformed a simple typographic mark into NÜTRL’s defining visual signature, giving the global brand a warm, recognizable identity as it introduced itself to Korean consumers. 

That smile scaled into NÜTRL’s brand platform for Korea, Smile Üp. More than a campaign line, it expressed the brand’s mission in the market: to bring a little lightness and a little more reason to smile to Koreans. 

This came to life through an original music video featuring S.COUPS and MINGYU, where the artists don’t just endorse NÜTRL from the outside, but become part of the brand universe itself. By reimagining their hit single “For you” as “For Ü”, the music video introduces NÜTRL through music, entertainment and a vibrant visual universe inspired by the drink’s light and refreshing formulation and personality.

“For Ü” expands NÜTRL’s identity into a world filled with playful visual cues and recognizable Korean cultural references, giving the brand a distinctly Korean expression without losing the identity that travels with it globally. The result gives fans multiple ways to discover NÜTRL, combining functional product storytelling with entertainment people would choose to watch and share.

The music video sits at the heart of a social-first play, supported by out-of-home and on-ground activations, helping establish NÜTRL in one of Korea's fastest-growing and most competitive ready-to-drink categories.

Alongside the campaign, GUT Singapore led the redesign of NÜTRL's packaging for the Korean market, working with GUT Design to create a cohesive identity across every touchpoint.

“Korea is one of the most exciting and competitive ready-to-drink markets in the world, and we wanted to enter with impact. There was no better way to do that than collaborating with artists who genuinely shape the culture. Working with S.COUPS and MINGYU gave NÜTRL a level of cultural credibility and energy few launches ever get, positioning the brand right where music and culture meet.” said Alex Lambrecht, Marketing Vice President at Anheuser-Busch InBev.

"This launch was about much more than introducing a new drink," said Carlos Camacho, Chief Creative Officer at GUT Singapore. "The smile hidden in NÜTRL's own name gave us a way in, and music let us build a world people would choose to spend time in, rather than an ad they'd skip. Everything, down to turning “For you” into “For Ü”, came from that one idea."

The campaign marks another collaboration between GUT Singapore and leading Korean entertainment IPs and personalities, with past collaborations including Netflix’s Culinary Class Wars 2, Napoli Matfia, Moon Sang Hoon and more. Rather than announcing NÜTRL’s arrival with a conventional launch, the agency has applied its pop-culture-first instinct for a market entry, building a world fans across South Korea, Asia and beyond will choose to step into.

GUT Singapore x NÜTRL “Smile Up”

records.title: Smiles Built for Life
records.description:
ClearChoice Dental Implant Center® today announced the launch of its bold new national brand campaign, Smiles Built for Life, a fully integrated platform anchored in one powerful truth: ClearChoice is one of the leading providers of permanent teeth the same day of surgery - backed by decades of expertise and a Lifetime Warranty on premium arches.

For millions of Americans living with severe dental issues, a smile can be a daily source of stress, embarrassment, or isolation. Smiles Built for Life meets patients in that moment, with a message of real hope. The campaign is designed to reinforce ClearChoice as the pioneer of same-day, full-arch dental implant treatment, offering not just speed, but peace of mind through a permanent, personalized solution.

“This is about changing the conversation,” said Marcelle Parrish, Chief Marketing and Commercial Officer at ClearChoice. “We’ve seen new players enter the category with big promises. But we believe no one has the scale, clinical model, or experience to deliver what we do—permanent teeth, same day, done right. Our patients want to stop worrying about their smile. This campaign shows them they finally can.”

The campaign is headlined by a national broadcast spot titled “Voice of Doubt,” which gives emotional voice to the inner concerns and hesitations of people living with tooth loss. The ad’s tone is both raw and hopeful, inviting viewers to imagine a different future, and a different kind of provider.

To bring this vision to life, ClearChoice partnered with independent creative agency Geletka+. Geletka+ led creative strategy, concept development, video production, and photography. The process was deeply collaborative, with input from patients, doctors, researchers, and internal teams alike.

The result is a fast-turn, 360 campaign with thousands of assets spanning TV, digital, social, print, and in-center content, each tailored to engage patients at key decision-making moments.

“This wasn’t just about making ads,” said John Geletka, Founder and CXO of Geletka+. “It was about building a brand platform that speaks directly to real human concerns and offers a permanent solution. ClearChoice is uniquely built to deliver on that promise, and we wanted the work to reflect that with emotional honesty and bold simplicity.”

Campaign Highlights:
●      “Same Day, Done Right”: Permanent teeth on the same day of surgery—backed by a Lifetime Warranty on premium arches and prosthodontist-led expertise.
●      No Compromises: Every smile is custom-designed and delivered in an all-in-one center, with no shortcuts or hidden costs.
●      Emotional Resonance: Campaign creative reflects deep audience insight, tested messaging, and the lived experience of ClearChoice patients.
●      Fast, Collaborative Execution: Entire campaign developed and launched in under 60 days—a modern model of agile, insight-driven marketing.

Smiles Built for Life marks the first major campaign produced in partnership with Geletka+, and sets the tone for a bold new chapter in ClearChoice’s growth and category leadership.

records.title: Smooth Break
records.description:
In a category dominated by wholesome smiles and morning sunshine, nutpods today announces a new campaign starring a pair of mustachioed men in silk suits who live in your fridge and sing about your coffee. Developed in partnership with CALLEN, the non-dairy creamer brand is turning a mundane morning moment into a full-blown musical interlude.

Titled “Smooth Break” the hero 30-second spot opens on a dreary breakfast table, with a man droning on about status meetings and Q3. The moment his partner pours nutpods into her coffee, the fridge swings open and out pops an 80s-style mustachioed duo, tossing confetti and belting out: “Smooth and creamy, creamy and smooth.” 

She puts down her coffee, and just as quickly as they appear, they snap back into silence, break character, and awkwardly begin sweeping up the mess while whispering “Go, go, go” to each other as they crawl back into the fridge. As soon as she takes another sip, they burst out again with another smooth serenade.

The tagline, “Have yourself a delicious moment,” drives home the idea that nutpods can inject a bit of joy and absurdity into an otherwise dull daily ritual. A :15 and two :06s accompany the campaign. 

The campaign is live today, June 2, across CTV, digital and social.

records.title: Solo tú, Papá: El arte detrás de la nostalgia
records.campaign_title: Solo tú, Papá: El arte detrás de la nostalgia
records.description:
La publicidad emocional no es nueva, pero lograr que se sienta auténtica en la era del hiperdigitalismo es un desafío titánico. Al adentrarnos en la temporada del Día del Padre, las marcas suelen recurrir a los clichés de siempre. Sin embargo, Almacenes Deprati, de la mano de la productora Fabryca y la creatividad de la agencia independiente BBA, ha decidido romper el molde visual y sonoro con su nueva campaña: “Solo tú, Papá”.

La propuesta es un homenaje al rol paterno y a su vez una masterclass de cómo el despliegue de medios 360 y la artesanía audiovisual pueden convivir para generar un impacto memorable.

Un viaje sonoro a la memoria colectiva
El corazón de la campaña late al ritmo de la nostalgia ecuatoriana. La pieza utiliza como hilo conductor "Solo Tú", en la voz del cantautor ecuatoriano Andreu Montesco que quedó inmortalizado en la memoria sonora del país gracias a la icónica versión tropical de Don Medardo y sus Players. 

La música deja de ser un acompañamiento para convertirse en el narrador emocional de una historia que celebra "esas pequeñas cosas que solo un papá sabe hacer: proteger, aconsejar, hacer reír y estar siempre presente".

El Video Hero de la campaña destaca por una estética visual única. En un mercado saturado de texturas digitales hipernítidas, Fabryca apostó por la cinematografía de época utilizando cámaras modernas equipadas con los legendarios Helios 44-2, lentes soviéticos fabricados originalmente a partir de los años 60.

Estas ópticas vintage son codiciadas en el cine contemporáneo por su imperfección técnica y su particular construcción basada en el diseño óptico alemán Biotar. Su característica más famosa es el swirly bokeh (un desenfoque de fondo circular o en forma de remolino) y un contraste suave con destellos (flares) cálidos y dramáticos al recibir luz directa.

Para elevar la apuesta visual de "Solo tú, Papá", el equipo de producción diseñó y creo filtros de forma artesanal. Tras múltiples pruebas de cámara, estos elementos físicos antepuestos al lente refractaron la luz de una manera única, logrando una textura orgánica, un desenfoque radial cálido y sumamente cinematográfico que evoca la estética de los recuerdos familiares. El resultado es una pieza audiovisual que se siente como un álbum de fotos vivo.

Deprati demuestra con "Solo tú, Papá" que el retail tradicional puede conectar desde la fibra más sensible. Al fusionar la moda, una joya del cancionero ecuatoriano y una fotografía técnica impecable, la marca firma una de las campañas más potentes del año en el mercado nacional.

records.title: Soup
records.description:
All you need is love, Asian wisdom, and mobile money.
And these ads? They're living proof.

The story drops you right into ancient dynasties, where our heroes are in a serious bind. But don't worry—before you can say "ancient drama," the Momo mobile money app swoops in and saves the day. 

It's like a time-traveling genie for your wallet.
This campaign blends old-world settings, contemporary humor and storytelling.

records.title: Soup Drops are back
records.description:
Progresso Soup Drops are back just in time for cold and flu season — and for any day that just sucks. After selling out in just minutes last January, the soup you can suck on now debuts the first-ever Progresso Soup Drops Variety Can featuring three of Progresso’s most iconic soup flavors.

Returning for year two and perfectly timed to National Soup Month, there's a Progresso Soup, and now a Soup Drop, to help turn any moment from "ugh" to "ahh":

· Reach for the iconic Chicken Noodle Soup Drop on sick days

· The comforting new Tomato Basil Soup Drop when it's snowy, gray and gross outside

· Or the hearty new Beef Pot Roast Soup Drop for the long, draining days that leave you running on empty

Each Soup Drop hits on the flavors fans know and love from Progresso, and this year, they're bringing the heat — literally. The new Progresso Soup Drops deliver a feeling of warmth in your mouth, making every drop taste even more like a bowl of Progresso Soup.

The limited-edition Progresso Soup Drops Variety Cans go on sale Thursday, Jan. 15 at 9 a.m. ET — and every Thursday for the remainder of January at 9 a.m. ET (while supplies last). Visit ProgressoSoupDrops.com to learn more, including how to get your hands on the exclusive Variety Cans available only at Walmart.com. Each order includes one Progresso Soup Drops Variety Can containing individually wrapped Soup Drops in all three flavors, plus a can of Progresso Chicken Noodle Soup. This year’s bundle retails for $2.97, about the price of a can of Progresso Soup, with free shipping for Walmart+ members or on all orders from Walmart.com over $35.

“Cold and flu season sucks, and the only way to combat this time of year is with the flavors of Progresso — whether that’s in a comforting bowl or through the joy of soup you can suck on,” said María Carolina Comings, VP, Business Unit Director for Progresso at General Mills. “This year, Progresso Soup Drops deliver more fun, more flavor and more comfort when you need it most.”

Get your own Progresso Soup Drops online and stock up on your favorite Progresso Soups at retailers and grocery stores nationwide. For more information, visit Progresso.com or follow @Progresso on Instagram and TikTok.

records.title: Speciality
records.description: The primary target group of Kaufland is families. That is why we used an insight every parent knows well: in the kitchen, you turn into a full-fledged chef, but no matter how hard you try to sell your creation to the kids, your child has their own taste preferences. And it really doesn’t take much for them to completely dismiss all your effort — one look and a splash of ketchup. But at Kaufland, that’s no problem at all; everyone can find something they like here.

records.title: Splash of Color
records.description:
To match the glamour of the Oscars red carpet on March 2, award-winning, San Francisco-based agency Erich & Kallman–AdAdge’s 2024 North American Small Agency of the Year–created a brand campaign for Empress 1908 Gin, the fastest growing and #1 ranked ultra-premium gin in the U.S. The :30 spot, entitled, “Splash of Color,” is Empress 1908 Gin’s award show debut and kickoff to the brand’s first-ever North America media campaign. 

Setting the scene
The spot opens in black and white with a chic, well-dressed woman quietly making her way to the bar before ordering an Empress & Tonic. The bartender grabs a bottle of Empress 1908 Indigo Gin–the only visual in bright technicolor–and starts pouring. As soon as the gin hits the glass, the vibrant motion of colors swirl dramatically, changing the surroundings. As the woman turns to face the room, the crowd is now suddenly colorful, stylish, and elegant, with everyone enjoying their own vibrant and beautiful Empress 1908 Gin cocktails.

“The black and white opening offers timelessness, while the introduction of color through Empress 1908 Indigo Gin immediately takes us into the present, with an elegant, modern-day celebration,” said Eric Kallman, Co-Founder and CCO, Erich & Kallman. “Since the ad is airing on Hollywood’s biggest night, we wanted it to reflect the height of glamour.” 

About the production 
Claire Arnold, the independent creative director, art director, filmmaker, and creative consultant based in London, directed “Splash of Color" and enlisted visually-driven production company La Pac, who operated in partnership with Arts & Sciences in Los Angeles.

About the campaign
The new “Make Life Extraordinary” campaign from Empress 1908 Gin launches with a media buy around the 97th Academy Awards featuring the “Splash of Color” spot. The cinematic spot dramatizes and brings to life how Empress 1908 Gin inspires the extraordinary–elevating everyday experiences with its sophistication and distinctiveness, as the campaign continues across TV, streaming, digital, social, OOH, and print through 2025. 

"Erich & Kallman didn’t just capture the look and flavor of Empress 1908 Gin — they brilliantly showcased how its striking presentation inspires a whole new style of cocktail creativity and enjoyment,” said Eric Dopkins, Founder and CEO of Milestone Brands. “For our Hollywood debut on the Oscars telecast, we wanted to create something that felt like a magnificent ode to cinema across the eras, which was achieved in a visually stunning way.”

records.title: Splashdown
records.description:
Budget Direct has launched the latest creative instalment in its highly successful Insurance Solved platform developed in collaboration with long-term agency partner 303.
Called Splashdown, the campaign is a satirical look at celebrity culture, portraying a glamorous group of space-tourists, and their hapless re-entry that crashes a suburban pool party. Amidst the selfies and comedic chaos, beloved super sleuths Sarge and his team, reassure the concerned homeowners that Budget Direct’s award-winning insurance has them covered.
The campaign will be seen across TV, radio, cinema, BVOD, SVOD, social and OOH.

records.title: Sprint
records.description:
Following the successful unveiling of Screwfix’s new brand platform, ‘No Stopping You’, on 10 October, the retailer today launches the second instalment of the campaign — ‘The New Recruit’, featuring Sir Mo Farah — created in partnership with M+C Saatchi Group UK, to promote Screwfix’s market-leading Sprint delivery service, offering customers delivery in as little as 20 minutes.

This latest 30-second ad forms the second part of the overarching ‘No Stopping You’ campaign, highlighting how Screwfix removes friction from the customer experience and demonstrates the brand’s commitment to making it as fast and simple as possible for tradespeople to get what they need. Featuring Sir Mo Farah, who this time, turns his attention to the Sprint delivery service — but, true to his running roots, he humorously takes the job a little too literally and sets off on foot to deliver the order himself. The playful spot brings the speed and efficiency of the Sprint service to life — showing that, with Screwfix, there really is no stopping the trade.

records.title: "Square Up" - Locally's D5 Store announcement
records.description: This 30 second spot announces a fashion retailer's brand new flagship store in an unconventional way, designed to hook the viewer (pun intended).

records.title: Start With Swisspers
records.description: No matter what makeup you put on, when you take it off, start with Swisspers cotton products.

records.title: Starwash
records.description: On the heels of this year’s Super Bowl ads buzz, Carl’s Jr. just launched a bold campaign starring Paris Hilton that blends AI technology with Y2K nostalgia in a reimaging of her iconic 2005 Carl’s Jr. burger commercial. The 30-second ad features the real Paris and her AI clones promoting the brand’s BOGO $1 Famous Star deal, served up with lots of iconic star power.

records.title: Step Inside Intelligence
records.description: When everyone is talking about AI, it can be difficult to separate possibility from practical value. Created for Cognizant, this film showcases the launch of the AI Innovation Studio at Barangaroo. An immersive environment designed to help organisations move beyond the hype and explore how artificial intelligence can create meaningful business outcomes.

records.title: Stay cool when strange things happen
records.campaign_title: Stay cool when strange things happen
records.description: Trident, in partnership with Stranger Things, launched a special-edition packaging to celebrate the premiere of the show’s final season on Netflix. This was just the starting point of an integrated campaign, featuring audiovisual content for TV and digital platforms, as well as photography and 3D executions for OOH and static formats.

records.title: Stuff It.  Live More.
records.description:
Meet Bev and Barry - the loveable stars of Storage King's category-breaking new ‘Stuff It. Live More.’ brand platform, set to transform the way Aussies and Kiwis look at storage.

Developed by Ogilvy and live this week, ‘Stuff It. Live More.’ launches with a campaign that shows how storage can be more than a transactional, last-minute solution, and instead a powerful life tool that creates space for what truly matters.  It will be seen from this week in Australia and New Zealand across TV, YouTube, OOH, Radio, online and instore.

Ogilvy Creative Director Shaun Branagan said the new brand platform and supporting campaign positions Storage King as an enabler of a fuller life, rather than just a provider of space. Using Bev and Barry in the new campaign executions was an opportunity to “show real characters with main character energy living out their dreams unconstrained by their ‘stuff’,” he explained.

records.title: Style It Out
records.description:
F&F is proving its style credentials and stepping away from supermarket fashion clichés in its latest 'Style It Out' campaign, created by BBH. The campaign builds on the momentum of the initial launch earlier this year and showcases the brand's latest Autumn/Winter collection.

The campaign sees the return of legendary photographer and Emmy-winning filmmaker Alex Prager to direct the new spots. Known for her distinctive cinematic style, Prager injects a new energy and attitude into the brand, transforming everyday mishaps into stylish, iconic moments.

The 'Style It Out' platform is grounded in the relatable truth that life is full of awkward and messy situations. Instead of focusing on over-the-top confidence, the campaign champions composure, showing how F&F fashion and homewares can help people navigate life’s little challenges with style.

A leaky ceiling. An awkward moment in an elevator. A car breaking down. Kids going wild with crayons. These relatable scenarios all turn chaos into chic.

The integrated campaign is designed to appeal to F&F's core audience of women aged 35+, while also attracting a new generation of shoppers between 25 and 35. 

Felipe Serradourada Guimarães, BBH London ECD, said: “Another installment of Style It Out for F&F. A simple idea that keeps getting better with every execution. F&F is making the high street look like the catwalk.” 

Rachel Nooney, F&F brand and marketing director added: “This second campaign under our F&F brand platform ‘Style It Out’ continues to highlight the style and quality that is synonymous with the brand. These stunning films and stills showcase our ranges across F&F fashion and home lifestyle fused with real-life moments that our customers relate to.”

The campaign will run across TVC, VOD, OOH, print, social, radio, and digital channels in the UK and Ireland, for two months, media handled by EssenceMediaCom.

records.title: Style that Sticks
records.description:
To reframe Command's brand narrative, Colle McVoy’s insight was simple: people don’t just want tools, they want inspiration.

"Style that Sticks", a new global campaign, captures both what Command does and what this campaign is about. Literally, its products stick (strong, reliable, damage-free). But culturally, great style also sticks – it inspires, spreads, and gets replicated. The double meaning turns a functional product truth into a cultural one: Command doesn’t just help you hang things, it helps your style take hold, leaving an impression that lasts and sparking ideas that others want to take and make their own.

Command has an entire universe of products designed not just to hang, but to transform, unlocking endless decorating and organizing possibilities.

To address this head-on, this campaign showcases head-turning design moments that are so irresistible, people can’t help but want them for themselves.
The first piece of the campaign to go live is a :30 Halloween-themed spot, “Spideys,” which will run across TV, CTV, YouTube, and social.
"Bells" is the holiday execution of the Style that Sticks campaign, where a single spark of inspiration ignites bold, Command-powered design ideas that spread, adapt, and transform spaces everywhere.
"With 'Style that Sticks,' we’re redefining what Command stands for," says Tate Galvin, Vice President, Home Improvement, 3M. "This campaign marks an exciting evolution – showing how our products can unlock creativity and self-expression for consumers in everyday spaces. Colle McVoy helped us bring that vision to life in a way that feels bold, stylish, and deeply human."

Command and Colle McVoy created a cultural invitation to show how one person’s creative spark with Command Products can ignite another’s, and another’s, and another’s – until the ripple effect transforms entire spaces.

"This campaign is a game-changer for Command," says Tricia Lynch, Group Account Director at Colle McVoy. "'Style that Sticks' isn’t just a clever line – it’s a bold repositioning that transforms our brand from a functional tool to a design partner. We tapped into something powerful: people don’t just want damage-free solutions – they want design that speaks to them. This work captures that beautifully, showing how Command can be the spark behind everyday creativity that spreads."

records.title: Style Unpacked
records.description:
The WTA (Women’s Tennis Association) is launching ‘Style Unpacked’, a new fashion series created with fan-first creative agency, Run Deep. The series expands the WTA’s content offering and features four key players including Victoria Mboko and Camila Osorio.

Tennis and fashion have always been entwined, but looking great both on and off court isn't easy when you're an athlete traveling around the world, living out of a suitcase, and focused on performance.

Sarah Swanson, Chief Brand Officer, WTA Ventures said: “"Fans follow the WTA Tour all season long to watch WTA players compete and win, but the deeper connection comes from understanding who they are beyond the court. Content like Style Unpacked gives audiences a window into players’ personality, perspective, humor and vulnerability. By showcasing these athletes in conversation, we create moments of relatability and emotional connection, continuing to place women's tennis in the broader cultural conversation."

Kicking off with the Madrid Open, four WTA players were paired with a Madrid stylist to help them find their look for specific, off-court moments during the tournament. Andrea Neira fronts the episodes, and while in Madrid, stylist Antonia Payeras was brought in to help curate their looks. The players are also photographed by Sheila Velasco before leaving the studio, creating a suite of assets to be shared across WTA and player social and digital channels. The aim is to repeat this format across the different cities that the players travel to across the season. 

In the first episode, which debuts today, Colombian star Osorio discusses her own personal style before Payeras goes hunting for some dress options ahead of her red carpet attendance at the 2026 Laureus World Sports Awards.

Jodie Fullagar, co-founder of Run Deep added: “It was a privilege to work with the WTA and these incredible young players on an entertainment format that celebrates the fashion of the host tournament city, and shows fans a different side to their favourite WTA players; stylish, fun and playful… they absolutely shone”

From creative to production approach, the players are always at the center. With inclusive, female-first crews, the players felt their best, got comfortable and opened up beyond the expected athlete narratives.

Recognising that modern fandom is built on vulnerability over highlights, the partnership aims to bridge the gap between world-class athleticism and human relatability. The shift unveils a new perspective to the traditional, highly curated "glamour" portraits, instead with a raw, style-led narrative that prioritises self-expression over industry expectations, manifesting in the content series ‘Style Unpacked’.

The series was produced with Far Media and will be posted across YouTube and Instagram, as well as WTA broadcast partners.

records.title: Style your way out
records.description:
Tesco's fashion and homeware brand F&F is showcasing how it can help customers navigate summer travel in a new ad campaign created by BBH London.

The work marks the second year of F&F's 'Style It Out' brand platform, demonstrating how the brand can help consumers navigate life whilst giving it a new richer meaning.

The campaign is built around the idea that while summer holidays are the stuff of dreams, getting there can be a nightmare. F&F saw a golden opportunity to spotlight the messier side of travel that is often ignored by other fashion brands, as millions of Brits prepare to go abroad this summer.

The brand continues to establish its style credentials this year by enlisting high-fashion director duo Julia & Vincent to shoot the campaign. They bring their distinct luxe cinematography to this season's campaign.

The 30-second hero film follows the story of a woman whose luggage gets lost. It opens on our protagonist waiting at baggage claim, realising that her luggage is not going to turn up. She heads to the lost luggage counter where she sees her image reflected in the glass and regains her composure, secure in the knowledge that she can navigate the remainder of her holiday with that one versatile outfit from F&F.

The same narrative arc runs through all elements of the campaign - AV, OOH, social and digital channels - with the work charting a journey to the airport, navigating all the situations you find yourself in while on holiday, as well as what can happen if you lose your luggage.

June will also see an activation in which F&F unite some lucky holidaymakers with emergency suitcases containing the brand's summer collection.

Rachel Nooney, Head of Brand and Marketing at F&F, said: "Summer holidays rarely go exactly to plan and we wanted to acknowledge the reality of travel in a way that feels relatable and entertaining. With F&F's summer collection, we're showing customers that versatile, stylish fashion can help them feel confident and prepared, whatever the journey throws at them."

Felipe Serradourada Guimaraes, Chief Creative Officer at BBH London & Dublin, said: "We're entering another year of 'Style it Out', with a more integrated campaign, not only in film but also as an activation, all with the single-minded insight of travel nightmares. Style out the chaos of summer. Hope your bags don't get lost."

Launching on 16 May with a 30-second spot during Britain's Got Talent on ITV, the campaign will run nationwide for six weeks from 18 May across TVC, sponsorship idents, print and social.

The campaign was directed by Paris-based artistic duo Julia & Vincent of DMB Production. Media planning and buying was handled by WPP Media.

records.title: Sun Shadows
records.description:
Every evening, sunset calls us outside. Not with a notification, but with light.

To celebrate Corona’s belief that life is best lived outside, we created a series of living posters that turned the setting sun into the brand itself. Captured at the exact moment the sun kissed the horizon over the city, long winter shadows stretched across the streets, invited us to the sunset and created the silhouette of a Corona bottle leading to the sunset.

A simple white chalk outline of the label completed the picture, allowing the sun and shadows to become the bottle for just a few fleeting moments.

No CGI. No manipulation. Just careful planning, perfect timing, and the reminder that nature still creates the most extraordinary spectacles, if we’re willing to step outside to see them.

Because when sunset calls, answer. It’s sunset time.

records.title: Surprising Strength
records.description:
Oikos® is showing up strong on football's biggest night for its sixth straight year, this time proving that strength can come from places you never expected – even yourself. Featuring multi-nominated actress Juno Temple and pro football star Myles Garrett in the all-new ad "Surprising Strength," acclaimed director Wayne McClammy and Oikos showcase that there's more to being strong than what meets the eye.

In the brand's newest spot, 'football's' sweetheart and one of the league's biggest musclemen come together in a humorous and action-packed race, as a last-minute gate change throws a wrench in travel plans. Luckily as America's #1 high-protein yogurt brand, Oikos' delicious and nutritious snacks help support strength and save the day. With so much protein-packed goodness loaded into such a small package, Oikos is here to show every one of us that we too can outstrong our everyday by making stronger snack choices on Game Day and throughout the year. STRONGER MAKES EVERYTHING BETTER®.

Juno Temple, known for bringing her charm and depth to underestimated characters, couldn't be more excited to team up with Oikos for her first-ever Big Game spot. "I seriously can't believe I'm in a Big Game ad. It's been super fun working with Oikos," beamed the actress. "This campaign is bold, unexpected, and celebrates a message I hold close to my heart – that strength can come from the most surprising places. It's always a thrill to flip the script and showcase empowered, strong women who rise to the occasion."

"The Big Game is a career-defining moment for athletes where they demonstrate their strength at the highest level, but we know that athletes aren't the only ones who need protein to power their game. At Oikos, we power all types of strength and we're proud to offer fans nutritious, high-quality protein options that are sure to provide a boost whenever they need it most in their everyday lives," says Victoria Badiola, Vice President of Greek & Functional Nutrition at Danone North America. "Being able to bring together the dynamic duo of Juno Temple and Myles Garrett while putting surprising strength at the forefront of our Big Game ad is a fun way to bring our brand ethos to life." 

"As a defensive end, I am constantly adjusting my game to fit different circumstances. I've learned to embrace sudden changes instead of fearing change," said Myles Garett, 2023 Defensive Player of the Year. "Challenges make me stronger and allows me to adapt in unique situations. This is the message I want to share through the Oikos ad: strength can show up in ways you don't expect – like when a friend lets you lean on their strength when you need it most."

On February 9, 2025, the ad will air on FOXSports.com, FOX Sports App, NFL App and Connected TV devices where users can stream the Super Bowl. Viewers in New York, NY., Los Angeles, CA., and Denver, CO., will be able to see the spot live within 30-minutes of kickoff on FOX Sports. Those in New Orleans, LA., can view the ad live on FOX's in-game Super Bowl broadcast.

records.title: Sweet Like Honey
records.description:
Royal Honey – The Art of Desire

Royal Honey isn’t just a product. It’s a promise of energy, intimacy, and indulgence inside a category that’s usually loud, literal, and uncomfortable.

Our challenge was precise: how do you communicate desire without embarrassment, and how do you sell intimacy without saying it?

So we changed the language. Instead of talking about performance, we focused on temptation. Instead of explicit claims, we built visual tension.

The creative direction treats Royal Honey like a luxury ritual, not a supplement, using minimal environments, controlled lighting, and carefully composed symbols. Honey becomes a metaphor for richness, flow, warmth, and restrained power. Every visual is designed to feel irresistible yet refined — provocative, but never vulgar. Nothing is explained; everything is felt. 

he campaign relies on suggestion rather than instruction, inviting the viewer in and letting curiosity do the rest. Royal Honey doesn’t shout benefits. It creates desire.

records.title: SYNCED
records.description:
In honor of National Caregiver’s Day (February 20), The Stroke Foundation and Remedy Edge (formerly Patients & Purpose and DDB Health) announced the premiere of  SYNCED – a 9-minute short film that spotlights the isolation and emotional strain felt by stroke survivors and their caregivers. In the film, an experimental bracelet allows a stroke survivor to share their thoughts and feelings. According to the Stroke Foundation, stroke affects nearly 800,000 Americans annually, and an estimated 53 million people provide unpaid care to loved ones.
The film follows a daughter in her late twenties who has become the unplanned primary caregiver to her mother. As the daughter navigates the frustration and isolation of caregiving, technology becomes the critical bridge that helps them relate to each other and communicate. 
SYNCED was deliberately crafted to feel like a lost film from the 1980s, shot in the era’s signature 4:3 aspect ratio and brought to life with period-accurate music and props. The experience is retro, until viewers notice the “Synced” bracelets. These unique idealistic devices allow a stroke survivor with limited speech to share her thoughts, feelings and memories directly into her daughter’s mind.  At its heart, SYNCED is a love story about what we lose when a stroke changes someone we love—and what it takes to find each other again. 
The film showcases unspoken love a daughter has for her mother as she cares for her. Its deep focus is also on the appreciation a parent has for a child caring for them, even if the parent cannot say it herself. Director Ilaria Serantoni said, “The aesthetic of this film—the repetition, the texture, the silence—that's what caregiving can feel like. We wanted to honor that truth visually." 
The film arrives at a critical time. “As the caregiving crisis grows in America, the system is still not built to support caregivers and stroke is one of the clearest examples,” said Tyler Maxson, Group Creative Director, Remedy Edge. “SYNCED is about the quiet seismic shift that happens inside a relationship after a life-changing health incident. The technology is fictional, but the emotional barriers caregivers and stroke survivors and their caregivers face are not.” 
By grounding the story in empathy, the film hopes to spark conversations about access, equity and the support caregivers need.
 “This film speaks to something timeless and unmistakable: a daughter’s love for her mother and the extraordinary people who show up every day for someone else,” said Florencia Rago, Executive Director of The Stroke Foundation. “As someone who has supported my mother through stroke recovery, creating this film was deeply personal for me.” 
Featuring standout performances from Fran Greene and Glory Gonzalez, SYNCED reminds us that love exists in frequencies that transcend language. You just have to know how to tune in. 
Visit SyncedFilm.com to watch and share the film and to learn how you can help support caregivers in need via a donation to The Stroke Foundation.

records.title: Take A Look
records.description:
With bathroom humor as its hook this hero film gives America’s toilets a voice and calls out the sign of dehydration that we know all-too-well: yellow pee.

records.title: Take The Alfredo
records.description:
Most people have a "pasta night" routine, but it almost always defaults to red sauce. To break the cycle, Bertolli and Fallon are launching “Take the Alfredo,” a new campaign designed to shake up the status quo and rediscover the joy of America’s #1 selling Alfredo.

Marking the brand's first major creative push in years, the work intentionally skips the industry-standard slow-motion sauce shots. Instead, the campaign utilizes cinematic visual metaphors to illustrate what it means to stand out from the pack and do things a little differently. In the spots "Flock" and "Rose," the creative moves away from the traditional culinary aesthetic to position Bertolli Alfredo as a premium, distinct choice—rather than just a back-of-the-pantry backup.

"Bertolli has always been the leader in Alfredo, but for this campaign, we wanted to move beyond just awareness and challenge the 'red sauce routine' head-on,” Soledad Querol, Executive Director, Marketing at Mizkan. “By working with Fallon to step outside the traditional culinary aesthetic, we’re positioning Bertolli Alfredo as a premium, distinct choice that stands out in a sea of red. It’s about reminding consumers that their midweek pasta night can be something a lot more elevated as we encourage consumers to ‘Take the Alfredo’.”

The goal is a reintroduction of a classic, encouraging consumers to elevate their midweek meals and, quite literally, take the Alfredo.

records.title: Take Time for the essential

In a world filled with constant distractions, taking a moment for yourself has become more important than ever.
With its latest campaign, Take Time for the essential , Aquafina encourages people to pause amidst the noise of everyday life and reconnect with what truly matters in the moment.
Through relatable scenes and a distinctive visual treatment that contrasts movement and stillness, the campaign captures brief moments of clarity in the middle of busy, overwhelming environments.
A simple reminder that sometimes, what matters most is taking a moment for yourself.

records.title: Take Your Brain Out
records.description: New research is revealing the impact screen time can have on developing brains, and it’s significant. The good news? Nature can help offset its effects. Time spent outdoors is linked to positive changes in children’s brain development. You could say that spending time outside resets little brains. That insight drove Sukle's new campaign for Generation Wild. In the hero :30, we bring viewers into a magical world showing different kids engaged in outdoor adventures with friends - friends who just happen to be anthropomorphized brains. Together they ride bikes, swing on a tree swing, roll down a grassy hill, and stare up at the clouds. Sukle worked with Passion Pictures and director Anna Mantzaris, renowned for her stop-motion animation for Apple’s ‘Fuzzy Feelings’ holiday campaign. And the earworm of a song was scored by Singing Serpent Music. The campaign extended to social media, OOH, a poster series featuring local artists, and fence art posted at local elementary schools.

records.title: “Tales of the Un-Probable”
records.description:
Newly launched creative agency Herd of Shepherds is making waves with its latest work: “Tales of the Un-Probable”, a category-redefining campaign for Smartsheet, the AI-powered, enterprise-grade work management platform.

The visually striking animated campaign highlights the extraordinary feats made possible by the powerful enterprise-grade technology Smartsheet offers, emphasizing how seemingly improbable achievements become reality when businesses harness the innovative platform to help their work flow freely.

Built around real customer stories, “Tales of the Un-Probable” is a departure from the industry’s formulaic approach to work management software marketing. Instead of dry, technical messaging accompanied by stilted office workers and software screens, the campaign embraces a whimsical animation style to convey the magic, scale and ambition of what Smartsheet enables.

The multi-platform campaign is based on the simple truth that while work management software might not be inherently exciting, the enterprise-grade power of Smartsheet transforms how businesses accomplish work in ways that are nothing short of extraordinary.

The spot “Space Dust” illustrates how Smartsheet helps orchestrate the intricacies of space exploration for a job site 140 million miles from Earth.  “Every Part in Place” focuses on the platform’s ability to track over 14,000 precision-crafted parts in the world’s fastest motor sport.  “Smiles” highlights how a nonprofit coordinates complex surgical logistics to change lives across the globe.

"We knew we had to bring this campaign to life in a way that felt as big and ambitious as the customers who use Smartsheet," said Matt Gilmore, Founding Partner at Herd of Shepherds, based in Seattle.  "B2B advertising tends to play it safe, but we saw an opportunity to craft something with real emotional weight, something inspiring that would push away from the homogeneity."

The campaign rolls out across TV, digital, and social platforms, delivering a fresh, visually rich alternative to the monotony of B2B marketing. 

Where most enterprise campaigns default to lifeless cubicles, monotone talking heads and dull UI demos, this campaign dares to be different. With bold, painterly animation and emotionally charged storytelling, it transforms work management from a dry necessity into a force for the extraordinary, making Smartsheet impossible to ignore.

The initiative was created in collaboration with John Newall, Senior Vice President, Marketing at Smartsheet, who said, "Smartsheet enables customers of any size, across industries, to seize new opportunities and drive unprecedented results. These customers are at the heart of our new campaign, and the imagery and narratives beautifully capture the magic they make with Smartsheet.”

“We wanted this campaign to feel as ambitious as the customers Smartsheet serves," said Megan Ball, Partner and Executive Producer, Herd of Shepherds. "It’s visually stunning, emotionally resonant, and most importantly, doesn’t feel like a typical B2B campaign.”

Herd of Shepherds is an independent, recently launched, creative agency built to do work that matters. Founded by industry veterans with a track record of bold, award-winning campaigns, the agency is designed for brands that want to stand out, take risks and create work people care about.

"We built this agency to focus on what matters most: the work," added Shawn Herron, Founding Partner, Herd of Shepherds. "Smartsheet was the perfect partner because they see creativity as a competitive advantage, and aren’t afraid to be bold.”
