"We experimented with concepts that played with scale and texture to figure out what could tell the best story in a 45 second commercial. It became clear that our asset builds would have to be exceptionally accurate, with detail being everything. "This attention to detail alongside a strictly matched depth of field and lens artifacts from the original shots in compositing is what made this creative idea work so well. "We pitched, shot, and finished this film in a global pandemic – this should have been a challenge for the team but due to our cloud-based technology we are able to seamlessly work remotely and have access to immediate scaling to accommodate the project workload. "Untold Studios have a great relationship with Epic Games and we put in place an on-set visualisation system using Unreal and Ncam. This meant we had live, tracked and rendered set extensions on set – something very different to framing an actor on a green screen with no visual reference. "We love to push the boundaries of creativity and technology at Untold Studios and it was brilliant to apply this way of working on this project." Schedule: 10 weeks.

records.title: DASHLANE "RANDOM ON PURPOSE"
records.description: Mill Director Oliver Davies: "The biggest challenge with this metaphorical tale of totally unguessable behavior was to source exactly the right stock footage to set up a believable nature doc vibe, and then seamlessly blend it with photoreal CGI and layers of design elements for when things start to get random. "Completed in just four weeks at the height of lockdown and across at least six time zones, it was a real team effort between agency, client, multiple departments at The Mill, and editor Ben Campbell at Cut & Run to find the best way of telling this unpredictable story. "Luckily for random rabbit (and me) everyone involved was 100% committed to the task and possessed much talent and good humour so it was a pleasure from start to finish."

records.title: THE MINI VISION URBANAUT "VIBE"
records.description: Matthias Zabiegly, VFX supervisor at Aixsponza in Munich, Germany: "We were tasked with creating launch animations, print renderings, an Instagram filter, and design snippets (showcasing design highlights of the MINI Vision Urbanaut) to cover an online release of the concept vehicle. "The biggest challenge was the merger of different graphic styles into something that doesn't look thrown together but rather belongs together. "We used a classical 3D rendering approach, added hand-drawn illustrations to that, and also had to work in live-action footage. "The animated Illustrations were based on footage of actors we shot. Figuring out how to do that shooting was done blocking everything out as a rough 3D animatic. "We then knew where the cameras were and also what the actions of the actors were. In order to be able to place the footage into the scene, we had to get rid of any movement in space of the actors. "So for example we had to stabilize and lock footage in place so an actor wasn't moving forward but walking in place. This way we could move the 3D cards around as we wished in 3D space. "Shooting on treadmills wasn't really an option as we also had to film rather complex interactions. That required good planning and a post-process that had a few turns and corners but in the end, everything worked out like a charm." Schedule: Four months.

records.title: VANMOOF "RIDE THE FUTURE TOGETHER"
records.description: Henry Foreman, head of design at The Mill in London: "This wasn't just about animating all of the pieces of a bicycle coming together and making it look beautiful. There was another layer of storytelling we had to get right. "For the client, they have a bigger message than just selling great bicycles. It had to communicate the need for people to come together and face the challenge of overcoming the impact of fossil fuel-based transport, without negativity or being overbearing – so we added a little humor and charm. A frog. Why not?! "A timeline this short for a full CG film is always going to be challenging, so we spent a lot of time upfront with Tom Dibb (Creative Director) and the Creative Strategy team getting the story right with loose animatics, whilst working on the technical aspects of ingesting and repairing the CAD models of the bikes at the same time. "We knew we could make the shots look great, but there were definitely hurdles in making sure the story made sense, whilst treading a fine line between being abstract and explicit."

records.title: VANMOOF "RETHINK THE CITY. REIMAGINE THE FUTURE"
records.campaign_title: VANMOOF "RETHINK THE CITY. REIMAGINE THE FUTURE"
records.description: Liza Uys, EP at Bewilder in Cape Town, South Africa: "We were commissioned to help bring a narrative and journey to the idea behind the VanMoof e-bike changing the future and changing the city towards a more green and eco-friendly place. We collaborated with illustrator Jim Stoten to bring his designs to life through animation. "The main challenge was to marry the illustration style to the animation style and form a creative solution that suits both when the illustration was not created with animation in mind. "Finding creative solutions and knowing where to give and take was important in our process. It was great working with Jim, who is very open to problem-solving and adapting his vision so we can get to solutions fast. "A created a workflow to support the continuous and layered style of illustration into animation and the camera work thereof. Some scenes had to carry very high resolutions and file sizes to endure those long zooms and transitions. "This type of animation, what we call cell/traditional animation, is a style that needs a lot of hands-on deck and has a lot of moving parts that must be stitched together. "Every frame has to go through line work recreation, line cleanup, and color and texturing work that matches its original design as best it can within animation. "Needless to say, a lot of communication and strategizing was involved by all parties to successfully pedal down the right path to our final animation." Schedule: "We had two weeks to get the storyboard and style frames in order with Jim Stoten before we started the animation. We needed a further five weeks to finish off and get the different variations and assets needed for delivery."

records.title: ASN BANK "THE SCAPEGOAT"
records.description: Justin Blyth, global head of creative at ambassadors in Amsterdam: "ASN Bank is the Netherlands' most sustainable bank, and for over four years has had an ongoing campaign ‘zo maakt geld gelukkig' (‘so money can create happiness') featuring CG animated woodland creatures that tell us important stories on financial sustainability. "Ambassadors had the joy to work on crafting all six commercials, and for this latest chapter, it was all about honoring the ASN fable forest's heritage but taking the creative message even further than before. "Director Nick Groeneveld and the team introduced lots of new characters, a crowd scene, multiple miniature sets, and helped tell this important environmental message with a wink. "Remote working is always going to pose new challenges for production, but this wasn't the first rodeo for Ambassadors, creative agency Selmore, and ASN Bank working together. "We used 'The Scapegoat' as an opportunity to trial working in a Wide Gamut Color Space, a VFX pipeline technique allowing for a much wider range of colors in the renders. "With this approach, our CG team could achieve even nicer-looking shots with super filmic, realistic lighting. We find it's good to test this out before you need to, so in the future, if there might be for example the specific requirements of an HDR deliverable, the studio is ready for that. "We started talking about this new chapter in the ASN Bank storybook of sustainability in late January this year, and by May it was showing on Dutch TV screens around the lowlands. "We worked on the full creative production from character design, storyboard, to shoot, 2D and 3D animation, CG, edit, original music composition and color grade. So, a ton! We're big fans of V-Ray by Chaos Group. "The environment is completely based on a real courtroom, but built from natural ingredients, which you will find in a deeper forest. A deep round mossy pit, ferns, mushrooms, roots used as benches, and an old tree used as a Judge's bench. "These are our favorite projects – built on trust with agency and client partners who give us creative, collaborative liberty through the entire process, from initial sketches to final online. "On top of that, making beautiful work for a great cause makes the whole process inspiring, and drives us to push our work to the next level."

records.title: "POKEMON X OREO LIMITED EDITION COOKIES"
records.description: Nintendo's Pikachu comes to life via limited-edition Pokémon Oreos disguised as retro Gameboy pixels in this quasi-meta crossover spot from the Framestore crew celebrating Pokémon's 25th Anniversary. Created in concert with 360i, MediaMonks, and VaynerMedia, the campaign highlights sixteen character designs available in Pokémon cookie packs. From Framestore: "Beginning with a rough edit in After Effects that utilized reference footage provided by Pokémon, our cel animators got to work hand drawing the characters and environments in over 600 frames. "From there, the frames were brought into Houdini to be processed and turned into the pixel grid, challenging the team to strike a perfect balance between pixels large enough to be recognizable as cookies while maintaining a tight grid that preserved the fidelity of the drawings."

records.title: COPPER "THE UNFAIR ADVANTAGE"
records.description: Strange and wonderful things are happening in the mountains of Iceland courtesy of director Diarmid Harrison-Murray, the VFX crew at Untold Studios in London, and actress Rebecca Ferguson ("Dune" and several editions of "Mission Impossible"). Director Diarmid Harrison-Murray: "This was a very agile and dynamic process from the start. The brief came in from Adam Parry at Piccadilly Curtains and our visions were creatively aligned from the beginning. "I wanted to make a film in which the visual effects were borne out of the landscape and inspired by its form; a revelation of hidden realities within, rather than a digital overlay. "Also Rebecca's journey and presence throughout these worlds were important to me as it gives the film a humanity that can sometimes be lost with big VFX shots."

records.title: 1792 BOURBON "UNTYPICAL"
records.description: Hornet director Ariel Costa pours his trademark collage talents into this atmospheric, jewel-toned spot for Sazerac's small-batch bourbon whiskey brand 1792 thru agency The Buntin Group. From Hornet: "Say goodbye to gravelly-voiced, whiskey-in-the-woods, campfire provincialism. And hello to cosmopolitan collage, stylized storytelling, and a jazz-fueled journey into the Untypical."

records.title: ESTEE LAUDER "CRAFTMANSHIP"
records.description: The Mill Design Studio and roster director FILFURY showcase the craftsmanship of Estée Lauder's heavyweight, soft-close, eyeshadow packaging with "an array of rich, elegant, and textural, graphic design vignettes". From the team at The Mill Design Studio: "With the spot's main focus being the craft, it felt appropriate to use the precision of 2D technical lines as the starting point. "From here the team played with light and shadow to reveal drafting tools, as they scored the screen for the initial product reveal. "This concept was built on by introducing abstract shapes that showcased different materials and textures – contributing to the abstract creation of the product. This was then manipulated with the use of sophisticated repeated patterns and formations. "The brand gave us such great creative freedom during our exploration phase and put full trust in the director's ideas and the ability of our artists to realize them effectively."

records.title: DORITOS "ANOTHER LEVEL"
records.description: Steve Mottershead, CD/owner at Artjail in New York: "The brief from the agency GS&P and Reset director Henry Scholfield was very ambitious. The concept was to show how trends come and go but Doritos has always been relevant and popular since it's been around. "The whole spot was planned to be a constant transition through all the fads and trends that have come and gone and some futuristic ones that haven't even happened yet. "So right from the get go we knew this one was gonna be both a creative and technically demanding project. "One of the biggest challenges was translating and executing the multitude of ideas that Henry was throwing our way. There are a staggering number of details packed into these 30 seconds, many which evolved and emerged along the way. Artjail head of 2D Lee Towndrow: "We love how many disparate cultural references Henry is able to tap and make them all fit. Aesthetics from the 70's, the 90's, 2000's on up to 2050 are in the mix and it all feels so natural. "The coda called for an entire future city which we built, replete with flying cars. "We referenced Bladerunner and Alita, two of our favorite films. "There were also a lot of additional details to finesse and pepper into this bonkers edit pulled off by the talented Sam Ostrove of Cabin Edit. Designer/CD Matt Greenwood:, "We kept pushing the motion graphics and adding lots of layers and it was a chance to be able to pull out all the stops." "There's so much visually going on throughout the spot, it was an interesting challenge to add to this look and it's fun for the viewer to catch all these crazy details. "Even though a lot of these crafted elements are only on screen for a quick moment, it adds a really rich overall feel to the piece. "The CG elements in the spot played a key role with the team providing a host of elements to help 2D and motion design blend certain shots together. "For example the blockbuster scene required a torrent of movies to fly up through the wormhole and a holographic transporter deck was also a CG lift. The goal was to help transform the final result into a better visual experience. Artjail lead CG artist Mark Ingle: "The creative workflow was unique in that it allowed many different interpretations of the glitch effects. A procedural approach in Houdini gave us the opportunity to quickly explore dozens of glitch styles in a short timeframe. "This was a true team effort and allowed us to use all the tools at our disposal; Creative and technical problem solving, 2D, CG, 360, motion design, matte painting, and color grading."

records.title: BBC WINTER OLYMPICS "EXTREME BY NATURE"
records.description: With a labor-intensive mix of in-camera effects, 3D-printed stop-motion, and algorithmic CGI, Blinkink director Balázs Simon showcases "how Olympians push themselves to the extreme" for the BBC Winter Olympics coverage. Balázs Simon: "I really admire people having the will to push things to the limits. Especially the winter games where they compete in environments that are so different from our usual experiences. "When I got approached by this project, the biggest question for me was how to portray and live up to that dedication. A good way was to bring the film out to the real world. "Although most of my work is tied to digital animation, I'm most intrigued by the physical reality and the uncertainties that come with it. In a way, I wanted to find myself in a similar situation as the Olympians: in a foreign, unforgiving place that needs to be conquered. "This resonated well with our controlling idea: to be able to compete, these people must be made of something different. We wanted to portray them being born into ice and snow and eventually breaking out."

records.title: SOUTH WESTERN RAILWAY "SPREAD YOUR WINGS"
records.description: New work from Nexus directors Smith & Foulkes will always brighten your day and so it is with this breezy spot for the UK's South Western Railway starring commuters Wesley Peck and Sandy C Gull thru agency St. Luke's. Alan Smith and Adam Foulkes: "We rarely get the chance to create characters from scratch, giving them individual behavioral habits and a shared history. "The commuting friendship is a very specific kind of relationship. You don't go down the pub with each other but you're comfortable enough to ramble on about not very much while staring out the window. "This reconnection between these two unlikely friends mirrors those happening up and down the country as we slowly re-emerge from our lockdown cocoons to step back into the wider world. Plenty of bird gags in this one."

records.title: CARLSBERG "CHAMBER OF SECRETS" (DIRECTOR'S CUT)
records.description: Albert Garcia, lead 2D artist at Glassworks in London: "The client wanted to present a friendly atmosphere with a good balance between the humor and the seriousness of a beer commercial. "The ad is therefore full of subtle comedic details that were incredibly fun to work on. For example, the friendly farmer robots, the angelical painting, or the David-like statue of Mads Mikkelsen. "Finding the right look for the robots was one of the main creative challenges for our team. "We needed to develop a farmer android that would look friendly and nonthreatening in a post-apocalyptic setting. So, we tested various expressions and looks until we found the one that suited the tone of the ad. "The ad features many different scenes and environments in a short period of time. They all had to be perfectly built and integrated, each one with different degrees of compositing and 3D. This meant that the on-set supervision and the VFX integration were a key part of the process "The Chamber scene was filmed in the impressive Rondel cellars in Barcelona. Our 2D and 3D teams built it up so that it would be reminiscent of the old Carlsberg brewery in Copenhagen. "The magnificent elephant sculptures frame the scene, and the Carlsberg logo and portraits subtly feature in the background."

records.title: MAGNUM "REMIX"
records.description: The design and animation team at ManvsMachine team up with Spanish agency LOLA MullenLowe to "reimagine what Magnum's iconic product shots could be." From ManvsMachine: "From the classic ‘pour' to the mouth-watering ‘crack', we exploded, twisted, melted, and dripped pure chocolate bliss all over the screen. "The Remix product line demonstrates the multiple ways flavors can combine, experimenting with fresh and modern takes on ingredient combinations. Magnum Dore evokes a sense of indulgent decadence, and the ever-iconic Classic range is pushed to its textural limits."

records.title: TROLLI "THE GOONIVERSE FACTORY"
records.description: Renee Zhan, director at Blinkink in London: "Trolli wanted to make their ‘darkest ad yet' to celebrate the release of the new Sour Burstin Crawlers. "The film was to take place in a factory which ground up worms into goo to inject into the bodies of their wormy brothers. "We had so many ideas that we wanted to fit into this project. Narrowing them down so they would fit in the time constraints of two 15s was the most challenging part. "We really wanted to go big on this campaign, to make huge factory interiors and expansive worlds. We decided to use CG to create these huge sets, but we really wanted to maintain the handmade feel and texture of the previous ads. "We worked closely with Saurus, a brilliant Norwegian CG company, to replicate the look and feel of stop motion sets and puppets. "Trolli, Wieden+Kennedy, and Blink Ink have a long and beautiful history of collaboration. The first films were directed by Becky and Joe, then Sam Gainsborough. "The humor, irreverence, and craftsmanship in their films were so inspiring. Making a Trolli ad was a dream of mine since I first began in advertising. It was such a rich and fun universe to draw from and build upon." Schedule: 10 weeks.

records.title: BANG & OLUFSEN, BALENCIAGA "SPEAKER BAG"
records.description: ManvsMachine's recent run of CG head-turners (see their Magnum "Remix" spot in Stash 154 and Mini "Elements" in Stash 153) continues with this spot for a portable speaker/handbag manufactured by luxury audio brand Bang & Olufsen and unveiled as a catwalk accessory at Balenciaga's 2022 couture show in Paris. Limited to an edition of 20, each Speaker Bag is machined from a single block of aluminum to resemble the sculptural form of Balenciaga's handbags and will only be available at select Balenciaga boutiques. Miklu Silvanto, chief design officer at Bang & Olufsen in Denmark: "This bag is a testament to what happens when two very special companies with a heritage of craftsmanship join forces. "From our aluminum factory to Balenciaga's atelier to an entirely remarkable product. You have to see, hear and feel it."

records.title: TAG HEUER "F1 COLOURS"
records.description: Anders Schroder, CD/Co-founder at Frame in Copenhagen, Denmark: "TAG Heuer has been synonymous with Formula 1 motor racing since 1971 so the creative challenge was to capture the thrilling suspense of F1 racing, depicted through the key features of the F1 Colours timepiece - all whilst celebrating the three distinct colorways. "First we needed to tackle the challenge of the device that was going to be the glue in the film. "We tried various ideas such as wind tunnel smoke, mechanical exploded views, and racing stripe patterns but quickly realized Tag Heuer had used most of these in earlier campaigns. "So, the only relevant idea left was using the idea of racing flags and banners. "We wanted to portray the race without being literal. We wanted to create something more sophisticated and conceptual so we identified iconic moments in F1 racing to serve as inspiration for the animation: pitstops, spin-outs, burnouts, collisions, finishing line crossings, cockpit POVs, etc. "At FRAME we always try to shave the idea down to its core essentials both conceptually and visually without unnecessary bells and whistles. "Therefore we decided to tell the story of an F1 race using only watches and flags in iconic racing situations. "For example, the scenario of a race car spinning out in the sandbox was told by having a watch twirl into a billowing flag which is much simpler and more elegant. We underlined these metaphorical shots with real-world F1 sounds. "The last step in creating the film was to string these metaphors together to form a rather linear narrative that would take the watches from the start lines, through various obstacles to the finishing line. "By far the biggest challenge was developing a sexy edit with its many ramped shots fitting together. "So we would time ramp in the editing and then once the edit was locked, we would go back into 3D and recreate these time ramps properly. The tricky thing was to combine this with all the cloth simulations in each scene." Schedule: Eight weeks.

records.title: MADE "NEVER ORDINARY"
records.description: Minna Griffiths, creative assistant at Optical Arts in London: "The agency Wonderhood Studios were launching a new brand platform for UK furniture maker MADE that focused on stepping away from the ordinary and embracing the distinctiveness and individualism of their customers. "One of the challenges of this project was combining the highly stylized set with the less rigid cinematic and narrative feel we were striving for – an atmosphere that was both playful and disconcerting without being too comedic or sinister. "We designed a series of bold and distinctive sets taking inspiration from modern showrooms and Memphis design as well as more traditional Victorian homes. "One of the biggest technical challenges was designing the fish head and bringing it to life as we had to make it fit on human shoulders and mimic the movements and facial expressions of the actor with our animation." Schedule: Six months.

records.title: ZHIBEN "DUO YUAN"
records.description: Anders Schroder, CD/co-founder at Frame in Copenhagen, Denmark: "As time passes and we live our busy city lives, our skin ages prematurely due to the pollutants that it absorbs. "This line of Zhiben products contains antioxidant properties that protect the skin by neutralizing these free radicals before they get absorbed. This was the story the client wanted us to tell in a metaphorical way. "We wanted to visualize the concept of ‘protection' which inspired us to create the visual metaphor of letting the rose petals catch the bottles as they were falling from the sky. "Rose petals exude a sense of delicate serenity and beauty. They are velvety and lush so they were ideal for playing the role of the ‘protectors' as the rose extract is also a part of the actual product. "The light in the scene is hard and directional to symbolize the harshness of the environment that the Zhiben product is protecting us from. "The entire film feels as if it is in slow motion but the lights and the shadows that are being cast move unnaturally fast, again to illustrate time passing. "All of this is packaged into a gentle and soft expression that resonates with the brand's usual communication and attitude. "What sets this film apart in our view, is the graceful and evolving flow of the editing and animation and the overall soft and gentle feel of the film. "The shader of the rose petal was extremely difficult to nail. It could very easily look like human skin which made it quite gross. "It was extremely minor details such as tiny adjustments of the hue, making the edges of the petal ultra-thin, and more subtle veins in the leaf that shifted the expression dramatically from human skin to rose petal." Schedule: Eight weeks.

records.title: META QUEST PRO "BEYOND REALITY"
records.description: From the team at ManvsMachine: "Working closely with the fine folk at Meta, we designed and directed the launch film for their most advanced VR headset yet, the Meta Quest Pro. "The film takes us on a mind-bending journey, effortlessly shifting from reality to a dream world in a variety of unexpected abstractions and metaphors. Beautifying the product, glorifying its capabilities, and throwing light on its high-end finish and design."

records.title: DEVIALET "OPÃRA DE PARIS"
records.description: Jack Seymour, creative lead at Found in London: "The product range is a collaboration between Devialet and The Palais Garnier Paris, so our brief was to combine the luxury of the Opéra de Paris with the contemporary forms of the Devialet speaker range. "Materiality and color were to be used to add cues from the interior of the Palais Garnier opera house which we could use to build a world that suggested architectural form, rather than an explicit rebuild of the venue. "Premium is the keyword here. Premium materials add up to a premium product that delivers a premium audio experience. "Ensuring the high-end aesthetic of the Devialet product range came across without being able to showcase its primary feature, the amazing sound quality was certainly a challenge. "Visually, we wanted to showcase the product's elegance and class, while hinting that under that flawless surface, there's harmony between the many innovative parts, that are both functional and beautiful. "Building the mechanics of the product plinths to feel elegant, complex, and technical took time and effort. Each plinth has a unique way of moving, all based on time, to reveal the inner workings. "Additionally re-creating the unique PUSHPUSH mechanic of the woofers (placed on either side of the products) had to be matched accurately so we used the real products at high volume to observe the way in which audio physically affects the speaker." Schedule: Seven weeks.

records.title: BETSSON "MILLIONS"
records.description: Andreas Ibohm, EP at Filmic Art in Stockholm: "Betsson is a Swedish company that offers a number of online gambling products. The brief was to make customers aware and keep them engaged over a longer time period with the daily questions and bets to 'keep the million'. "One creative challenge was to achieve the luxurious look and the feeling of diamonds both up close and from far away without having it look like pieces of glass or just dust. "The diamonds had to twinkle in the right places so we had to adjust the sparkling and glittering manually to heighten the experience. "In general, 3D simulations are always a challenge. The simulations don't always end up in the way one would aesthetically want them to. "So it is a time-consuming process with a lot of tweaking and going back and forth before you achieve the standard and look that is expected. Making an unrealistic action like diamonds flying in cloud formation look realistic was a definite challenge."

records.title: ALIENWARE "X16 LAPTOP" (DIRECTOR'S CUT)
records.description: Katerina Mileva, creative researcher at Trizz Studio in Barcelona: "The new X16 lineup from Alienware is a design-centric range of extremely high-performance gaming laptops, which break away from their more traditional gaming look and move toward more minimalistic territory. "We were asked to create a visual world around the product to reflect this new product design philosophy. "The main creative challenge was to find a visual path that was both visually striking and innovative, but at the same time did not steer too far from the previous Alienware world of color and light – a refresh on their existing visual language. "The biggest technical challenge was management of the complex simulations all working together in one scene from a rendering/memory standpoint." Schedule: 10 weeks.

records.title: BAUME & MERCIER "RIVIERA MOON PHASE"
records.description: With a combination of CG and macro cinematography, Paris creative digital agency I-réel expands its portfolio of luxury product films with this intimate and intricate work for venerable Swiss watchmaker Baume & Mercier. ​​​​​​​ Simon Ravet, director and lead motion designer at I-réel: "The Riviera watch is inspired by the French Riviera mood: sea, sun, and the art of living on the Côte d'Azur. "In addition, each collection of the brand uses its own design. Our objective for this film was to link those two universes, one from the maritime world and the other astronomical, with different textures. "This project is completely post-produced in 4K resolution. The Moonphase images were shot with our RED 8K camera in our in-house studio, coupled with our motion-control robot. CGI sequences were created with 3ds Max and V-Ray. "The film is divided into four parts, where each texture highlights a specific detail of the watch. For the opening we created small pebbles, reminding us of the lunar surface, pushed back by an invisible object, emitting light, and recalling the different moon phases. "In the second part, we focus on the dial, which is encircled by a thin blue disc. Closer, blue streaks stand for the movement of the waves. It took us lots of experiments to create this texture, associated with a ripple animation to represent the sea. "The rendering is of a subtle softness, and the light hangs perfectly on the fringe waves. "You can't talk about the Riviera without mentioning water. For this part, we created a transparent outer dial but kept the indexes (the hour indication markers) in steel. Then we poured water into this cylinder. "The idea was to see the liquid bouncing in that shape and create a structure halfway between an art installation and science fiction, where gravity would not exist."

records.title: HUBLOT BIG BANG "MECA-10 BLACK MAGIC 45MM"
records.description: Salvatore Giunta, founder/CD and Claudio Gasparollo, senior designer at Ditroit in Milan, Italy: "Hublot asked our studio to highlight the new Big Bang Meca-10 Black Magic 45mm through bold and minimalistic imagery, dark tones, neat lighting, and contrasty images. "They also suggested introducing a clean industrial environment as the ideal setting for the watch. Red lasers and neon lights could be another touch to allow for more evocative and engaging storytelling. "We really wanted to lead the company into embracing a more editorial kind of aesthetics, where 3D photorealistic renders could blend seamlessly with flat colors and silhouettes – typical elements of an illustrative approach. "This was a bit different compared to the usual Hublot communication style, but somehow we managed to get the right balance between the different elements. "This was the first time for us using very complex 3D watch CAD models so it took a significant amount of time to organize and learn how to manage the endless number of pieces. "Even nowadays, flexibility and updatability are still touchy topics, an ongoing and ever-learning process. Moreover, the overall render time was very long, since the required output quality forced us to crank up the render settings quite a bit. "The production schedule lasted approximately three months, spread between the concept adjustments, an initial R&D phase, a more advanced production period, and the very last finalization."

records.title: MERCEDES-BENZ "GLC RELAUNCH"
records.description: Director Shane Griffin in New York City: "The core concept was to visualize the birth and construction of the new Mercedes GLC, using the fundamental elements that make up the car; glass, chrome, electricity, etc. "These elements, densely packed together, burst out like the Big Bang that started the universe. "We've seen a lot of very technical constructions of cars and products as of late, so creatively we were searching for a novel approach to build the car, at a pace that felt natural, not overly technical, and not rushed. "It's a fine balance when you're trying to fit the entire thing into 30 seconds, so we did a lot of R&D on effects to find the right pacing. "We also worked hard establishing a very bespoke palette for all the shots, so the live action and CG shots melted together with the same romanced lighting. "We established a look for this prior to the shoot and created a scene in Unreal Engine to use as the backplate for our virtual production shoot, which, luckily we got a near-perfect match for on our location day. "We developed a couple of different approaches for the fluid look of the car paint surface, such as VDB, Pyro, and opacity-based techniques. "During the shoot, we actually did strip a car down entirely to just the exoskeleton and the wheels, the Mercedes engineer who was driving it sat on an apple box. "The schedule was roughly eight weeks, including the two-day shoot in LA – one location on an old missile silo site, and another on the Orbital virtual stage."

records.title: BANG & OLUFSEN AND FERRARI "DRIVEN TO PERFECTION"
records.campaign_title: BANG & OLUFSEN AND FERRARI "DRIVEN TO PERFECTION"

records.title: AUDI "THE LAST DANCE"
records.description: Javier Vallejo, founder and CD at JVG in Madrid: "This project is a portfolio version of a job commissioned by Audi Germany for their official magazine. "Although both the request and the final result had little to do with this piece, we couldn't waste the incredible results we achieved in the R&D phase, especially as it coincided with the end of production of the amazing Audi R8. "The video is clearly divided into two parts, beginning with dozens of beauty shots of the car, and from the 33-second mark, the actual driving action, the 'Last Dance' itself that actually never ends. "Making this work seamlessly while incorporating many other pacing changes in the first part was the main challenge. "The most difficult technical aspect was seamlessly blending numerous distinct shots so that they worked well together in perfect harmony without appearing entirely unrelated but also not from the same scene. "As this is a director's cut we didn't have strict timelines, but it took us approximately two months working inbetween commercial projects."

records.title: TERMINO "MODULAR KITCHEN"
records.description: Aurélien Thomas, director/animator in Lyon, France: "The main goal of this video was to promote the launch of the product on the client's pre-order website and social media. "There were three main challenges. The first was to explain the concept of a modular kitchen which is new to most people. "The second was that the client wanted very ‘high end' visuals, inspired by luxury brands and fashion campaigns. "The last and I think the biggest challenge, is there was not really any storyline or storyboard at the beginning of the project which led to many big changes to the story and visuals before settling on the version you see here. "The biggest technical challenge was to be efficient with my time because the client's budget was pretty small and the deadlines were tight. "Most of the time on the project was spent on visual research (about a week, part-time). "The animation was pretty quick (around two days). Then post-production/editing and sound design went pretty smoothly in about two days. "This project was very interesting because I had a lot of creative freedom. The idea of combining two different films in one (orange and natural/cold) color came when I saw that the client had a hard time deciding between the two options during the research phase. "Even if this kind of project with smaller clients has a reduced budget, I tend to always accept them because this is how you can attract bigger clients and more profitable projects in the long run."

records.title: WORLD ANIMAL PROTECTION "THE THOUGHTFUL PIG"
records.description: Jorge Montiel Meurer, animation director at The Mill in London: "At the heart of this campaign lies our protagonist, a photo-realistic CG pig asking the question that tugs at our ethical compasses: ‘Do you think that I think?' "This simple yet profound query is the gateway to an exploration of the abilities and intelligence possessed by pigs. "Our journey began with an extensive research phase. We delved into the lives and behavior of real pigs to understand their movements, expressions, and anatomy. We closely observed various pig breeds to ensure accuracy and realism. "The first step in bringing our CG pig to life was creating a 3D model. This involved sculpting the pig's digital form and paying meticulous attention to anatomical details. "We crafted two different looks; a young, healthy appearance for the first part of the film and a dirty, sad look for the final reveal. "Animating our hero pig was one of the most challenging aspects. We had to convey complex emotions and thoughts while maintaining realism. "We used reference videos of real pigs to replicate their movements, and our animators spent countless hours fine-tuning the character's gestures, expressions, and eye movements. "In the end, the creation of our pig was a labor of love, driven by our passion for storytelling and our commitment to raising awareness about animal cruelty."

records.title: OAKLEY MUZM "MARS"
records.description: Robin Volk, managing director at Styleframe in Frankfurt, Germany: "To emphasize the iconic status of the Mars glasses, our goal was to create a film featuring fast-moving footage that captures planet environmental views, rover details, and an elevated product reveal. "When talking about Oakley's most disruptive designs, Mars is top of mind. The piece was originally envisioned by then-Oakley board member Michael Jordan, who wanted a design that turned heads. "In March 1998, Michael got his wish: Oakley Mars sunglasses were released to the public and turned into one of the most collectible Oakley sunglasses of all time. "We were super excited when our client EssilorLuxottica asked us to produce a teaser for the revival of this legendary piece of eyewear. "We started by doing extensive research and development to find the right look and experimented with the Mars environment, the eyewear itself and the color palette. "A highlight of this project was the creation of the Oakley Mars Rover. Using the NASA Rover as a base, we redesigned it to have a more Oakley-influenced design, drawing inspiration from the unique, Brutalist, yet organic architecture of Oakley's headquarters." Schedule: Five weeks.

records.title: DURACELL "BUNNY SAVES CHRISTMAS"
records.description: French director Geoffroy Barbet-Massin, who we last covered for his twist on traditional Japanese art for France TV's coverage of the 2021 Tokyo Olympics (Stash 148), flies off in a different direction in this CG holiday comedy for Duracell. Produced by The Mill+ with VFX handled by The Mill Paris team through agency Wunderman Thompson, the spot revolves around the idea that Santa almost blew his one job by skimping on the batteries that power Rudolph's nose.

records.title: SKINCEUTICALS
records.description: Alexandra Kotova, Producer at Media.Work in Los Angeles: "Proclaiming its mission to improve skin health backed by science, SkinCeuticals invited us to create a series of visualizations showcasing the brand's core message. "Our task was to integrate the unique benefits of the products and communicate the essential tenets based on research and innovation. "Talking about the creative challenges of the project, we aimed to connect the power points of medical procedure, science, and the product's advantages. "In drawing a strong visual thread between these components, we developed a set of metaphors to demonstrate a clear commitment to research and evidence-based validity. "With the formulas of the brand's primary products in our arsenal, we dedicated ourselves to an extensive visual exploration to highlight the uniqueness and active action of each of them but staying within a consistent visual language of the entire series. "We used Houdini and Redshift which allowed us to build our working tools and move our imagination into digital reality. Regarding the hardware, we used our own render farm which includes more than twenty machines." Schedule: Two months.

records.title: SKODA "DISCOVER A NEW KIND OF SPACE"
records.campaign_title: SKODA "DISCOVER A NEW KIND OF SPACE"
records.description: German post and VFX house ACHT backs up English director Joshua Vii as he takes a bee's eye view in this mix of motion-control and CG exploring the exterior and interior of the new Skoda Kodiaq crossover SUV. Produced through Film Deluxe GmbH for agency FCB London to air in Czechia and the UK, the film was shot in Prague and finished at ACHT on what the director calls "the tightest of postproduction schedules." Joshua Vii: "Rarely does a camera have a reason to move in the manner we do in this film. Usually, it's a purely stylistic choice, but here we had an opportunity to embody the point of view of a small bumble bee, adding a narrative touch to each camera move as the bee discovers and explores Skoda's latest SUV. "It was a very technical piece to pull off, combining seamless CGI together with precisely designed motion control shots, some of which were taken directly from FBX files output and mimicked from cinema 4D, while other shots were handcrafted on set due to needing to adapt the path of the camera to the geometry of the set and car. "In order to pull this off, every shot in the film was intricately pre-visualized, beginning by flying an iPhone around my own car to get a sense of where we wanted to be on our journey." "It was important to have the right post-production partner for this and ACHT Studio really pulled off the impossible with our time frame of just 2.5 weeks to edit, grade, animate, light and render CGI, composite, and compose the sound design and music. "Txo pull this off, every shot in the film was intricately pre-visualized, beginning by flying an iPhone around my own car to get a sense of where we wanted to be on our journey, and then crafting the curves and pace of the camera in Cinema 4D which were then handed over to ACHT to be perfected and embedded into their workflow. "It meant that before we shot the film we had a good sense of the edit and pace, and allowed us to overlay mattes of the car interior when shooting the exterior plates which would be composited afterwards. "ACHT did an incredible job bringing everything together and were amazing partners throughout the process, with a true creative understanding of what would help to elevate the film, from bumps and creases in the interior leather, to refining the design of our bumble bee. "FCB London oversaw the creative of the project and brought a solid creative vision of the piece, backing us through a complex process to create a bold visual piece."

records.title: LA MARZOCCO
records.description: Samuel Fast Hurtigkarl, CD/co-founder at Brikk Animation in Stockholm: "The materials and pallet of the new limited edition La Marzocco Linea Mini coffee maker is inspired by the Scandinavian countries so the idea with this film was to show the machine's journey from Florence, Italy to Bergen, Norway. "The main challenge was the short time we had to produce it – four weeks from brief to delivery. To move quickly, we utilized a small team. I served as both the producer and the director to put together my most trusted artists. "It's a pretty dreamy piece with little narrative, so we decided to focus our effort on the design rather than the animation to execute it on time. "The film is aimed at going out on Social Media, but we also produced a few assets that served as a Lo-Fi screensaver on YouTube and a few additional assets for the campaign site. "I should also mention, we love the product. I'm a huge espresso aficionado, so working with a client with a beautiful product who dared to trust the team and me was a dream come true."

records.title: DEWAR'S "DOUBLE DOUBLE"
records.description: Chad Howitt, CD at ManvsMachine in Los Angeles: "Primarily known for their Dewars White Label, the brand wanted to reinforce the Double Double as their luxury product line. "Focusing on craft and substance over style, they wanted to use a room's interior design to redefine what a good scotch whiskey is and break the old and overly traditional perceptions. "Our biggest artistic challenge was the interior design of the rooms and establishing visuals that everyone could agree on. "When creating the ‘traditional ornate room', how far is too far? When does filigree become too much for anybody? "There are wonderful Baroque and Rococo-era designs that are breathtaking, but we needed to embrace it with more of an outlandish approach – like someone with money, but no taste. "On the opposite side, the ‘clean white room' needed to feel like an improvement on the gold room. "Modern aesthetics push design boundaries and room functionality, which often, can be too avant-garde for everyone's tastes. So finding those borders was difficult. "Art directing FLIP and Vellum sims is always a heavy lift that takes lots of time. It's also never a one-and-done process. As revisions and feedback come in, we repeat the process. "Thankfully, our team was able to take complex setups and adjust to the agency's notes to ensure the clients were happy with the final product.

records.title: BBC EUROS "MORE TWISTS, MORE TURNS"
records.description: The quick pace and uncertain outcomes of the Euro 2024 tournament on BBC find an apt metaphor in star-studded pinball action via Blinkink directors Balázs Simon and Raman Djafari with Berlin's Woodblock handling animation. Rasmus Smith Bech, ECD at BBC Creative: "With all its action, emotion, and unexpected previous winners, The Euros is more unpredictable than most international tournaments. "A giant, mad Euros pinball machine felt like the appropriate canvas to bring that beautiful excitement to life." "The film will not only be a promo for the tournament but also its opening titles across all of the BBC's television coverage of the event which starts on 14th June." From the team at Blinkink: "Set to a backdrop of iconic landmarks from the host nation Germany, we follow the ball as it ricochets back and forth between the biggest names in European football – from Kane, Bellingham, Robertson and McTominay to Musiala, Ronaldo and De Bruyne. "The film will not only be a promo for the tournament but its opening titles across all of the BBC's television coverage of the event which starts on 14th June. "Soundtracked by an instrumental version of Nothing But Thieves track ‘Welcome to the DCC', the pinball world pings, clatters, and clanks with sound design from GAS and topped off with archival and bespoke commentary from famous BBC commentators like Guy Mowbray, Vicki Sparks, Steve Wilson, Liam McLeod, James McFadden, and Robyn Cowen."

records.title: AUDIBLE "COSMIC VACUUM"
records.description: London VFX masters Electric Theatre Collective and Partizan director Antoine Bardou-Jacquet (whose last collab was this mini-superhero romp for Coke) re-team for more world-building fun in a pair of spots for Audible thru agency Fold7. Dave Billing, ECD/Partner at Fold7: "Guided by the tagline ‘There's more to imagine when you listen,' we explore how Audible immerses us all in extraordinary worlds, changing our mood, perceptions, and views. "The campaign brings to life the magic in the meeting point between the wonder of our imaginations and the mundanity of the everyday. "[The work] is created through the marriage of old world production techniques with new world technology. A true reflection of Audible's enduring legacy of craft, and their commitment to supporting the creative communities across the world. Running across ten markets, spanning TV, digital, social, radio and OOH."

records.title: RICOLA "THROAT BALM"
records.description: Marcel Hita, CD at Trizz Studio in Barcelona: "The project brief was to create an animation piece that visually conveys concepts such as soothing, smoothness, and relief using a visual language inspired by the key ingredients of the product: caramel, honey, and Swiss herbs. "Our primary challenge was to craft a compelling narrative using only these three ingredients to develop a visual language that captures the product's deliciousness through a dynamic and artistic lens. "You know you're facing a challenge when you aim to blend fluid simulations with controlled and dynamic animation and all the elements need to look photo-realistic. "To achieve this balance, we established a general structure to define timings and motion intentions. From there, we created various simulations that interacted with hand-animated elements like typography and the Ricola product. "Finally, we fine-tuned and refined the motion and lighting of the piece, highlighting every detail characteristic of the Ricola ingredients. "With elements like refractions, subsurface scattering, and complex simulations, the renders were certainly heavy! "With Ricola, we were blessed to have the time in the initial stages of production to dedicate to exploring look development and animation to capture the message and feel we wanted to portray."

records.title: G/FORE "G18"
records.description: Bryant Nichols, CD and Maria Hanafy, Managing Director at FutureDeluxe in Los Angeles: "The initial project brief was quite different from where we landed. "Originally, the client wanted to see their shoe enlarged and traveling through a NYC city street. "We went back and forth on the concept after realizing the initial idea wasn't working. "We landed on something called 'shape deform' where we start on the shoe and it warps and contorts into different shapes. "We went through Unreal Engine testing, decks of references, etc, which led us to the honor and rare luxury of a client who is asking for their shoe to be distorted. To pin down the client's idea of weirdness we went through several rounds of ideation. "The team started animation testing with all manner of odd and hilarious deformations with the art direction crafting a bright and punchy palette to really hero the black and white shoe. "The product is always such an important piece of the puzzle, shoes are always a tricky one, we reached out to our Sydney studio to give us a hand. "They were able to quickly provide us with a shoe that looked photo-real. Not to mention the knowledge they provided in the scanning process. "Creating the morphed shapes in Houdini and then bringing them into Cinema 4D to be used in a pose morph allowed us to utilize the power of Houdini but with the speed and simplicity of C4D for animation and rendering."

records.title: CASETIFY "ULTRA BOUNCE CASE FOR APPLE IPHONE 16"
records.campaign_title: CASETIFY "ULTRA BOUNCE CASE FOR APPLE IPHONE 16"
records.description: Chris Gil CEO at Tektura Studio in Łódź, Poland: "Casetify's brief for this project was to showcase the Ultra Bounce Case for the iPhone 16, highlighting its premium design, durability, and aesthetic appeal. "The animation needed to reflect the smooth, durable materials and emphasize the seamless blend of style and protection. "The main creative challenge was effectively conveying both style and durability in a visually striking way. "The team worked to balance high-contrast shadow effects with soft lighting to emphasize the case's premium materials, without detracting from the refined, minimalistic look. "A significant technical challenge was achieving the ideal balance of lighting and shadow for a smooth yet impactful visual effect. "It was essential to maintain precision in camera movements and lighting to highlight the case's core features—its durability and stylish design. "The animation aligns with current 3D design trends, using minimalism, high-contrast shadowing, and soft lighting to create a tactile, visually engaging experience. "This approach added depth and emphasized the case's durability and elegance without overcomplicating the design. "The sound and music by Zelig Sound further enhanced the premium feel, ensuring a stylish and memorable impression of the product."

records.title: SONOS "ARC ULTRA"
records.description: Ant Baena, ECD at FutureDeluxe in London: "Sonos challenged us to visualize immersive sound in a fresh and exciting way for the relaunch of their high-end sound bar, the Arc Ultra. "We collaborated with Warner Brothers and Legendary Entertainment to bring the world of ‘Dune' into the home. "The project's most challenging aspect was creating simulations and effects that felt unique and ownable to us as a studio and our client and also lived alongside the visual world of the movie that took years to perfect and develop. "The film is so visually rich we weren't short of inspiration but building a world that tied the film in with a high-end CG living space and sand simulations took some trial and error. "We work with artists all over the globe, so one technical challenge was moving the large complicated simulations and setups between artists, which is never as quick and seamless as you'd like it to be. "We also spent a lot of time remapping, which strains the technical setups within Houdini, especially when we're changing things, creating a lot of back and forth. "This piece was part of a wider product launch of Arc Ultra and Sub 4. FutureDeluxe collaborated with Sonos to create a wealth of product assets to be used online and on social media to help reinforce the new engineering and technology within the products." Schedule: Six weeks.

records.title: ACURA "SOMETHING FOR EVERYONE
records.description: Shane Griffin, Director at GRIF studio in New York: "The agency MullenLowe approached us with an ambitious idea to craft a journey for the new Acura ADX through multiple surrealist worlds, each one reflecting a selling point of the car, referencing Culture, Fun, Technology, and Performance. "Each world had its unique mood and treatment of the car, so from a motion design perspective this was a great challenge and required us to think about unique lighting, movements, fx, and environments for each section, while also having that cohesively sit together as a final piece with a distinct color palette. "Because there was a request to keep the car static, we needed to establish a sense of scale and depth with the environments, and also design them so they framed the car as the center of attention. "The look development process was a ton of fun, and the client encouraged us to go wild with the ideas. "The main technical challenge was with the density and detail of the CAD model of the ADX vehicle, and adapting that for all the fun FX we developed. "From VDB sims, to tech blowaparts, to wind tunnels and pyro sims, each sim involved using the CAD data, so we had to invent new workflows as we're adapting and experimenting. "For example, we loaded the entire CAD data model into TyFlow to achieve the blow-apart effect, so no proxies or reference models could be used, this was time intensive, with huge file sizes, but ultimately worth it. "We also used a combo of different pyro techniques to achieve the wind tunnel and turn burnout. "For the wind tunnel, we settled on using Embergen to simulate the wind, as it gave us near real-time feedback to craft and art direct the fine details of exactly how the aerodynamics would work." Schedule: Seven weeks.

records.title: NIKE "LEBRON XXII"
records.description: The latest 3D motion work from Rimantas Lukavicius and the KORB team for Nike finds the Lithuania-based studio crushing symbols and icons from LeBron Jame's career in a spot for the LeBron XXII shoes releasing this week. Among the objects virtually destroyed by the new footwear are representations of several of LeBron's NBA foes including the Toronto Raptors and Boston Celtics, plus the media, the record books, and finally his age (turned 40 in December 2024). Rimantas Lukavicius: "It is inspiring that projects like this that are not only beautifully rendered but also carry deeper meanings and storytelling are still in demand. "Thanks to masterminds Michael Spoljaric and Choi Hunwoo at Nike, who came up with such brilliant ideas. "The technical goal was to make the film look as real as those viral crushing videos circulating online while also elevating the aesthetic side. "A lot of experimentation and physics simulations were involved, applying pressure to objects with different properties, such as crushing, squeezing, pushing, fracturing, etc. "Overall, the product's slogan ‘Pressure Tested. Pressure Ready.' makes perfect sense and truly reflects the process behind the spot it as well."

records.title: MOET & CHANDON "COLLECTION IMPERIALE"
records.description: Erwin Charrier, director at Pleix in Paris: "Moët & Chandon tasked us with translating the concept of 'Haute Œnologie' into a 30-second journey. "Drawing inspiration from the refined elegance of high fashion jewelry, we explored and developed various creative directions before distilling them into the final concept. "We envisioned luxurious, microscopic worlds where dancing bubbles transform into crystalline forms, ultimately revealing the iconic bottle and celebrating the spirit of the Collection Impériale. "The first challenge was to come up with an idea that instantly evokes high fashion jewelry, haute couture, and champagne. The second was finding the right visual style. "Real bubbles are very complex visually, and we didn't want to fall into a world that was too macro-photographic and concrete and also wanted to avoid it looking too much like CG liquid. "Luxury is about dreams and desire, often interpreted in an abstract, arty, and minimalist way. So, we chose a metaphorical representation of champagne bubbles. "Our client liked the research we did with Midjourney, and the first challenge was to replicate this very pure look without looking too perfect, as CGI can often be. "So we developed a system of 3D prisms in front of the 3D camera, adding a more natural look and micro-flares, as if shot through an old lens. "DOPs use the same principle on shoots when they want a more natural image that flares in the highlights. There are 2D plugins that do this badly, and we tested a brute-force approach for the first time. "Animation was also an interesting task, as we had to find the right balance between organic yet simple movements to maintain a certain purity. "At first, we experimented with highly complex particle systems and fluid dynamics, before finally going to very simple, hand-made choreographies. "Moët & Chandon approached us directly, which meant we first had to develop a concept before moving forward with the film. "It took about two months of R&D and key visual development before the idea and storyboard were approved and a total of four months to complete the final delivery. "The first music video we directed was for Plaid, so it was a real pleasure to collaborate with them and Warp Records once again on the soundtrack for this project. The music played a crucial role in bringing the film to life."

records.title: "NIKE AIR MAX 1000"
records.description: Donny Smith, director of outreach at Already Been Chewed in Dallas, TX: "Based on the production process at 3D-printed footwear brand Zellerfeld, we created a story behind the making of the Nike Airmax 1000 and its sustainability. "We needed the spot to be about 70% ‘real' (could happen in real life) and about 30% surreal. "Zellerfeld gave us a video chat tour of their facilities and process to produce the sneakers. We based our storyline on that information, including the fact that the shoes are recyclable. "There's a lot that goes into the production of the sneakers to communicate in a short amount of time, so there's quite a bit of artistic interpretation on our part. "We had not previously visualized the 3D printing process so the team jumped into Houdini and began exploring how to incorporate the G-code for the 3D printed files. "The combination of using real data that the 3D printer processes with a Houdini workflow made the spot adaptable and procedural in many ways. "We were also exploring Universal Scene Description workflows with Solaris tools in Houdini, so that was challenging." Schedule: Six weeks.

records.title: SKODA "BE MORE"
records.description: From The Mill team in London: "Skoda's ‘Be More' campaign, launching the all-new Elroq electric car, is a perfect example of what happens when a great creative idea meets top-tier craftsmanship. "One of the key challenges in creature animation is striking the right balance – avoiding excessive humanization while still creating characters that connect with audiences. "The idea was to draw striking parallels between the car's innovations and nature's most fascinating abilities. "To maintain authenticity, we studied real-life animal behaviors, using subtle body language and natural movement to bring each metaphor to life. "This approach not only grounded the animation in realism but also allowed the film's humor and charm to shine through in a way that felt both organic and engaging. "For the animation team, this research phase was one of the most exciting aspects of the project. "The vast diversity of the animal kingdom provided endless inspiration, offering fresh and unexpected ways to convey emotion and enhance storytelling."

records.title: GENESIS "NO OLD IDEAS"
records.description: Partizan director Antoine Bardou Jacquet and the VFX crew at Electric Theatre Collective answer the brief to separate Genesis from heritage luxury vehicle brands with a horde of antiquated light bulbs chasing the 2026 GV70 SUV. Jason Sperling, CCO at agency Innocean USA: "In a segment dominated by many venerable old badges, we wanted to make the point that old thinking can be an enemy to progress and originality. "The GV70 isn't weighed down by a long history and those legacy ideas, represented here by weathered, steampunk light bulbs."

records.title: "ESQUIRE CAPSULE RANGE ROVER SPORT"
records.description: Oleg Rumyantsev, senior motion designer at QLO Agency in Fethiye, Turkey: "The brief was very straightforward — the client wanted a motion video that aligned with the product's branding and visual style. T "The main goal was to showcase the capsule, highlight its features, and convey its aesthetics. "The brand's aesthetic is bold and clearly defined, which made it easy to find the right mood and visual direction. "I collaborated with my partner and friend Matvei Lisitsa, Art Director at QLO, who developed the branding for the client, which made it easy to stay aligned with the visual style. "The main challenge was keeping the video dynamic by maintaining a fast-paced sequence of shots. "One notable aspect was that I had to open the program EmberGen for the first time and learn it to create high-quality smoke effects for a few shots. The rest is just applying the experience I've gained from working with Cinema 4D over the past year. "The video was created for use on social media, the brand's newly updated website, and marked the presentation of the first working prototype of the capsule." Schedule: Five weeks, including one week of pre-production.

records.title: NIKE "DN8"
records.description: Garett Gioia, art director at FutureDeluxe in London: "To express the innovations of the Nike Dn8 sneaker, we were tasked with creating a suite of content for the experiential launch, including looping assets, huge collages, and this launch film. "One of the biggest challenges was reining in so much of the amazing R&D. When you have such a large area for play, it was easy to get lost in the exploration. "We had to find a balance of letting experimentation drive the energy, while making sure every moment still felt intentional and aligned with the product story. "A big part of the spot's vibe came from the chaos that emerged from generative tools like TouchDesigner, which we used to augment our renders. "Its unpredictability brought that raw, dynamic spirit that feels so aligned with Nike, embracing the unexpected. Schedule: Two months.

records.title: CHIVAS REGAL "REGALITY RISES"
records.description: CD Rimantas Lukavicius at KORB: "The agency team at We Say Hi approached us with an exciting challenge: to create a series of CGI shots bringing luxury, elegance, and sophistication to life that seamlessly blended with live action footage shot by the amazing director/photographer Rankin. "Our role was to craft key CGI elements, including the peacock, butterflies, dynamic liquid simulations, and photo-real product shots. "The peacock was the most complex challenge. Its feathers had to be designed to incorporate Chivas Regal logos while maintaining natural movement and a lifelike appearance. "The liquid simulations were designed to make the whiskey move like fluid gold, rich and captivating as it swirled and caught the light. "Every detail was fine-tuned to make the product shine, ensuring the bottle and branding looked flawless."

records.title: COINBASE "THE SYSTEM IS UPDATED"
records.description: Daniel Oeffinger, group creative director at Buck in Brooklyn, NY: "We worked with agency Isle of Any to create an anthem film for Coinbase that would catch attention and stand apart from traditional media broadcast spots. "The creative jumping off point was inspired by the 'blue screen of death', a reset that would set the stage for a new Coinbase-led world entirely built from code. "We wanted this world to be fun, slightly irreverent, and to ride the line between 'how did they do that' and 'who cares, this is a party'. "To hit those marks, we explored a lot of technical possibilities that would push this look and feel further than a traditional ascii-mapped approach. "A lot of traditional ascii image-mapping solutions are an over-the-top filter, where pixel values are converted to image sets, without much ability to control the rendered 'code'. "We needed more control over the ascii, something closer to a particle system. Our animation team, led by Anton Thallner, landed on a workflow that combined 2D and 3D inputs to create a controllable ascii setup that dynamics, gravity, and disruption could influence."

records.title: POWELL LACROSSE
records.description: Brandon Hirzel, CD at Bemo Studio in Los Angeles: "Mike Powell of Powell Lacrosse reached out to us wanting to make their first commercial showing off the new product line and bring attention to the unique voice of their brand. "Not only do they make some of the best innovative gear in their industry, they also have an unapologetic energy to their brand that propels them to the forefront of the sport. All of this needed to be understood visually inside the project. "After meeting with the client, we realized the creative direction of the project needed to be bold and full of energy. "We started to concept ways to achieve this within a single style, but soon realized the only way to match their voice was to combine multiple animation techniques into a full design-driven dopamine rush. "There are always technical challenges when mixing 2D, 3D, cel animation, and type-driven motion graphics. "It came down to having a clear plan and understanding the order in which each asset needed to be developed. This established pipeline set each artist up for success and created efficiencies within our workflow. "One of the amazing synchronicities about this project was the history that we have with the sport. The owners of Powell Lacrosse, their creative lead, and the creative lead at Bemo all played Lacrosse in a significant way. "It has been a big part of each of our lives. This was very helpful to understand the nuance of the design and led to a strong, unified alliance creating this project for a greater purpose and love of the sport." Schedule: Six weeks.

records.title: HUAWEI MATE XT ULTIMATE DESIGN
records.description: Mateusz Górski, EP at Millarc: "We were asked to create a video that would highlight the engineering precision of Huawei's Mate XT Ultimate Design, the world's first double-folding smartphone, with a focus on showcasing the two hinges. "The technical challenge was to create a functional rig as the hinges interacted with one another, so closing one caused the other to move. "We also focused on the number of hinge elements to create visually appealing shots while optimizing the model. Piotr Wątroba, art director at Millarc: "The main challenge was to capture the precision and engineering of the hinge mechanism in a way that not only conveyed its technical complexity but also made the folding process feel smooth, elegant, and visually satisfying. "The key was to find a balance between technical accuracy and artistic expression, ensuring the animation was both clear and emotionally engaging."

records.title: KOMERÄNÃ BANKA
records.description: Directing duo Jan Kalvoda and Premysl Ponahly (aka Wolfberg) and Slovak 3D/VFX house ALIEN bring all your scammer fears to life in this spot for Czech bank Komerční banka. Jan Kalvoda and Premysl Ponahly: "Our task was to bring cyber-criminals to life by designing monsters that personify the many threats lurking in our banking systems. "The client wanted characters they could fully own, so we were asked to design something unique. "We first went through several stages, presenting the agency and client with rough drawings while being careful not to resemble any existing monster characters out there. This was a fully analogue approach (no AI-generation). "Each character had their own special skills: the monster on the phone can make several calls at once, the one that steals your credit cards is an octopus with lots of hands, and the imposter selling tricky loans speaks faster than you can think. "Eventually, our 2D illustrations were approved, and we were able to develop them into 3D characters. "Then we had to make sure they could interact seamlessly with both the environments and the actors. Working together with ALIEN studio, we brought the characters to life using motion capture, and then finally, we annihilated them."

records.title: CUPRA "CUPRA X ZELLERFELD"
records.description: Denis Danin, head of studio/art director at Innerlights in Yerevan, Armenia: "The project was created for Milan Design Week, where Spanish automotive brand Cupra was unveiling several new products. "We were invited to produce a film that would spotlight their new 3D-printed sneaker, developed in collaboration with Zellerfeld. The goal was to showcase the sneaker's design and its connection to Cupra's aesthetic. "The brief included two main directives. First, we needed to open by showcasing the car capsule, then transition into the sneaker, showing how it's printed. "Second, we had to highlight the parametric design elements shared by both the car and the sneaker, visually drawing a connection between the two products. "The biggest creative challenge was developing that concept and storyline to unify the different worlds of the car and the sneaker, both visually and narratively. "We needed an element that would not only tie these two products together within the same universe, but also serve a functional purpose. "That's where the idea of lasers came in. Futuristic, sleek, and technological, just like Cupra and Zellerfeld, the lasers became a key visual bridge between the products. "They helped us guide the viewer's eye, emphasize the shared parametric design details, and introduce the brand's signature copper color. "The lasers essentially became the third character in the story, scanning the space, analyzing the surfaces, printing the sneaker, and creating a seamless flow between two otherwise unrelated objects. "We had a week for developing the concept and three weeks for production. The deadline was non-negotiable due to the live event in Milan, so we had to keep a tight and focused workflow."

Max Zhang: "With the Vivo S30 positioned as a summer ‘dopamine' phone with a light, feminine, and upbeat vibe, we went through three rounds of storyboarding internally to make sure the tone and rhythm felt right. "Balancing 2D and 3D animation was definitely the core challenge of the project, but also the most rewarding." "The first version leaned heavily on pure geometric shapes and motion; the second explored hand gestures and the energetic pop aesthetics inspired by K-pop girl groups. Eventually, we landed on a version that balanced graphic motion with product showcase. "One of the biggest challenges was figuring out how to seamlessly integrate the graphic animation with the phone itself. "We also experimented with combining 2D and 3D hands. In the end, we brought together a group of talented artists to illustrate both hands and the phone in a stylized way. This collaboration turned out to be one of the most fun parts of the process. "Balancing 2D and 3D animation was definitely the core challenge of the project, but also the most rewarding. We're especially fond of how the final quick-cut sequence brought all the elements together with great energy and rhythm."

records.title: FIJI WATER "SHAPING AN ICON"
records.description: Nadia Tzuo, Director at MakeMake in Santa Monica, CA: "The objective was to create a fresh look that reimagines the journey of Fiji water and create an immersive experience while maintaining the presence of the bottle's shape. "This idea gives us a rich, creative canvas. It's a poetic invitation to see nature not as a backdrop, but as the sculptor itself. "The challenge was finding the balance between the iconic shape and natural elements, and making the transitions flow in harmony. "The sequence unfolds in four chapters, each scene celebrating a unique element of the water's story from sky to soil, tailored to embrace the nature of the Fiji island and carefully hand-picked to build the shape of the iconic Fiji bottle. "The look is achieved with a combination of CG passes and compositing, created in Cinema4D and Nuke." Schedule: Three weeks.

records.title: UEFA WOMEN'S EURO TOURNAMENT 2025 "NAMES WILL BE MADE"
records.campaign_title: UEFA WOMEN'S EURO TOURNAMENT 2025 "NAMES WILL BE MADE"
records.description: Bart Yates, EP at Blinkink: "With AI threatening to reshape so much of the creative world, we wanted to go in the opposite direction, producing something tactile, raw, and handcrafted. "Going down the claymation route allowed us to craft something with real intention and personality, at a time when it matters the most. "It's physical, full of character and energy, just like football. This film is about celebrating human effort, and the finished product is a testament to everyone involved, from the crew behind the scenes to the players on the pitch. "Before model-making began, the concept team worked to set a core 2D style that would cement the striking compositions we see in the film. "Similarly, model puppets were first illustrated and then crafted into clay, with a strong likeness to the players. "The art department spent seven busy weeks building the sets and puppets, using 100 kilos worth of clay to sculpt all the elements across the 13-day shoot."

records.title: USM "HALLER SOFT PANEL"
records.description: Andreas Ibsen, CD, and Thomas Bay, co-founder at Frame in Copenhagen: "Swiss furniture manufacturer USM asked us to introduce their new magnetic panels without focusing on specific configurations, locations, or situations. "The goal was to highlight the product itself, leading us to design a non-sensical megastructure built from the USM Haller system. "This construction provided the framework for showcasing the panels' colors, functions, and design options while enabling playful compositions and dynamic movement. "The film also needed to align with the client's vision for the product launch at the Salone del Mobile trade show in Milan. "The biggest creative challenge was balancing the various elements: the furniture components, the oversized megastructure, the vibrant color palette, and the sunny, blue-sky aesthetic. "The megastructure inherently introduced a sense of chaos, and instead of fighting it, we leaned into that madness. "Our creative approach emphasized options, multiplicity, fun, and creativity — very much in line with the client's emphasis on "playful." "Another creative priority was introducing fabric as a new material in the USM Haller system. "We started with free-flowing textile to communicate tactility, then contrasted it with solid metal, ending with the ball joints shaping the final magnetic panels. "The technical challenge was to ensure accuracy at every scale and camera angle while handling the complexity of the megastructure. "We avoided using multiple levels of detail to keep the workflow consistent, which gave us complete freedom during R&D without risking inaccuracies. "To solve this, we built a USM Haller system builder HDA where each module existed as its own node. This allowed us to manipulate and animate individual modules while preserving the procedural integrity of the larger system. "For efficiency, Redshift proxies were used for most geometry, with rods generated procedurally through sweeps and curves. This setup ensured real-time viewport playback and fast rendering." Schedule: Seven weeks.

records.title: VAN RYSEL "INFERNO"
records.description: Virgile Machala and Maria Markova, producers at Eddy in Paris: "Van Rysel needed a bold, unconventional film to launch their new RCR-F INFERNO capsule, a line of high-performance cycling gear. "The goal was double: present their most advanced bike in action, and deliver a sensory, visceral experience that would resonate with cyclists. "Instead of following traditional premium codes, they asked for something more instinctive, more physical, something that could embody speed, pressure, and obsession. "The brief left a lot of room for interpretation, which allowed us to build a metaphorical, immersive vision of Hell, seen from inside a rider's mind. "The main challenge was to find the right balance between narrative ambition and raw emotional impact. "We wanted to convey both the technical precision of elite cycling and the trance-like state of exhaustion athletes experience in competition.
